title: AWS Certified AI Practitioner
sourceNote: Ingested from src/data/aifc01/qb-*.js via scripts/ingest-aif-from-js.mjs. Ordering items (24) are converted to single-select sequence questions. Numeric id = sequential 1–528 sorted by domain → task → source sequence. Correct option rationale is filled from explanation; distractor rationales preserved from source.

questions.question: A logistics company is briefing its leadership team on terminology before starting an AI project. An executive asks how deep learning relates to the other terms in the briefing. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Deep learning and machine learning are separate fields, and neither is part of artificial intelligence.
options.rationale: Both machine learning and deep learning sit inside the broader field of artificial intelligence.

options.text: Deep learning is a subset of machine learning that uses neural networks with many layers, and machine learning is a subset of artificial intelligence.
options.rationale: The terms nest inside each other: artificial intelligence is the broadest field, machine learning is the subset where systems learn patterns from data instead of being explicitly programmed, and deep learning is the subset of machine learning built on multi-layer neural networks. Generative AI is an application of deep learning that produces new content. Keeping this hierarchy straight prevents mismatched expectations when scoping projects.

options.text: Machine learning is a subset of deep learning, and generative AI is unrelated to both.
options.rationale: The relationship is reversed: deep learning is the narrower subset of machine learning.

options.text: Artificial intelligence is a subset of deep learning because deep learning came first historically.
options.rationale: Artificial intelligence is the broadest of these terms, not a subset of deep learning.

questions.question: A telecom provider has five years of customer records in which each account is already marked as either churned or retained. The company wants a model that predicts which current customers will churn. Which type of machine learning does this describe?

options.text: Supervised learning
options.rationale: Supervised learning trains on examples where the correct answer, or label, is already known, so the model learns the mapping from input features to that known outcome. Because every historical account carries a churned or retained label, this is a textbook supervised classification problem. The presence of trustworthy labels is the deciding clue.

options.text: Unsupervised learning
options.rationale: Unsupervised learning works on data with no labels and finds structure such as clusters.

options.text: Reinforcement learning
options.rationale: Reinforcement learning learns from rewards earned by taking actions, not from labeled records.

options.text: Self-supervised pre-training of a foundation model
options.rationale: Self-supervised pre-training builds general foundation models from massive unlabeled corpora, not a single churn prediction.

questions.question: A gaming studio has behavioral data for millions of players but no predefined player categories and no labels. The studio wants to discover natural groupings of similar players to guide content design. Which machine learning approach fits this goal?

options.text: Binary classification
options.rationale: Binary classification requires labeled examples of two known classes.

options.text: Linear regression
options.rationale: Regression predicts a continuous numeric target and needs labeled values.

options.text: Reinforcement learning
options.rationale: Reinforcement learning needs an environment and reward signal, not a one-time segmentation of existing data.

options.text: Clustering with unsupervised learning
options.rationale: Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups records by similarity when no target label exists, which is exactly what discovering unknown player segments requires. Classification and regression both need labeled target values to learn from. The absence of any label is the signal that points to unsupervised learning.

questions.question: A food delivery company wants a model that outputs the expected delivery time in minutes for each new order. Which type of machine learning problem is this?

options.text: Multi-class classification, because there are many possible delivery routes
options.rationale: Classification would apply only if the output were a discrete category such as on time or late.

options.text: Clustering, because similar orders should be grouped
options.rationale: Clustering groups unlabeled records and does not produce a per-order time estimate.

options.text: Regression, because the model predicts a continuous numeric value
options.rationale: Regression models predict a continuous numeric output such as minutes, dollars, or temperature, while classification predicts a discrete category. Asking for an estimated number of minutes rather than a bucket like fast or slow makes this a regression task. If the business instead wanted an on-time or late flag, the same data would support a classification model.

options.text: Dimensionality reduction, because order data has many columns
options.rationale: Dimensionality reduction compresses features and is a preprocessing technique, not a prediction target.

questions.question: A manufacturer wants to inspect photographs of parts on an assembly line and flag units with visible surface cracks. Which field of AI does this use case belong to?

options.text: Natural language processing
options.rationale: Natural language processing operates on text or transcribed language, not raw images.

options.text: Speech synthesis
options.rationale: Speech synthesis generates spoken audio from text and is unrelated to visual inspection.

options.text: Time-series forecasting
options.rationale: Time-series forecasting predicts future values from ordered historical measurements.

options.text: Computer vision
options.rationale: Computer vision is the field concerned with extracting meaning from images and video, including tasks such as image classification, object detection, and defect detection. Natural language processing deals with text and speech content. Matching the data type in the scenario, images in this case, to the right AI field is a core foundational skill.

questions.question: A healthcare provider wants software to read free-text clinician notes and determine which conditions each note mentions. Which AI capability is the provider applying?

options.text: Natural language processing
options.rationale: Natural language processing covers the techniques that let computers interpret and generate human language, including entity extraction from unstructured clinical text. The data here is written language, which is the defining characteristic. Computer vision would apply only if the notes were scanned images that first required text extraction.

options.text: Computer vision
options.rationale: Computer vision interprets images and video rather than written language.

options.text: Anomaly detection on numeric sensor streams
options.rationale: Anomaly detection on sensor streams targets numeric measurements, not narrative text.

options.text: Reinforcement learning
options.rationale: Reinforcement learning optimizes sequential decisions through rewards, not text understanding.

questions.question: A robotics team is training a warehouse robot to move pallets efficiently. The robot tries actions, receives a numeric reward when it improves throughput, and adjusts its behavior over many attempts. Which learning paradigm is being used?

options.text: Supervised learning with labeled trajectories
options.rationale: Supervised learning needs a labeled correct output for each input, not reward feedback.

options.text: Unsupervised learning
options.rationale: Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabeled data and has no notion of reward.

options.text: Reinforcement learning
options.rationale: Reinforcement learning trains an agent that interacts with an environment, takes actions, and learns a policy from reward or penalty feedback rather than from a fixed labeled dataset. The trial-and-feedback loop over repeated attempts is the identifying pattern. Supervised learning would instead require a correct action recorded for every situation in advance.

options.text: Transfer learning
options.rationale: Transfer learning reuses knowledge from a pretrained model and is not defined by reward feedback.

questions.question: A data team is describing its inputs to a new analyst. Which example best represents structured data?

options.text: A folder of customer support call recordings
options.rationale: Audio recordings are unstructured data with no predefined schema.

options.text: A collection of scanned contract PDFs
options.rationale: Scanned PDFs are unstructured documents until text and fields are extracted.

options.text: A relational database table of orders with columns for order ID, amount, and date
options.rationale: Structured data is organized into a predefined schema of rows and columns, such as a database table or a CSV file, so each value has a known type and meaning. Audio, images, and free-form documents are unstructured because they carry no inherent tabular schema. Recognizing the data type guides which services and model families are appropriate.

options.text: A set of product photographs
options.rationale: Images are unstructured data represented as pixel arrays.

questions.question: An energy utility collects meter readings every 15 minutes for each building and wants to predict next week's consumption. Which description of this dataset is most accurate?

options.text: Time-series data, because observations are ordered by timestamp and sequence matters
options.rationale: Time-series data consists of measurements recorded in timestamp order, where the sequence and intervals carry information that models must respect. Consumption forecasting depends on trends, seasonality, and recent history, all of which are time-series properties. Treating such data as unordered rows discards the signal that makes forecasting possible.

options.text: Image data, because readings are visualized on dashboards
options.rationale: How data is displayed does not change its underlying type; the readings are numeric measurements.

options.text: Unlabeled text data, because readings arrive as log lines
options.rationale: The readings are numeric values, and the sequence rather than language content is what matters.

options.text: Categorical data, because each building has an identifier
options.rationale: Building identifiers are one categorical column, but they do not define the dataset as a whole.

questions.question: A retail company must generate demand predictions for 500,000 products once per night, and no user is waiting for an individual result. Which inferencing approach best matches this requirement?

options.text: Real-time inference behind a persistent low-latency endpoint
options.rationale: A persistent low-latency endpoint is unnecessary when no one waits for individual predictions.

options.text: Batch inference over the full dataset on a schedule
options.rationale: Batch inference processes a large collection of records in one scheduled job and writes results to storage, which fits high-volume workloads where latency per record does not matter. Real-time inference keeps an endpoint always available to answer single requests in milliseconds and generally costs more for the same volume. Matching the inference mode to the latency requirement is a common exam distinction.

options.text: Continued pre-training of the model each night
options.rationale: Continued pre-training changes model weights and is a training activity, not inference.

options.text: Interactive human review of every prediction
options.rationale: Human review of 500,000 predictions per night is not an inference strategy and would not scale.

questions.question: A payments company must approve or decline each card transaction in under 100 milliseconds using a fraud model. Which inferencing approach is required?

options.text: Batch inference run every hour
options.rationale: Hourly batch scoring cannot decide a transaction that must be answered immediately.

options.text: Real-time inference through an always-available endpoint
options.rationale: Real-time inference serves individual requests through a persistently available endpoint so a prediction returns within milliseconds, which is mandatory when a live transaction is blocked on the answer. Batch and asynchronous modes trade latency for throughput and cost efficiency. The presence of a hard per-request latency budget always points to real-time inference.

options.text: Offline evaluation on a held-out test set
options.rationale: Offline evaluation measures model quality before deployment and does not serve live traffic.

options.text: Asynchronous inference with results delivered the next day
options.rationale: Next-day asynchronous results arrive far too late to authorize a payment.

questions.question: A credit union's loan default model scores 99 percent accuracy on the training data but only 68 percent on new applications it has never seen. Which problem does this pattern indicate?

options.text: Underfitting
options.rationale: Underfitting shows poor performance on both training and unseen data, not a large gap.

options.text: Overfitting
options.rationale: Overfitting occurs when a model memorizes noise and specific quirks of the training data instead of learning generalizable patterns, which produces excellent training scores and poor performance on unseen data. The gap between training and validation or test performance is the diagnostic signal. Remedies include more training data, simpler models, regularization, and early stopping.

options.text: Class imbalance in the target variable
options.rationale: Class imbalance typically depresses minority-class metrics on all splits rather than creating this specific gap.

options.text: Insufficient inference capacity
options.rationale: Inference capacity affects latency and throughput, not predictive accuracy.

questions.question: A public sector team trains a very simple model on complex citizen service data. Accuracy is low on the training set and equally low on the validation set. Which conclusion is most accurate?

options.text: The model is overfitting and needs more regularization
options.rationale: Overfitting would produce strong training accuracy alongside weak validation accuracy.

options.text: The model is underfitting and is too simple to capture the underlying patterns
options.rationale: Underfitting means the model has too little capacity, too few features, or too little training to represent the real relationships in the data, so it performs poorly everywhere including on data it has already seen. Consistently weak scores across both splits distinguish underfitting from overfitting. Fixes include a more expressive model, better features, or longer training.

options.text: The training data is leaking into the validation set
options.rationale: Data leakage usually inflates validation scores rather than depressing them.

options.text: The endpoint requires a larger instance type
options.rationale: A larger instance changes speed and cost, not the model's ability to fit patterns.

questions.question: A media analytics team is documenting basic modeling vocabulary for new hires. Which two statements correctly define the terms? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A feature is an individual input variable that the model uses to make a prediction.
options.rationale: Features are the input variables fed to a model, and the algorithm is the learning procedure whose output is the trained model containing learned parameters. Weights are those learned parameters, while hyperparameters are the settings chosen before training, such as learning rate or number of epochs. Mixing up weights and hyperparameters is one of the most common foundational errors.

options.text: A hyperparameter is a value learned automatically during training from the data.
options.rationale: Hyperparameters are set before training; learned values are parameters such as weights.

options.text: An algorithm is the procedure used to learn patterns, while the model is the trained artifact it produces.
options.rationale: Features are the input variables fed to a model, and the algorithm is the learning procedure whose output is the trained model containing learned parameters. Weights are those learned parameters, while hyperparameters are the settings chosen before training, such as learning rate or number of epochs. Mixing up weights and hyperparameters is one of the most common foundational errors.

options.text: A label is the raw file format in which training data is stored.
options.rationale: A label is the known correct output for a training example, not a file format.

options.text: Weights are the configuration settings a practitioner chooses before training begins.
options.rationale: Weights are learned during training; the settings chosen beforehand are hyperparameters.

questions.question: A ride-hailing company derives a new column, trip distance divided by trip duration, from raw pickup and dropoff records to improve model accuracy. What is this activity called?

options.text: Feature engineering
options.rationale: Feature engineering is the process of transforming raw data into input variables that better expose the underlying signal to a model, including deriving ratios, aggregations, and encodings. It typically delivers larger accuracy gains than algorithm changes on tabular problems. Hyperparameter tuning, by contrast, adjusts training settings rather than the inputs themselves.

options.text: Hyperparameter tuning
options.rationale: Hyperparameter tuning searches training configuration values and does not create new input columns.

options.text: Model deployment
options.rationale: Deployment makes a trained model available for inference and does not alter inputs.

options.text: Data labeling
options.rationale: Labeling assigns known target values to examples rather than deriving new features.

questions.question: A hospital research group must train a supervised image model but has 40,000 unannotated X-ray images. What must the group do before supervised training can begin?

options.text: Increase the number of epochs to compensate for missing labels
options.rationale: Epochs control how many passes training makes over data and cannot substitute for labels.

options.text: Label the images so each one carries the correct known outcome
options.rationale: Supervised learning requires labeled data, meaning each training example is paired with the correct answer the model should learn to produce. Without labels there is no target for the algorithm to optimize against, so annotation is a prerequisite rather than an optional step. Unlabeled data can still support unsupervised or self-supervised methods.

options.text: Switch the optimizer to reduce training cost
options.rationale: The optimizer affects how weights update, not whether ground truth exists.

options.text: Deploy the images to a real-time inference endpoint
options.rationale: Deployment serves predictions from a trained model and does not create training labels.

questions.question: An insurance company is explaining neural networks to non-technical stakeholders. Which description is accurate at a conceptual level?

options.text: A neural network stores training records and returns the closest match by exact lookup.
options.rationale: Exact-match lookup describes a database or a nearest-neighbor style memory, not how a neural network computes.

options.text: A neural network is made of layers of interconnected nodes whose weighted connections are adjusted during training.
options.rationale: A neural network is composed of layers of nodes, or neurons, connected by weights, and training adjusts those weights so the network's outputs move closer to the desired results. Depth, meaning many hidden layers, is what makes a network a deep learning model and enables it to learn complex representations from images, audio, and text. Neural networks learn parameters rather than storing and looking up examples.

options.text: A neural network requires that all input data be structured tabular data with fewer than 20 columns.
options.rationale: Neural networks handle images, audio, and text as well as tabular data with any number of features.

options.text: A neural network eliminates the need for any training data because it reasons from first principles.
options.rationale: Neural networks learn entirely from training data and cannot function without it.

questions.question: A marketing agency wants a system that writes original product descriptions and generates matching promotional images from text prompts. Which category of AI does this describe?

options.text: Generative AI
options.rationale: Generative AI produces new content such as text, images, audio, or code rather than assigning a label or a number to an existing input. It is built on deep learning, typically using large models trained on very large datasets. Discriminative approaches such as classification only choose among predefined outputs.

options.text: Classical supervised classification
options.rationale: Classification assigns inputs to predefined categories and does not create new content.

options.text: Anomaly detection
options.rationale: Anomaly detection flags unusual records and produces no generated output.

options.text: Rule-based expert systems
options.rationale: Rule-based systems apply hand-coded logic and cannot compose novel text or images.

questions.question: A publishing company is describing what makes a large language model large. Which statement is the most accurate foundational description?

options.text: It is a deep learning model with a very large number of parameters trained on vast amounts of text to predict tokens in sequence.
options.rationale: A large language model is a deep neural network, usually a transformer, with billions of parameters trained on huge text corpora using a next-token or masked-token objective. That scale of parameters and data is what produces broad language capability that generalizes to many tasks. The model generates output token by token rather than retrieving stored answers.

options.text: It is a keyword search index that has been compressed for fast retrieval.
options.rationale: A search index retrieves existing documents; it does not generate new language.

options.text: It is a spreadsheet of question and answer pairs that grows as users interact with it.
options.rationale: Large language models store learned parameters, not a lookup table of question and answer pairs.

options.text: It is a translation dictionary that maps each word in one language to one word in another.
options.rationale: Word-for-word dictionaries lack the contextual modeling that language models perform.

questions.question: A legal technology team needs to find documents that are semantically similar to a query even when the wording differs. They plan to convert text into numeric vectors that place related meanings close together. What are these vectors called?

options.text: Hyperparameters
options.rationale: Hyperparameters are training configuration settings, not representations of content.

options.text: Embeddings
options.rationale: Embeddings are dense numeric vector representations of text, images, or other content in which semantic similarity corresponds to closeness in vector space. Similarity search over embeddings is what lets a system match meaning rather than exact keywords, and it underpins retrieval workflows and recommendation features. The vectors are produced by an embedding model.

options.text: Epochs
options.rationale: An epoch is one complete pass over the training dataset.

options.text: Confusion matrices
options.rationale: A confusion matrix is an evaluation table of predicted versus actual classes.

questions.question: A wildlife nonprofit has only 900 labeled camera-trap images. Rather than training a vision model from scratch, the team starts from a model already trained on millions of general images and adapts it to their species. Which concept are they applying?

options.text: Transfer learning
options.rationale: Transfer learning reuses representations learned by a model trained on a large general dataset and adapts them to a related task with a much smaller dataset, which reduces both data requirements and compute cost. It is the standard approach when labeled examples are scarce. Fine-tuning a foundation model is a widely used form of transfer learning.

options.text: Data augmentation
options.rationale: Data augmentation creates modified copies of existing examples but does not reuse a pretrained model.

options.text: Hyperparameter tuning
options.rationale: Hyperparameter tuning optimizes training settings and does not import prior knowledge.

options.text: Ensemble learning
options.rationale: Ensemble learning combines multiple models trained on the same task rather than transferring knowledge.

questions.question: A machine learning engineer at a bank sets the number of epochs to 50 before starting a training job. What does the epoch setting control?

options.text: How many complete passes the training process makes over the entire training dataset
options.rationale: An epoch is one full pass of the training algorithm over the whole training dataset, and the epoch count is a hyperparameter set before training. Too few epochs can leave a model underfitted, while too many can drive it toward overfitting, which is why practitioners monitor validation metrics across epochs. Epochs are unrelated to serving capacity.

options.text: How many features the model is allowed to use
options.rationale: The set of usable features comes from the dataset and feature selection, not the epoch count.

options.text: How many concurrent inference requests the endpoint accepts
options.rationale: Concurrency is an inference and infrastructure setting, unrelated to training passes.

options.text: How many decimal places are kept in the model weights
options.rationale: Numeric precision is controlled by data types such as FP16 or FP32, not by epochs.

questions.question: A research team is analyzing the bias-variance tradeoff for a demand model. Which two statements are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: High variance means the model is very sensitive to the specific training sample and tends to overfit.
options.rationale: In this statistical sense, bias is error from overly simplistic assumptions, which causes underfitting, and variance is error from excessive sensitivity to the particular training sample, which causes overfitting. Increasing complexity typically lowers bias while raising variance, so practitioners seek a balance that minimizes total error on unseen data. Note that this modeling sense of bias is different from fairness bias against groups of people.

options.text: High bias means the model makes overly simple assumptions and tends to underfit.
options.rationale: In this statistical sense, bias is error from overly simplistic assumptions, which causes underfitting, and variance is error from excessive sensitivity to the particular training sample, which causes overfitting. Increasing complexity typically lowers bias while raising variance, so practitioners seek a balance that minimizes total error on unseen data. Note that this modeling sense of bias is different from fairness bias against groups of people.

options.text: High variance always improves generalization to new data.
options.rationale: High variance hurts generalization because the model fits noise in the training sample.

options.text: Increasing model complexity reliably reduces both bias and variance at the same time.
options.rationale: Adding complexity generally trades reduced bias for increased variance rather than reducing both.

options.text: Bias and variance are measures of inference latency.
options.rationale: Bias and variance describe sources of prediction error, not latency.

questions.question: A startup is choosing compute for training a deep neural network on millions of images. Which statement about hardware is accurate at a conceptual level?

options.text: CPUs are always faster than GPUs for deep learning because they have higher clock speeds.
options.rationale: Higher clock speed does not offset the parallelism advantage GPUs have on matrix math.

options.text: GPUs and purpose-built accelerators speed up deep learning because they perform massively parallel matrix operations.
options.rationale: Deep learning training and inference are dominated by large matrix multiplications, and GPUs and purpose-built accelerators execute thousands of these operations in parallel, which is why they finish jobs far faster than general purpose CPUs. CPUs remain fine for lightweight models, small-scale inference, and data preparation. Hardware affects speed and cost, not how much data a model needs.

options.text: Deep learning training cannot use accelerators and must run on general purpose CPUs.
options.rationale: Accelerators are widely used for deep learning and are often the practical choice.

options.text: Accelerators reduce the amount of training data a model needs to converge.
options.rationale: Hardware changes training speed and cost but not the data volume required to learn.

questions.question: A university lab wants a precise definition to share with students. Which statement best defines machine learning?

options.text: Systems that learn patterns from data to make predictions without being explicitly programmed with rules for each case
options.rationale: Machine learning is the discipline in which algorithms infer patterns from data and use them to make predictions or decisions, rather than relying on rules coded by hand for every situation. This data-driven approach is what allows models to handle cases developers never enumerated. Rule engines, storage systems, and accelerator hardware are different things entirely.

options.text: Software that follows a fixed set of hand-written if-then rules maintained by developers
options.rationale: Hand-written if-then logic describes a rule-based system, which is not machine learning.

options.text: Any program that stores large volumes of data in a data warehouse
options.rationale: Storing data is a prerequisite for analytics but is not learning from it.

options.text: Hardware designed specifically to run parallel numeric workloads
options.rationale: That describes accelerator hardware such as GPUs, not the discipline of machine learning.

questions.question: A logistics company is running its first supervised machine learning project. Place the machine learning lifecycle stages in the correct order.

options.text: 1. Deploy the model and monitor its performance in production → 2. Evaluate the trained model against a held-out dataset → 3. Train the model on the prepared training data → 4. Collect and prepare the labeled data, including feature engineering
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Train the model on the prepared training data → 2. Evaluate the trained model against a held-out dataset → 3. Deploy the model and monitor its performance in production → 4. Collect and prepare the labeled data, including feature engineering
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Collect and prepare the labeled data, including feature engineering → 2. Train the model on the prepared training data → 3. Evaluate the trained model against a held-out dataset → 4. Deploy the model and monitor its performance in production
options.rationale: A supervised project starts with collecting and preparing labeled data, since data quality sets the ceiling on results. Training then fits model parameters to that data, and evaluation on held-out data measures whether the model generalizes. Only after acceptable evaluation results does the model move to deployment, where ongoing monitoring detects drift and degradation.

options.text: 1. Train the model on the prepared training data → 2. Collect and prepare the labeled data, including feature engineering → 3. Evaluate the trained model against a held-out dataset → 4. Deploy the model and monitor its performance in production
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

questions.question: A retailer splits its historical sales data into training, validation, and test sets. What is the primary purpose of the held-out test set?

options.text: To provide a final unbiased estimate of performance on data the model never saw during training or tuning
options.rationale: The test set is reserved until the very end so it can give an honest estimate of how the model will perform on new data, because it influenced neither the learned weights nor the tuning decisions. The validation set is what guides hyperparameter choices during development. Reusing the test set for tuning quietly inflates the reported numbers.

options.text: To supply extra examples that increase the model's training accuracy
options.rationale: Test data is deliberately excluded from training, so it cannot raise training accuracy.

options.text: To store the model weights after training completes
options.rationale: Model weights are saved as artifacts in storage, not in a data split.

options.text: To generate the labels that the training set is missing
options.rationale: Splits do not create labels; labeling is a separate data preparation activity.

questions.question: A streaming service wants to sort incoming support tickets into one of five predefined categories such as billing, playback, or account access. Which machine learning task does this represent?

options.text: Multi-class classification
options.rationale: Multi-class classification assigns each input to exactly one of three or more predefined labels, which is what routing tickets into five known categories requires. Binary classification would apply if there were only two possible labels. Because the categories already exist and labeled examples can be gathered, this is supervised rather than unsupervised work.

options.text: Regression
options.rationale: Regression predicts continuous numeric values, not category membership.

options.text: Clustering
options.rationale: Clustering would discover new groupings rather than use the five predefined categories.

options.text: Forecasting
options.rationale: Forecasting predicts future values in a time-ordered series.

questions.question: A car rental company is documenting the difference between a model and an algorithm. Which pairing is correct?

options.text: The algorithm is the deployed endpoint, and the model is the network configuration around it
options.rationale: An endpoint is deployment infrastructure, not the learning procedure.

options.text: The algorithm is the learning procedure applied to data, and the model is the trained artifact containing learned parameters
options.rationale: An algorithm is the mathematical procedure that learns from data, such as gradient boosting or a transformer training routine, and the model is the resulting artifact that holds the learned weights and can produce predictions. One algorithm can produce many different models depending on the data and settings used. Keeping the distinction clear helps when comparing training options.

options.text: The algorithm and the model are interchangeable words for the same object
options.rationale: The terms describe different things: a procedure versus its trained output.

options.text: The algorithm is the labeled dataset, and the model is the set of hyperparameters
options.rationale: Datasets and hyperparameters are inputs to training, not definitions of these two terms.

questions.question: A public health agency is inventorying its data before an AI project. Which two items are unstructured data? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Recorded audio from a telehealth call center
options.rationale: Unstructured data has no predefined schema, so audio recordings and free-form written comments both qualify and require AI techniques such as speech recognition or natural language processing to become useful. CSV exports, database tables, and numeric series are structured or semi-structured with defined columns and types. The distinction drives which services and model families fit a use case.

options.text: A CSV export of appointment counts by clinic and month
options.rationale: A CSV with defined columns is structured tabular data.

options.text: Free-text patient feedback comments
options.rationale: Unstructured data has no predefined schema, so audio recordings and free-form written comments both qualify and require AI techniques such as speech recognition or natural language processing to become useful. CSV exports, database tables, and numeric series are structured or semi-structured with defined columns and types. The distinction drives which services and model families fit a use case.

options.text: A database table of vaccine inventory quantities
options.rationale: A database table has a fixed schema, making it structured data.

options.text: A numeric time series of daily emergency room visits
options.rationale: A numeric daily series is structured time-series data.

questions.question: An analytics team notices that their sales model performs well overall but poorly on data from a newly opened region that was barely present in the training set. Which training data concept best explains this outcome?

options.text: The model has too many hyperparameters
options.rationale: Hyperparameter count does not explain a gap concentrated in one underrepresented segment.

options.text: The training data was not representative of the population the model must serve
options.rationale: A model can only learn patterns present in its training data, so groups or conditions that are underrepresented tend to receive weaker predictions. Representativeness, coverage, and volume of training data are therefore central to both accuracy and fairness. The fix is collecting more data from the underrepresented region and retraining.

options.text: The inference endpoint is undersized for the new region's traffic
options.rationale: Endpoint sizing affects latency and throughput, not accuracy for a specific region.

options.text: The model needs a lower temperature setting
options.rationale: Temperature applies to generative model sampling, not to a tabular sales prediction model.

questions.question: A shipping firm has a trained model in production and sends new shipment records to it to obtain predicted transit times. What is this act of generating predictions from a trained model called?

options.text: Inferencing
options.rationale: Inferencing, sometimes called scoring or prediction, is the phase in which a trained model receives new inputs and produces outputs. Training builds the model once, while inference runs repeatedly for the life of the application and typically drives most ongoing cost. Recognizing the training versus inference split is fundamental to reasoning about architecture and spend.

options.text: Feature engineering
options.rationale: Feature engineering prepares input variables and happens before training.

options.text: Hyperparameter tuning
options.rationale: Hyperparameter tuning searches training settings and is not prediction.

questions.question: A newspaper wants a foundation model to answer questions grounded in its own archive. An engineer notes that the archive text must first be converted into vectors for similarity search. Which type of model performs that conversion?

options.text: An image generation model
options.rationale: Image generation models create pictures and cannot produce text embeddings for search.

options.text: An embedding model
options.rationale: An embedding model converts text into fixed-length numeric vectors that capture semantic meaning, enabling similarity search over a vector index. That step is the foundation of retrieval-based workflows, where relevant passages are found by vector proximity and then supplied to a generative model. Generation and classification models serve different purposes in the pipeline.

options.text: A speech recognition model
options.rationale: Speech recognition converts audio to text, which is a separate preprocessing step.

options.text: A classification model
options.rationale: A classification model outputs category labels rather than reusable semantic vectors.

questions.question: A manufacturing analytics group is deciding which of its planned projects can proceed without any labeled data. Which two tasks are unsupervised learning tasks? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Predicting the exact number of units a plant will produce next quarter
options.rationale: Predicting a specific numeric quantity is supervised regression and needs labeled history.

options.text: Grouping machines into segments based on similar vibration profiles
options.rationale: Unsupervised learning finds structure in data without target labels, and both clustering into segments and dimensionality reduction fit that definition. Predicting units, days of remaining life, or a pass and fail outcome all require labeled historical targets, making them supervised regression or classification. The presence or absence of a known target value is the deciding test.

options.text: Deciding whether a finished part passes or fails inspection using historical pass and fail records
options.rationale: Pass and fail records are labels, so this is supervised classification.

options.text: Reducing 200 sensor columns into a smaller set of components that retain most of the variation
options.rationale: Unsupervised learning finds structure in data without target labels, and both clustering into segments and dimensionality reduction fit that definition. Predicting units, days of remaining life, or a pass and fail outcome all require labeled historical targets, making them supervised regression or classification. The presence or absence of a known target value is the deciding test.

options.text: Estimating the remaining useful life in days for each pump using recorded failure dates
options.rationale: Recorded failure dates provide labels, making this supervised regression.

questions.question: A stadium operator is listing which planned features rely on computer vision. Which two use cases are computer vision tasks? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Counting how many people appear in security camera frames at each gate
options.rationale: Computer vision interprets visual input, so counting people in video frames and detecting damage in photographs both qualify. Identifying the input data type reliably points to the right AI field.

options.text: Summarizing written fan survey responses into themes
options.rationale: Summarizing written responses is a natural language processing task.

options.text: Detecting whether a photographed turnstile shows visible damage
options.rationale: Computer vision interprets visual input, so counting people in video frames and detecting damage in photographs both qualify. Summarizing and translating already-digital text are natural language processing tasks, and revenue forecasting is a time-series problem on numeric data. Identifying the input data type reliably points to the right AI field.

options.text: Translating printed program text from English into Spanish once the text is already digital
options.rationale: Translating digital text is natural language processing, not image analysis.

options.text: Forecasting next month's ticket revenue from historical sales
options.rationale: Revenue forecasting works on numeric time-series data.

questions.question: A media company is planning compute for a deep learning workload. Which two statements about processors and accelerators are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Evaluation is always required regardless of the hardware used.

options.text: GPUs and purpose-built accelerators shorten deep learning training time by parallelizing large matrix computations
options.rationale: Accelerators shorten deep learning training because they run the many parallel matrix operations these models require, while CPUs remain a sensible lower-cost option for small models and light inference traffic. Hardware choice affects speed and cost, not model accuracy, and training and inference hardware can differ. Teams commonly train on accelerators and then serve smaller or optimized models on cheaper compute.

questions.question: A retail data team is training new analysts on data terminology. Which two statements about labeled and unlabeled data are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Unlabeled data is always higher quality than labeled data because no human has touched it.
options.rationale: Quality depends on collection and curation, not on whether data is labeled.

options.text: Labeled data pairs each example with the known correct output that a supervised model learns to predict.
options.rationale: Labeled data includes the ground-truth answer for each example, which is what supervised algorithms optimize against, while unlabeled data lacks that target but still powers unsupervised learning and the self-supervised pre-training behind foundation models. Labeling usually requires human or programmatic effort and is often the most expensive part of a supervised project. No amount of extra epochs substitutes for missing labels.

options.text: Supervised learning can proceed on entirely unlabeled data if the number of epochs is increased.
options.rationale: Supervised learning has no target to optimize without labels, regardless of epochs.

options.text: Labeling is always automatic and free because labels already exist inside every dataset.
options.rationale: Labels typically must be created through human annotation or programmatic rules, at real cost.

options.text: Unlabeled data can still be used, for example in unsupervised learning and in self-supervised pre-training of foundation models.

options.text: 1. Update the weights slightly in the direction that reduces the error → 2. Propagate the error backward through the layers to measure each weight's contribution to it → 3. Compare the predictions with the correct labels to compute the loss → 4. Pass a batch of training examples forward through the network to produce predictions
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

Update the weights slightly in the direction that reduces the error → 4. Pass a batch of training examples forward through the network to produce predictions

options.rationale: Each training iteration begins with a forward pass that turns inputs into predictions using the current weights. The loss function then quantifies how far those predictions are from the labels, and backpropagation distributes that error backward to compute how much each weight contributed. Finally the optimizer nudges the weights to reduce the loss, and the cycle repeats across many batches and epochs.

questions.question: A gaming company is comparing inference options for two workloads. Which two statements about batch and real-time inferencing are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Batch inference processes a large set of records as a scheduled job and writes the results to storage.
options.rationale: Batch inference is optimized for throughput: it scores many records in one scheduled run and persists the output, with no user waiting on any single record. Real-time inference is optimized for latency, keeping an endpoint ready to answer individual requests immediately, which usually costs more for equivalent volume. Hardware choice is independent of the inference mode.

options.text: Batch inference returns each individual prediction within milliseconds to a waiting user.
options.rationale: Millisecond per-request responses describe real-time inference, not batch.

options.text: Real-time inference is always cheaper than batch inference for large nightly scoring jobs.
options.rationale: Keeping an endpoint always available typically costs more than a scheduled batch job for bulk scoring.

options.text: Real-time inference serves individual requests with low latency from an available endpoint.

questions.question: An engineering manager is correcting misconceptions about how large language models work. Which two statements are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A large language model retrieves its answers verbatim from a database of stored documents.
options.rationale: Answers are generated from learned parameters, not retrieved verbatim from a database.

options.text: A large language model retrains its weights automatically every time a user submits a prompt.
options.rationale: Weights stay frozen during inference; changing them requires a separate training process.

options.text: A large language model generates text by repeatedly predicting the next token given the tokens produced so far.
options.rationale: Language models operate on tokens, which are words or subword fragments, and they generate output one token at a time by predicting the most likely continuation of the sequence. Their weights are fixed at inference time; ordinary prompts do not retrain the model, and answers are generated rather than looked up from a document store. These points explain both the power and the hallucination risk of generative models.

options.text: A large language model can only accept structured tabular data as input.
options.rationale: Language models consume text and, for multimodal variants, images, not only tabular data.

options.text: Tokens are the small text units, such as words or subword pieces, that a language model reads and produces.

questions.question: A streaming media company wants to show each subscriber a personalized list of titles based on that subscriber's viewing history and on what similar subscribers watch. The company has no in-house data science staff. Which AWS service meets this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes text for sentiment, entities, and topics; it does not generate recommendations.

options.text: Amazon Personalize
options.rationale: Amazon Personalize is a managed recommendation service that learns from user interaction data, item metadata, and user metadata to return real-time recommendations and personalized rankings. It is the standard match for recommendation use cases when a team has no ML specialists. The other services in the list analyze text, search documents, or analyze images, none of which model individual user preferences.

options.text: Amazon Kendra
options.rationale: Kendra ranks documents in response to search queries rather than recommending catalog items to a specific user.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition
options.rationale: Rekognition analyzes images and video and cannot model viewing preferences.

questions.question: A healthcare billing team receives thousands of scanned insurance claim forms as PDF files each day. Staff currently retype the printed field values and table rows into a claims system. Which AWS service should the team use to automate the data capture?

options.text: Amazon Textract
options.rationale: Amazon Textract goes beyond simple optical character recognition by returning text, key-value pairs from forms, and table structures from scanned documents. That output maps directly to the fields a claims system needs. Document data capture is Textract's core use case, while the other services handle language translation, speech, and search.

options.text: Amazon Translate
options.rationale: Translate converts text between languages and does not read scanned documents.

options.text: Amazon Transcribe
options.rationale: Transcribe converts speech in audio or video to text, not printed text in images.

options.text: Amazon Kendra
options.rationale: Kendra searches content that has already been indexed as text; it does not extract fields and tables from scans.

questions.question: A logistics company calculates shipping surcharges from a published table of fixed fees per weight band and destination zone. The rates are set by contract and change only when a contract is renegotiated. A developer proposes training an ML model to predict each surcharge. Which approach is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Train a regression model in Amazon SageMaker AI because the inputs are numeric
options.rationale: A model would approximate an exact published rule and could return a value that does not match the contract.

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock with a prompt that asks a foundation model for the surcharge amount
options.rationale: Foundation model output is non-deterministic and unsuitable for a contractual fee that must be exact.

options.text: Implement the surcharge table as deterministic business rules in application code
options.rationale: When the logic is completely known, stable, and must produce exact repeatable values, a deterministic rules implementation is cheaper, faster, and fully auditable. ML is valuable when patterns are complex or unknown and cannot be written as rules. Introducing a model here would only approximate a rule that is already documented exactly.

options.text: Use Amazon Personalize to select the correct surcharge for each shipment
options.rationale: Personalize recommends items to users; it does not compute contractual fees.

questions.question: A public sector agency is evaluating Amazon Comprehend for its document workflows. Which two tasks is Amazon Comprehend well suited for? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Detecting and redacting personally identifiable information in free-text case notes
options.rationale: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service for text that is already digital. It detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, and PII, and it supports custom classification models trained on labeled examples. Speech, scanned documents, and speech synthesis belong to Transcribe, Textract, and Polly respectively.

options.text: Converting recorded public hearings into written transcripts
options.rationale: Amazon Transcribe converts speech to text.

options.text: Classifying incoming citizen emails into predefined complaint categories
options.rationale: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service for text that is already digital. It detects entities, key phrases, language, sentiment, and PII, and it supports custom classification models trained on labeled examples. Speech, scanned documents, and speech synthesis belong to Transcribe, Textract, and Polly respectively.

options.text: Extracting handwritten values from scanned paper forms
options.rationale: Amazon Textract extracts printed and handwritten values from scanned documents.

options.text: Generating a synthetic voice announcement for a public alert system
options.rationale: Amazon Polly generates speech from text.

questions.question: An online gaming company wants to score new account registrations and in-game purchases in near real time to flag likely fraudulent activity. The team has several years of labeled historical transactions but limited ML expertise. Which AWS service is purpose-built for this requirement?

options.text: Amazon Rekognition
options.rationale: Rekognition analyzes images and video, not transaction events.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes text and cannot score transaction risk.

options.text: Amazon Personalize
options.rationale: Personalize recommends items to users rather than detecting fraud.

options.text: Amazon Fraud Detector
options.rationale: Amazon Fraud Detector is a managed service for online fraud use cases such as new account fraud and payment fraud. It combines a customer's historical labeled event data with models AWS has trained on fraud patterns, and it exposes rules plus real-time prediction endpoints without requiring the team to build a model from scratch.

questions.question: A national retailer wants an audio version of its product safety notices so that customers can listen to them in the mobile app. The notices are stored as text. Which AWS service should the retailer use?

options.text: Amazon Transcribe
options.rationale: Transcribe converts speech to text, the opposite of what is needed.

options.text: Amazon Polly
options.rationale: Amazon Polly is a text-to-speech service that converts written text into lifelike speech audio. Transcribe performs the opposite conversion, turning speech into text. Keeping the direction of the conversion straight is the distinction this item tests.

options.text: Amazon Translate
options.rationale: Translate converts text between languages without producing audio.

options.text: Amazon Lex
options.rationale: Lex builds conversational interfaces; speech synthesis is not its purpose.

questions.question: A manufacturing company stores thousands of maintenance manuals, standard operating procedures, and internal wiki pages across Amazon S3 and SharePoint. Technicians want to ask natural language questions such as "what torque setting applies to the line 4 conveyor bolts" and get the answer with a link to the source document. Which AWS service best meets this requirement?

options.text: Amazon Comprehend custom classification
options.rationale: Custom classification assigns labels to documents; it does not answer natural language questions.

options.text: Amazon Textract
options.rationale: Textract extracts content from scanned documents but does not index or search a corpus.

options.text: Amazon Kendra
options.rationale: Amazon Kendra is an intelligent enterprise search service that indexes content from connectors such as S3 and SharePoint and returns ranked answers and passages for natural language questions, with source attribution. Comprehend labels or analyzes text, Textract reads scans, and Polly produces audio, so none of them provide search over a document corpus.

options.text: Amazon Polly
options.rationale: Polly converts text to speech and has no search capability.

questions.question: A regional bank must give applicants a specific, legally reviewable reason for every declined loan application, and regulators require that the decision logic be inspectable line by line. The bank's eligibility policy is fully documented. Which factor MOST strongly argues against replacing the policy engine with a deep learning model?

options.text: Deep learning models cannot process numeric application data
options.rationale: Deep learning models routinely process numeric tabular data.

options.text: Deep learning models cannot be hosted on AWS in a regulated account
options.rationale: Regulated workloads can run on AWS; hosting is not the blocker.

options.text: Deep learning models require the data to be stored outside of the bank's AWS account
options.rationale: Training and inference data can remain in the customer's own account and Region.

options.text: Deep learning models are harder to interpret, which conflicts with the explainability requirement
options.rationale: Interpretability is a key part of assessing AI suitability. Complex models can outperform rules on unknown patterns, but their internal reasoning is difficult to explain, which is a problem where each decision must be defended to a regulator or applicant. When the policy is already documented and must be auditable, a deterministic rules engine is the better fit.

questions.question: A media company wants to automate parts of its video publishing pipeline with Amazon Rekognition. Which two tasks can Rekognition perform? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Translate on-screen subtitles into Spanish

options.text: Produce a synthetic narrator voice for a documentary

questions.question: A grocery chain wants to predict weekly demand for each product at each store for the next 12 weeks, using three years of historical sales along with promotion calendars and local holidays. Which type of ML problem does this represent?

options.text: Binary classification
options.rationale: Binary classification predicts one of two categories, not a future quantity.

options.text: Time series forecasting
options.rationale: Predicting future numeric values from historical values ordered in time, with related series such as promotions and holidays, is a time series forecasting problem. Classification predicts a category, clustering groups unlabeled records, and image classification applies to visual data.

options.text: Clustering
options.rationale: Clustering finds groups in unlabeled data and does not predict future values.

options.text: Image classification
options.rationale: Image classification applies to visual inputs, not sales history.

questions.question: A business analyst at an insurance company has a labeled CSV export of past policy renewals in Amazon S3 and wants to build and evaluate a churn prediction model. The analyst writes SQL but no Python. Which AWS capability meets this need with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Canvas
options.rationale: Amazon SageMaker Canvas is a no-code visual interface that lets business users import tabular data, build models, view accuracy metrics, and generate predictions without writing code. Custom training jobs require ML engineering skills, Knowledge Bases support retrieval for generative applications, and Q Developer assists with software development tasks.

options.text: A custom training script on Amazon SageMaker AI training jobs
options.rationale: Writing a custom training script requires Python and ML expertise the analyst does not have.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.rationale: Knowledge Bases provide retrieval augmented generation over documents, not tabular churn prediction.

options.text: Amazon Q Developer
options.rationale: Q Developer is a coding assistant, not a tabular model builder.

options.text: Amazon Polly

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes text attributes but does not maintain dialog state or collect slots.

options.text: Amazon Textract
options.rationale: Textract extracts data from documents and has no conversational capability.

questions.question: A global consultancy wants an internal generative AI assistant that answers employee questions using content in Amazon S3, Microsoft SharePoint, and Salesforce, respects each employee's existing permissions, and cites its sources. options.rationale: Amazon Q Business is a managed generative AI assistant for enterprise content. options.text: Amazon Q Developer
options.rationale: Q Developer assists with coding, debugging, and AWS development tasks rather than company-wide document Q and A.

options.text: Amazon Lex
options.rationale: Lex handles structured intent-based dialogs and does not index enterprise repositories.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
options.rationale: JumpStart provides model hosting and fine-tuning, not a ready-made enterprise assistant.

questions.question: A software team wants in-IDE help writing unit tests, explaining unfamiliar legacy functions, and suggesting code as developers type. Which AWS service is intended for this use case?

options.text: Amazon Q Business
options.rationale: Q Business answers questions over enterprise documents rather than assisting inside an IDE.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes natural language text and does not generate code.

options.text: Amazon Q Developer
options.rationale: Amazon Q Developer is a generative AI assistant for software development that provides inline code suggestions, code explanations, test generation, and help with AWS resources inside the IDE and CLI. Q Business is the enterprise content assistant, and the other options serve text analysis and workflow orchestration.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Flows
options.rationale: Bedrock Flows orchestrates generative AI workflows; it is not a developer coding assistant.

questions.question: A hospital network records patient consultations in English and needs the written summaries made available to Spanish-speaking and Portuguese-speaking families. options.rationale: Polly generates speech from text and Comprehend analyzes text; neither transcribes audio or translates.

options.text: Amazon Textract, then Amazon Kendra
options.rationale: Textract reads scanned documents and Kendra searches indexed content; neither handles audio or translation.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition, then Amazon Translate
options.rationale: Rekognition analyzes images and video frames, not spoken audio.

options.rationale: Amazon Transcribe converts the recorded speech into text, and Amazon Translate then converts that text into Spanish and Portuguese. The item tests the ability to chain the right speech and language services in the correct order rather than confusing them with document, vision, or speech synthesis services.

questions.question: A payment processor must block transactions that exceed a hard regulatory limit of 10,000 USD per transfer, and separately wants to flag unusual spending patterns that may indicate account takeover. Which design correctly assigns each requirement?

options.text: Use a deterministic rule for the 10,000 USD limit and an ML model for unusual spending patterns
options.rationale: A fixed regulatory threshold is a known, exact rule and must be enforced deterministically so it never varies. Detecting unusual spending patterns involves relationships that are not fully known in advance and change over time, which is where ML adds value. Good designs combine both rather than forcing one technique onto every requirement.

options.text: Use an ML model for both requirements so that thresholds can adapt over time
options.rationale: A hard regulatory limit must not adapt or be approximated by a model.

options.text: Use deterministic rules for both requirements to keep the system auditable
options.rationale: Rules alone cannot discover the evolving patterns that indicate account takeover.

options.text: Use a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock to evaluate both requirements in a single prompt
options.rationale: Foundation models produce non-deterministic output and are a poor fit for enforcing an exact limit.

questions.question: A photo-sharing platform wants to automatically reject uploaded images containing nudity or graphic violence before they appear in public feeds, and it wants the flagged uploads reviewed by a moderator. Which pair of AWS capabilities supports this workflow?

options.text: Amazon Comprehend and SageMaker Feature Store
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes text and Feature Store stores ML features; neither screens images.

options.text: Amazon Textract and Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Textract reads documents and Guardrails filters generative AI content, not uploaded photos.

options.text: Amazon Personalize and SageMaker Model Monitor
options.rationale: Personalize recommends items and Model Monitor watches deployed model data quality.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition content moderation and Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
options.rationale: Amazon Rekognition content moderation returns moderation labels with confidence scores for images and video, and Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) routes low-confidence or flagged predictions to human reviewers. Together they cover automated screening plus human-in-the-loop review, which is a common pattern where mistakes carry reputational risk.

questions.question: A utility company is deciding whether a proposed project is a good candidate for machine learning. Which two conditions indicate that ML is a SUITABLE choice? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The relationship between the inputs and the outcome is complex and not fully documented
options.rationale: ML fits problems where the mapping from inputs to outcomes is complex or unknown and where enough representative historical data exists to learn from. It is a poor fit when outputs must be exact and reproducible against a published rule, when the logic is a simple documented calculation, or when zero errors are demanded, since models are probabilistic.

options.text: Every decision must produce an identical result for the same input, verified against a published table
options.rationale: Requiring identical, table-verified output points to a deterministic rules implementation.

options.text: A large volume of relevant historical data with known outcomes is available
options.rationale: ML fits problems where the mapping from inputs to outcomes is complex or unknown and where enough representative historical data exists to learn from. It is a poor fit when outputs must be exact and reproducible against a published rule, when the logic is a simple documented calculation, or when zero errors are demanded, since models are probabilistic.

options.text: The business requires that no incorrect prediction is ever possible
options.rationale: ML models are probabilistic and always carry some error rate.

options.text: The task is a single arithmetic calculation defined by regulation
options.rationale: A defined arithmetic rule should be coded directly rather than learned.

questions.question: An e-commerce company wants to group its customers into segments based on browsing and purchase behavior. The company has no predefined segment labels and wants the segments discovered from the data. Which type of machine learning does this describe?

options.text: Supervised learning
options.rationale: Supervised learning needs labeled target values, which the company does not have.

options.text: Reinforcement learning
options.rationale: Reinforcement learning learns through trial and reward signals, not by segmenting existing records.

options.text: Unsupervised learning
options.rationale: Discovering groups in data that has no labels is unsupervised learning, typically implemented with clustering. Supervised learning requires labeled examples of the target, reinforcement learning learns from rewards during interaction with an environment, and transfer learning reuses a pretrained model for a related task.

options.text: Transfer learning
options.rationale: Transfer learning adapts an existing trained model; it is not a way to discover unlabeled groups.

questions.question: A transportation agency is starting a machine learning project to predict maintenance needs for its bus fleet. Place the standard ML lifecycle phases in the correct order.

options.text: 1. Define the business problem and success metrics → 2. Collect and prepare the maintenance and sensor data → 3. Train and tune a model on the prepared data → 4. Evaluate the model and deploy it to production → 5. Monitor the deployed model and retrain as data changes
options.rationale: The ML lifecycle starts with framing the business problem and how success will be measured, then data collection and preparation, then model training and tuning, then evaluation and deployment, and finally ongoing monitoring with retraining as data drifts. Skipping problem framing is a common cause of models that perform well technically but deliver no business value.

options.text: 1. Monitor the deployed model and retrain as data changes → 2. Evaluate the model and deploy it to production → 3. Train and tune a model on the prepared data → 4. Collect and prepare the maintenance and sensor data → 5. Define the business problem and success metrics
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

questions.question: A telecom provider wants to analyze millions of customer support chat transcripts to understand which product issues drive negative sentiment. The provider does not want to build or train a model. Which AWS service meets this requirement?

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Amazon Comprehend provides pretrained APIs for sentiment analysis, key phrase extraction, entity recognition, and topic modeling over text, so the provider can analyze existing transcripts without training anything. Lex builds bots, Fraud Detector scores fraud risk, and Transcribe would be needed only if the source were audio.

options.text: Amazon Lex
options.rationale: Lex creates conversational bots rather than analyzing archives of past conversations.

options.text: Amazon Fraud Detector
options.rationale: Fraud Detector scores event risk and does not perform sentiment analysis.

options.text: Amazon Transcribe
options.rationale: Transcribe converts audio to text; the transcripts are already text.

questions.question: A finance team must produce month-end account balances for regulatory filings. An executive suggests using a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock to compute the balances from raw ledger entries. What is the MOST significant technical concern with this proposal?

options.text: Foundation models cannot accept numeric input in a prompt
options.rationale: Numbers can be included in a prompt; the problem is the reliability of the output.

options.text: Bedrock does not support batch processing of large inputs
options.rationale: Bedrock supports batch inference, so throughput is not the core issue.

options.text: Foundation models produce non-deterministic output, so identical inputs can yield different balances
options.rationale: Generative models sample from a probability distribution, so the same prompt can produce different responses and arithmetic is not guaranteed correct. Regulatory balances require exact, reproducible computation, which belongs in deterministic code or a database query. Recognizing where non-deterministic output is unacceptable is a core suitability judgment.

options.text: Bedrock cannot be used inside a private VPC
options.rationale: Bedrock can be accessed privately using VPC endpoints, so network isolation is not the concern.

questions.question: A mortgage lender processes scanned loan packages that contain both printed application forms and handwritten borrower notes. The lender needs the printed field values, the table of monthly obligations, and the handwritten notes captured as text. Which AWS service should the lender use?

options.text: Amazon Rekognition
options.rationale: Rekognition detects short text in images and scenes; it does not return form fields or table structure from documents.

options.text: Amazon Textract
options.rationale: Amazon Textract extracts printed and handwritten text along with form key-value pairs and table structures from scanned documents. Rekognition detects text in images but is designed for scene text such as signs and license plates rather than structured document extraction, which is the distinction being tested here.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes text that has already been extracted rather than reading scanned pages.

options.text: Amazon Kendra
options.rationale: Kendra searches indexed content and does not perform document extraction.

questions.question: A national retailer is planning several AI initiatives. Which two use cases are appropriate for Amazon Personalize? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Ranking a promotional email's product list for each individual subscriber
options.rationale: Amazon Personalize supports recommendation recipes including personalized ranking of a candidate list for a specific user and related-item recommendations. options.rationale: Amazon Personalize supports recommendation recipes including personalized ranking of a candidate list for a specific user and related-item recommendations. Staffing forecasts are a time series problem, counterfeit photo detection is computer vision, and redaction of sensitive data in text is a job for Amazon Comprehend PII detection.

options.text: Detecting counterfeit product photos submitted by third-party sellers
options.rationale: Detecting counterfeit images requires computer vision such as Amazon Rekognition.

options.text: Redacting credit card numbers from customer service notes

questions.question: A startup wants to launch an image-based plant disease identifier in six weeks. It has only 40 labeled photos per disease and a two-person engineering team with no ML background. Which approach is MOST realistic for the first release?

options.text: Train a convolutional neural network from scratch on the 40 photos per class
options.rationale: Forty images per class is far too little to train a network from scratch without severe overfitting.

options.text: Replace the ML approach with a deterministic rules engine based on pixel color thresholds
options.rationale: Fixed pixel thresholds cannot generalize across lighting, species, and disease stages.

options.text: Skip the project because computer vision always requires millions of labeled images
options.rationale: Pretrained models and transfer learning make smaller datasets viable, so abandoning the project is unnecessary.

options.text: Start with a managed vision service or a pretrained model and expand the labeled dataset before considering custom training
options.rationale: Assessing suitability includes assessing readiness. With very little labeled data and no ML expertise, starting from a managed service or pretrained model and investing in labeling is the practical path, because pretrained models already encode general visual features. Training from scratch on tiny datasets overfits, and rigid color rules cannot capture disease appearance across lighting and species.

questions.question: A hotel group publishes its website in nine languages and updates promotional copy several times a week. Human translation cannot keep pace and quality is inconsistent across vendors. Which AWS service should the group adopt for the bulk of this content?

options.text: Amazon Translate
options.rationale: Amazon Translate provides on-demand and batch neural machine translation between supported languages and supports custom terminology so brand terms stay consistent. Comprehend analyzes text without translating it, Polly produces audio, and Q Business answers questions over enterprise content.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes language attributes such as sentiment and entities; it does not translate.

options.text: Amazon Polly

options.text: Amazon Q Business
options.rationale: Q Business is an enterprise assistant, not a bulk translation pipeline.

questions.question: An industrial equipment maker collects vibration and temperature readings from thousands of pumps every minute. options.text: Anomaly detection
options.rationale: Identifying readings that deviate from a learned normal pattern, without predefined labels or thresholds, is anomaly detection. Multi-class classification requires labeled categories, while summarization and object detection apply to text and images respectively.

options.text: Multi-class classification
options.rationale: Multi-class classification needs labeled failure categories, which the engineers do not have.

options.text: Text summarization
options.rationale: Summarization applies to text, not sensor streams.

options.text: Object detection
options.rationale: Object detection locates items in images and does not apply to numeric telemetry.

questions.question: A contact center already routes calls with a fixed menu and now wants callers to speak naturally, have their intent recognized, and be connected to the right queue or self-serve where possible. Which AWS service provides the natural language understanding and dialog management for this?
