options.rationale: Text-to-speech systems produce audio and are distinct from language models.

options.text: A neural network trained on massive text corpora to predict the next token in a sequence
options.rationale: An LLM is a very large neural network, typically transformer-based, trained on huge volumes of text to predict the next token given the preceding tokens. This simple objective, applied at scale, produces general abilities such as answering questions, summarizing, and writing code.

questions.question: A solutions architect is choosing inference parameters for an Amazon Bedrock text model. Which two statements about sampling parameters are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Top-k restricts sampling to a fixed number of the most probable candidate tokens
options.rationale: Top-k keeps only the k most probable tokens as candidates at each step, while top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose combined probability reaches p. Temperature separately reshapes the probability distribution over those candidates; none of these parameters control response count, length, or model choice.

options.text: Temperature changes the maximum length of the generated response
options.rationale: Response length is controlled by the max tokens parameter, not temperature.

options.text: Top-p restricts sampling to tokens within a cumulative probability threshold
options.rationale: Top-k keeps only the k most probable tokens as candidates at each step, while top-p keeps the smallest set of tokens whose combined probability reaches p. Temperature separately reshapes the probability distribution over those candidates; none of these parameters control response count, length, or model choice.

options.text: Top-k sets the number of responses the model returns per request
options.rationale: Top-k filters candidate tokens per step; it does not create multiple responses.

options.text: Temperature determines which foundation model processes the request
options.rationale: Model selection is part of the API request, not an inference sampling parameter.

questions.question: An e-commerce company computes embeddings for its product catalog and for each search query, then returns the products whose vectors are closest to the query vector. What is this retrieval technique called?

options.text: Lexical keyword matching
options.rationale: Keyword matching compares literal terms and misses synonyms and paraphrases.

options.text: Semantic search using vector similarity
options.rationale: Semantic search embeds queries and items into the same vector space and ranks results by vector similarity measures such as cosine similarity, so items that mean the same thing match even without shared keywords. Lexical search, by contrast, ranks on exact or stemmed term overlap.

options.text: Regular expression filtering
options.rationale: Regular expressions match character patterns, not meaning.

options.text: Batch ETL aggregation
options.rationale: ETL aggregation transforms data for analytics and is not a retrieval technique.

questions.question: A film studio is planning generative AI pilots. Which two tasks require a multimodal or image and video generation model rather than a text-only model? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Creating storyboard illustrations from written scene descriptions
options.rationale: Generating illustrations and video from a written prompt requires a model that outputs visual modalities, such as a diffusion-based image or video model. Summarizing, translating, and rewriting are all text-in and text-out tasks that a text-only foundation model handles.

options.text: Summarizing a screenplay into a one-page synopsis
options.rationale: Summarization takes text in and returns text out.

options.text: Producing a short animated video clip from a text prompt
options.rationale: Generating illustrations and video from a written prompt requires a model that outputs visual modalities, such as a diffusion-based image or video model. Summarizing, translating, and rewriting are all text-in and text-out tasks that a text-only foundation model handles.

options.text: Translating subtitles from Spanish into Portuguese
options.rationale: Subtitle translation is a text-to-text task.

options.text: Rewriting dialogue lines in a more formal tone
options.rationale: Rewriting tone is a text generation task with no visual output.

questions.question: An analytics team is estimating cost and feasibility for a document question-answering feature. Which statement about tokens is accurate?

options.text: One token always equals exactly one word in every language
options.rationale: Tokens are subword units, so token counts and word counts differ, especially across languages.

options.text: Only the prompt consumes tokens; generated output is free of token limits
options.rationale: Generated output tokens are counted and limited as well.

options.text: Tokens apply to image models only, not to language models
options.rationale: Token accounting is central to language models.

options.text: Both the prompt and the completion consume tokens, and they share the model's context window
options.rationale: Token usage covers input and output together, and the sum of prompt tokens and completion tokens must fit within the model's context window. Tokens are subword units, so counts vary by language and by wording rather than mapping one to one with words.

questions.question: A supply chain company is documenting the stages of the foundation model lifecycle for its governance board. Which two statements about the lifecycle are accurate? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Pre-training uses very large volumes of mostly unlabeled data to build general capability
options.rationale: Pre-training builds broad capability from huge, largely unlabeled corpora, and fine-tuning then adapts that model to a specific task with a much smaller curated dataset. Evaluation happens before and after deployment, and feedback gathered in production feeds the next iteration of the lifecycle.

options.text: Fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model to a narrower task using a smaller curated dataset
options.rationale: Pre-training builds broad capability from huge, largely unlabeled corpora, and fine-tuning then adapts that model to a specific task with a much smaller curated dataset. Evaluation happens before and after deployment, and feedback gathered in production feeds the next iteration of the lifecycle.

options.text: Evaluation happens only after several years of production use
options.rationale: Evaluation occurs before release and continues on an ongoing basis after deployment.

options.text: Deployment ends the lifecycle, and user feedback has no role afterward
options.rationale: Post-deployment monitoring and user feedback drive continuous improvement.

options.text: Data selection is unnecessary because foundation models filter all training data automatically
options.rationale: Careful data selection and curation is a deliberate early lifecycle stage.

questions.question: An insurance company is designing a knowledge assistant over its claims handbooks and must choose a vector store. Which two capabilities should the team expect from a vector database in this architecture? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Storing high-dimensional embeddings together with metadata for filtering
options.rationale: A vector database stores embeddings with associated metadata and performs nearest-neighbor search so the application can retrieve the most semantically similar chunks for a query. It does not train models, generate embeddings, or validate the factual accuracy of the model's final answer.

options.text: Automatically fine-tuning the foundation model on retrieved passages
options.rationale: Vector stores retrieve data; they do not train or fine-tune models.

options.text: Running approximate nearest-neighbor search to find semantically similar chunks
options.rationale: A vector database stores embeddings with associated metadata and performs nearest-neighbor search so the application can retrieve the most semantically similar chunks for a query. It does not train models, generate embeddings, or validate the factual accuracy of the model's final answer.

options.text: Guaranteeing that generated answers contain no factual errors
options.rationale: Retrieval improves grounding but cannot guarantee error-free generation.

options.text: Replacing the need for an embedding model
options.rationale: An embedding model is still required to convert text into vectors before storage.

questions.question: A hospital network wants to reduce hallucinated answers in a clinical documentation assistant while keeping operational effort low. Which two approaches directly address this goal? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Ground responses in retrieved passages from approved internal sources
options.rationale: Grounding with retrieval supplies verified source text the model can rely on instead of inventing details, and prompt instructions that restrict the model to the provided context and allow it to decline reduce fabricated claims. Higher temperature increases randomness, and longer responses or a different modality do nothing for factual grounding.

options.text: Raise the temperature parameter to broaden the model's word choices
options.rationale: Higher temperature increases randomness, which tends to increase hallucination.

options.text: Increase the max tokens limit so answers can be longer
options.rationale: A longer response limit gives more room for unsupported content, not less.

options.text: Instruct the model to answer only from the provided context and to say when information is missing
options.rationale: Grounding with retrieval supplies verified source text the model can rely on instead of inventing details, and prompt instructions that restrict the model to the provided context and allow it to decline reduce fabricated claims. Higher temperature increases randomness, and longer responses or a different modality do nothing for factual grounding.

options.text: Switch from a multimodal model to an image generation model
options.rationale: Changing to an image generation model does not fit a text documentation task.

questions.question: A media company wants to launch a feature that drafts marketing copy within six weeks, and it has no machine learning engineers on staff. Which characteristic of using a pre-trained foundation model on Amazon Bedrock provides the greatest advantage for this goal?

options.text: Speed to market, because the model is already trained and is reached through a managed API
options.rationale: Pre-trained foundation models remove the data collection, training, and infrastructure work that a custom model requires, so a team can reach a working prototype in days instead of months. Speed to market, simplicity, and adaptability are the core business advantages of generative AI. Using a foundation model does not make output deterministic, unbiased, or exempt from review.

options.text: Guaranteed identical output for every request that uses the same prompt
options.rationale: Foundation models sample tokens probabilistically, so repeated calls can return different wording.

options.text: Elimination of the need to evaluate output quality before publishing
options.rationale: Generated content still needs accuracy and brand review, especially for public marketing material.

options.text: Automatic removal of all bias from the generated text
options.rationale: Foundation models inherit bias from training data and require testing and guardrails.

questions.question: A logistics company needs one solution that can summarize driver notes, draft customer status emails, and answer employee questions about internal shipping policies. Which approach uses the adaptability of generative AI with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Train a separate custom model for each of the three tasks with Amazon SageMaker AI
options.rationale: Three custom models triple the labeling, training, and maintenance effort.

options.text: Use one foundation model on Amazon Bedrock and adapt it to each task through prompt engineering
options.rationale: A single foundation model can perform many language tasks when it is instructed differently, which makes prompt engineering the lowest-effort starting point. Separate custom models, continued pre-training, and hand-written rules each add data, training, and maintenance work for results that prompting may already deliver.

options.text: Run continued pre-training on a foundation model separately for each task
options.rationale: Continued pre-training needs large volumes of domain data plus significant cost and expertise.

options.text: Build three rule-based text processing pipelines
options.rationale: Rule-based pipelines cannot generalize to open-ended summarization or drafting.

questions.question: A retailer expects generative AI chat traffic to increase tenfold during a holiday sale and then return to normal. The team does not want to plan or manage capacity. Which option meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy an open-source model on Amazon EC2 GPU instances and scale the fleet manually
options.rationale: Self-managed GPU fleets require sizing, patching, and scaling work.

options.text: Buy Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput sized for the peak and keep it all year
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput held year-round for one peak is costly and still needs sizing.

options.text: Use on-demand inference on Amazon Bedrock, which scales with request volume and bills per token
options.rationale: On-demand inference on Amazon Bedrock is a managed, pay-per-token option that absorbs variable traffic with no capacity planning, which reflects the responsiveness advantage of managed generative AI. Provisioned Throughput sized for a seasonal peak wastes money off-season, self-managed GPUs add operational work, and batch processing breaks an interactive experience.

options.text: Queue all chat requests and process them once per day with batch inference
options.rationale: Daily batch processing cannot support a live chat conversation.

questions.question: A public sector agency wants its staff to produce plain-language summaries of long regulations more quickly. Which statement best describes a realistic benefit of using generative AI for this work?

options.text: It produces legally binding text that needs no review
options.rationale: Generated text can contain errors or omissions and must be reviewed, especially in regulated communication.

options.text: It removes the need for subject matter experts in the process
options.rationale: Experts are still needed to validate meaning and approve final wording.

options.text: It returns the same summary word for word on every run
options.rationale: Sampling causes wording to vary between runs unless generation settings are tightly constrained.

options.text: It can draft readable summaries at scale that staff then review and finalize
options.rationale: Generative AI delivers the most value as a drafting accelerator: it creates a usable first version quickly while a human stays accountable for accuracy and tone. Claims that it eliminates review, replaces experts, or behaves deterministically overstate what the technology does.

questions.question: A financial services firm pilots a chatbot that answers questions about its products. Testers report that the bot occasionally cites a product feature that the firm does not offer, stated in a confident tone. Which limitation of generative AI does this describe?

options.text: Overfitting
options.rationale: Overfitting is a training problem where a model memorizes training data and generalizes poorly.

options.text: Data drift
options.rationale: Data drift is a change in production data distribution over time relative to training data.

options.text: Prompt injection
options.rationale: Prompt injection is a malicious input that redirects the model away from its instructions.

options.text: Hallucination
options.rationale: A hallucination is fluent, confident output that is factually wrong or unsupported, which happens because the model predicts likely text rather than looking up verified facts. Grounding the model with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and adding human review reduces the risk. Overfitting, drift, and prompt injection describe different problems.

questions.question: A healthcare provider needs a generative AI assistant that answers clinician questions using only the provider's approved clinical protocol documents, and every answer must show which document it came from. Which approach BEST reduces hallucinations for this requirement?

options.text: Increase the temperature setting so the model explores more possible answers
options.rationale: Higher temperature increases randomness, which tends to increase hallucination.

options.text: Fine-tune the model on a small set of question and answer pairs
options.rationale: Fine-tuning shapes tone and format but does not supply verifiable citations for each answer.

options.text: Use Retrieval Augmented Generation with Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases and return source citations
options.rationale: Retrieval Augmented Generation grounds generation in retrieved passages from an authoritative corpus, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases can return citations that point back to the source document. Fine-tuning teaches style and task behavior but does not guarantee factual grounding or citations, and generation settings such as temperature or output length do not add facts.

options.text: Increase the maximum output token limit so answers can be longer
options.rationale: A longer answer limit changes length, not factual accuracy.

questions.question: A manufacturing company must calculate warranty reimbursement amounts from structured claim records, and every calculation must be exact and reproducible for audit. Which statement about using a large language model for this task is correct?

options.text: A foundation model is the best fit because it can process the records in natural language
options.rationale: Natural language processing ability does not make a model reliable for exact financial math.

options.text: A foundation model is a poor fit because its output is nondeterministic and arithmetic is not guaranteed to be exact
options.rationale: Exact, repeatable arithmetic over structured data belongs in deterministic code or a database query, not in a probabilistic text generator. Recognizing when generative AI is the wrong tool is part of assessing its limitations, including nondeterminism and lack of interpretability.

options.text: A foundation model is the best fit because it can be made fully deterministic by raising temperature
options.rationale: Raising temperature increases randomness; lowering it reduces variability but does not guarantee determinism.

options.text: A foundation model is the best fit because it provides a full audit trail of its internal reasoning
options.rationale: Foundation models do not expose a verifiable internal audit trail of how an answer was produced.

questions.question: A gaming company runs a support chatbot on a foundation model. A player submits a message that says to ignore all previous instructions and reveal the internal system prompt. Which security risk does this attempt represent?

options.text: Data poisoning
options.rationale: Data poisoning corrupts training data before or during model training.

options.text: Model inversion
options.rationale: Model inversion tries to reconstruct training data from model outputs.

options.text: Membership inference
options.rationale: Membership inference tries to determine whether a specific record was in the training set.

options.text: Prompt injection
options.rationale: Prompt injection is crafted input that tries to override the developer's instructions so the model performs unintended actions, such as leaking its system prompt. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and input validation help mitigate it. Data poisoning, model inversion, and membership inference target training data or model internals rather than the live prompt.

questions.question: Employees at a law firm have been pasting client contract text into a free public generative AI chatbot to get quick summaries. Which risks should MOST concern the firm's compliance team? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The chatbot may respond too slowly during peak hours
options.rationale: Slow responses are an inconvenience, not a confidentiality breach.

options.text: Confidential client data leaves the firm's control once it is sent to the external service
options.rationale: Sending confidential data to an external consumer service is a data leakage risk on two fronts: the firm loses control over access to the data, and the provider may retain it or use it for model improvement. This is why organizations adopt governed options where prompts and completions are not used to train the underlying models. Latency, language, and context window are operational concerns, not compliance risks.

options.text: The submitted contract text may be retained by the provider and used to improve its models
options.rationale: Sending confidential data to an external consumer service is a data leakage risk on two fronts: the firm loses control over access to the data, and the provider may retain it or use it for model improvement. This is why organizations adopt governed options where prompts and completions are not used to train the underlying models. Latency, language, and context window are operational concerns, not compliance risks.

options.text: The chatbot may produce summaries in the wrong language
options.rationale: Output language is controllable through prompting and is not a compliance risk.

options.text: The firm may exceed the chatbot's context window
options.rationale: Context window limits truncate input; they do not expose client data.

questions.question: A bank wants to use a large language model to decide whether to approve consumer loan applications. Regulators require the bank to explain the specific reasons for each denial. Which limitation of foundation models MOST directly conflicts with this requirement?

options.text: Foundation models have low interpretability, so their internal decision process is difficult to explain
options.rationale: Foundation models are very large neural networks whose internal reasoning cannot be traced to specific, verifiable factors, which conflicts with regulatory demands for adverse action explanations. High-stakes, regulated decisions favor simpler, more interpretable models with tools such as SageMaker Clarify for explainability analysis.

options.text: Foundation models cannot process numeric input of any kind
options.rationale: Models can read numbers in text, even though exact computation is unreliable; input format is not the core issue.

options.text: Foundation models are only available in a small number of AWS Regions
options.rationale: Regional availability varies but is not the fundamental conflict with explainability rules.

options.text: Foundation models cannot output a simple approve or deny label
options.rationale: A model can easily be prompted to output a label; justifying the label is the problem.

questions.question: A media startup is evaluating whether to add generative AI to its publishing workflow. Which risks are specific concerns the startup should assess before launch? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Generated articles may include fabricated facts stated confidently
options.rationale: Hallucination and intellectual property exposure are two of the most cited risks for publishing use cases: models can invent facts, and generated text or images can resemble copyrighted works from training data. The other statements are factually wrong; models run continuously, can generate long documents, and managed services can be configured to satisfy residency requirements.

options.text: Generated content may raise intellectual property concerns if it closely resembles copyrighted training material
options.rationale: Hallucination and intellectual property exposure are two of the most cited risks for publishing use cases: models can invent facts, and generated text or images can resemble copyrighted works from training data. The other statements are factually wrong; models run continuously, can generate long documents, and managed services can be configured to satisfy residency requirements.

options.text: The foundation model will refuse to run outside business hours
options.rationale: Managed model endpoints serve requests at any time.

options.text: Foundation models cannot generate text longer than one paragraph
options.rationale: Output length is bounded by token limits that allow many pages of text.

options.text: Using a managed AI service always violates data residency laws
options.rationale: Data residency depends on Region and configuration choices, not on managed services as a category.

questions.question: A company's finance team is surprised that the monthly bill for its generative AI application varies widely even though the number of users is stable. Which TWO factors MOST likely contribute to this variation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Longer prompts, including large retrieved context passages, increase the number of billed input tokens
options.rationale: On-demand generative AI pricing is metered per input and output token, so prompt length, retrieved context size, and response length all move the bill even when user counts are flat. This cost unpredictability is managed through prompt design, output token limits, model choice, and usage monitoring.

options.text: Longer model responses increase the number of billed output tokens
options.rationale: On-demand generative AI pricing is metered per input and output token, so prompt length, retrieved context size, and response length all move the bill even when user counts are flat. This cost unpredictability is managed through prompt design, output token limits, model choice, and usage monitoring.

options.text: On-demand token prices are renegotiated every hour on a GPU spot market
options.rationale: On-demand token prices are published rates, not hourly spot market prices.

options.text: Foundation models bill a fixed per-user license fee that changes each month
options.rationale: On-demand Amazon Bedrock pricing is usage based, not a per-user license fee.

options.text: Requests that return an error are billed at ten times the normal rate
options.rationale: Billing is based on tokens processed, not on penalty rates for errors.

questions.question: A social platform is testing a foundation model for auto-replies. During red-team testing the model sometimes produces insulting or hateful text when provoked. Which AWS capability is designed to filter this harmful content in both prompts and responses?

options.text: SageMaker Model Monitor
options.rationale: Model Monitor detects data and quality drift for models in production; it does not filter toxic text.

options.text: Amazon Macie
options.rationale: Macie finds sensitive data in S3 buckets; it does not moderate model conversations.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails applies configurable safeguards such as content filters for hate, insults, violence, and sexual content, along with denied topics and sensitive information filters, to both user inputs and model outputs. Model Monitor watches deployed ML model quality, Macie discovers sensitive data in Amazon S3, and CloudTrail logs API activity.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API calls for auditing; it does not inspect generated content.

questions.question: A customer service team runs the same prompt through a foundation model twice and receives two differently worded but similar answers. The team asks why. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The model samples from a probability distribution over tokens, so outputs can vary between runs
options.rationale: Generative models are nondeterministic by design: each token is sampled from a probability distribution shaped by settings such as temperature, top-p, and top-k. Lowering temperature makes output more consistent but variability can remain. Retraining, context expiry, and service routing are not what causes run-to-run variation.

options.text: The model was retrained between the two requests
options.rationale: Foundation models are not retrained between individual inference requests.

options.text: The context window expired between requests, forcing a new answer
options.rationale: A context window is a per-request input size limit; it does not expire between calls.

options.text: One request was routed to a completely different AWS service
options.rationale: Both requests go to the same model endpoint; routing does not explain wording changes.

questions.question: A healthcare company is choosing a foundation model on Amazon Bedrock for an assistant that must analyze medical intake forms containing both text and photographs, and it must serve users in an AWS Region approved for its compliance program. Which selection criteria are MOST important for this use case? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Multimodal capability so the model can process images and text together
options.rationale: The requirements state two hard constraints: the model must accept image and text input, which requires a multimodal model, and it must be offered in the approved Region. Model age, popularity, and naming are not meaningful selection criteria; capability, modality, Region availability, cost, latency, and customization support are.

options.text: Availability of the model in the required AWS Region
options.rationale: The requirements state two hard constraints: the model must accept image and text input, which requires a multimodal model, and it must be offered in the approved Region. Model age, popularity, and naming are not meaningful selection criteria; capability, modality, Region availability, cost, latency, and customization support are.

options.text: Whether the model was released before 2020
options.rationale: Release date does not determine fitness; capability and evaluation results do.

options.text: The number of other companies using the same model
options.rationale: Adoption by others does not satisfy this company's modality or compliance constraints.

options.text: Whether the model name includes the word medical
options.rationale: A model's name says nothing about its measured performance on a task.

questions.question: A legal technology company needs a foundation model that can accept an entire 300-page contract in a single request so the model can answer questions that reference clauses from any part of the document. Which model characteristic should the company evaluate FIRST?

options.text: Top-k sampling range
options.rationale: Top-k controls sampling diversity during generation, not input capacity.

options.text: Context window size
options.rationale: The context window is the maximum number of tokens a model can consider in one request, covering the prompt, any inserted documents, and the response. A 300-page contract requires a model with a very large context window; otherwise the document must be chunked and retrieved. Sampling settings, languages, and dataset licensing do not determine how much input fits.

options.text: Number of supported output languages
options.rationale: Multilingual support matters for language coverage, not for document length.

options.text: Training dataset license
options.rationale: Training data licensing relates to IP risk, not to input size.

questions.question: A gaming studio needs sub-second responses for short in-game dialogue suggestions and wants to minimize inference cost at very high request volume. Quality requirements are modest. Which model choice BEST fits these requirements?

options.text: The largest available frontier model, because larger models are always the right default
options.rationale: The largest model costs more and responds more slowly; the requirements do not demand top-tier quality.

options.text: A smaller, faster foundation model that meets the quality bar at lower latency and lower cost per token
options.rationale: Model selection is a tradeoff among cost, latency, and accuracy. Smaller models respond faster and cost less per token, so when they meet the quality bar they are the better choice for high-volume, latency-sensitive workloads. Oversized models or multi-model ensembles raise both latency and cost without a required quality gain.

options.text: An ensemble of three large models voting on each response
options.rationale: Running three large models multiplies cost and latency, the opposite of the goal.

options.text: A model chosen only for its support of 30 or more languages
options.rationale: Language coverage is not one of the stated requirements.

questions.question: A travel company wants its assistant to answer customer questions in Spanish, Japanese, and German as well as English. When comparing foundation models on Amazon Bedrock, which model attribute MOST directly addresses this requirement?

options.text: Model size in parameters
options.rationale: A large model is not automatically strong in every language.

options.text: Provisioned Throughput pricing
options.rationale: Pricing structure affects cost, not language ability.

options.text: Multilingual capability of the model
options.rationale: Multilingual support describes which languages a model understands and generates well, and it varies significantly between models, so it must be verified against the target languages. Parameter count, pricing model, and output limits do not indicate language coverage.

options.text: Maximum output token limit
options.rationale: Output token limits bound response length, not language support.

questions.question: A company shortlists two foundation models. Model A scores slightly higher on public benchmarks. Model B costs 70 percent less per 1,000 tokens and responds twice as fast. The use case is internal meeting summarization where minor quality differences are acceptable. What is the MOST appropriate next step before choosing?

options.text: Choose Model A because higher benchmark scores always transfer to every task
options.rationale: Benchmark leadership does not guarantee better results on a specific internal task.

options.text: Choose Model B immediately because cost is the only criterion that matters
options.rationale: Cost matters, but quality must be validated as acceptable first.

options.text: Evaluate both models on a sample of the company's own meeting transcripts and compare quality against cost and latency
options.rationale: Public benchmarks measure general ability but do not guarantee performance on a specific workload, so the right practice is to evaluate candidate models on representative company data, using tools such as Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation, then weigh quality against cost and latency. If Model B meets the quality bar on real transcripts, its cost and speed advantages make it the better business choice.

options.text: Choose the model with the larger parameter count
options.rationale: Parameter count is a poor proxy for task performance and ignores cost and latency.

questions.question: A pharmaceutical company plans to eventually fine-tune a foundation model on proprietary research abstracts. When shortlisting models on Amazon Bedrock today, which selection criterion does this future plan add?

options.text: Whether the model supports customization such as fine-tuning
options.rationale: Not every foundation model on Amazon Bedrock supports customization; fine-tuning is available only for specific models. If customization is on the roadmap, model choice must include customization support alongside cost, latency, and quality. Price, streaming, and image generation do not address the fine-tuning plan.

options.text: Whether the model has the lowest on-demand token price
options.rationale: The cheapest model may not be customizable at all.

options.text: Whether the model supports streaming responses
options.rationale: Streaming improves perceived latency but is unrelated to fine-tuning support.

options.text: Whether the model can generate images
options.rationale: Image generation is a different modality and irrelevant to this text use case.

questions.question: A startup must decide between calling a proprietary foundation model through Amazon Bedrock and self-hosting an open-weights model on GPU instances it manages. Which statements accurately describe this build versus buy tradeoff? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The managed API option shifts infrastructure management to AWS and reaches production faster
options.rationale: The core tradeoff is speed and simplicity versus control and responsibility: a managed API removes infrastructure work and accelerates launch, while self-hosting offers deeper control over model, versioning, and environment at the price of GPU management and specialized skills. Cost advantage depends on utilization, managed platforms do offer customization paths, and many open-weights models carry commercial-friendly licenses.

options.text: Self-hosting gives more control over the model and environment but requires ML and infrastructure expertise
options.rationale: The core tradeoff is speed and simplicity versus control and responsibility: a managed API removes infrastructure work and accelerates launch, while self-hosting offers deeper control over model, versioning, and environment at the price of GPU management and specialized skills. Cost advantage depends on utilization, managed platforms do offer customization paths, and many open-weights models carry commercial-friendly licenses.

options.text: Self-hosting is always cheaper regardless of traffic volume
options.rationale: At low or spiky utilization, per-token managed pricing is often cheaper than idle GPUs.

options.text: A managed API legally prevents the startup from ever customizing a model
options.rationale: Amazon Bedrock supports fine-tuning for certain models, so customization remains possible.

options.text: Open-weights models cannot be used for commercial purposes
options.rationale: Many open-weights models, such as Meta Llama variants, permit commercial use under their licenses.

questions.question: An online retailer adds a generative AI shopping assistant to product pages. The business sponsor wants to know whether the assistant increases the percentage of visitors who complete a purchase. Which metric directly measures this outcome?

options.text: Cost per inference
options.rationale: Cost per inference tracks spending, not customer purchasing behavior.

options.text: Conversion rate
options.rationale: Conversion rate measures the share of visitors who complete a desired action such as a purchase, so comparing conversion between users who engage with the assistant and those who do not shows business impact. Cost per inference measures expense, tokens per second measures throughput, and parameter count describes model size, none of which capture purchasing behavior.

options.text: Tokens per second
options.rationale: Tokens per second is a performance throughput metric.

options.text: Model parameter count
options.rationale: Parameter count is a model property, not a business outcome.

questions.question: A subscription streaming service launches a generative AI recommendation and search experience. Executives want to know whether the feature makes each subscriber more valuable over the entire time they remain a customer. Which metric BEST captures this?

options.text: Customer lifetime value
options.rationale: Customer lifetime value estimates total revenue a customer generates across the whole relationship, so an increase after launch indicates the feature deepens engagement and retention. Cost per token and time to first token are operational metrics, and training loss is a model training statistic.

options.text: Cost per token
options.rationale: Cost per token measures inference expense, not customer value.

options.text: Time to first token
options.rationale: Time to first token measures response latency.

options.text: Training loss
options.rationale: Training loss reflects model fit during training, not business value.

questions.question: A telecom company deploys a generative AI assistant that drafts responses for support agents. Leadership wants a single number showing whether agents resolve tickets with less effort than before. Which metric is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Average handling time per ticket compared with the pre-launch baseline
options.rationale: Efficiency gains are measured by comparing an operational baseline before and after deployment, and average handling time per ticket captures agent effort directly. Counting evaluated models, parameters, or prompt templates describes project activity rather than realized business benefit.

options.text: Number of foundation models evaluated during the pilot
options.rationale: The number of models tested is a project activity measure, not an efficiency outcome.

options.text: Total parameters in the selected model
options.rationale: Parameter count says nothing about agent productivity.

options.text: Number of prompt templates in the repository
options.rationale: Template count measures artifacts created, not effort saved.

questions.question: A finance company must justify continued investment in its generative AI document assistant. Which measurements are appropriate business value metrics for this decision? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Average revenue per user for accounts that use the assistant
options.rationale: Business value is assessed by linking the feature to revenue and to cost displaced. Average revenue per user shows monetization impact, and comparing cost per inference with the cost of the manual process shows whether automation pays off. Infrastructure counts, index size, and prompt length are implementation details.

options.text: Cost per inference relative to the manual process cost it replaces
options.rationale: Business value is assessed by linking the feature to revenue and to cost displaced. Average revenue per user shows monetization impact, and comparing cost per inference with the cost of the manual process shows whether automation pays off. Infrastructure counts, index size, and prompt length are implementation details.

options.text: The number of GPUs in the AWS Region hosting the model
options.rationale: Regional GPU capacity is not a business outcome the company controls or reports.

options.text: The size of the vector index in gigabytes
options.rationale: Index size is a storage detail, not a value measure.

options.text: The number of tokens in the longest system prompt
options.rationale: System prompt length affects token cost slightly but is not a business metric.

questions.question: A conglomerate wants one generative AI platform that serves legal, HR, engineering, and marketing teams instead of four narrow tools. Which advantage of foundation models makes this feasible?

options.text: Cross-domain performance, since a single foundation model generalizes across many subject areas and tasks
options.rationale: Foundation models are trained on broad, diverse data, so one model can be pointed at legal drafting, HR question answering, code assistance, and marketing copy through prompting and grounding. That cross-domain performance is what allows a shared platform. Determinism, interpretability, and free inference are not properties of these models.

options.text: Deterministic output, which guarantees consistent results for every department
options.rationale: Generative models sample probabilistically and do not guarantee identical output.

options.text: Full interpretability, which lets each department audit internal reasoning
options.rationale: Foundation models have limited interpretability and cannot expose auditable reasoning.

options.text: Zero inference cost after the first request is cached
options.rationale: Caching can reduce cost for repeated content but inference is never free.

questions.question: An insurance company needs to predict, from 10 years of structured policy and claim records, the probability that a policyholder will file a claim next year. Which approach is MOST appropriate?

options.text: Prompt a large language model to guess a probability for each policyholder
options.rationale: An LLM has no calibrated probability estimate for this company's policyholders and cannot be validated the same way.

options.text: Build a supervised classification model with Amazon SageMaker AI using the historical tabular data
options.rationale: Predicting a numeric probability from labeled historical tabular data is a classic supervised learning problem, best solved with a trained classification model that can be evaluated with standard metrics and monitored over time. This item tests recognizing when generative AI is the wrong tool.

options.text: Use a text-to-image foundation model on Amazon Bedrock
options.rationale: Image generation is unrelated to numeric risk prediction.

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases to retrieve policy documents and let the model answer
options.rationale: Retrieval over documents answers questions about text; it does not produce statistical predictions.

questions.question: A logistics company needs to extract printed addresses and table data from millions of scanned paper shipping manifests. Which AWS service is the MOST appropriate choice?

options.text: Amazon Textract
options.rationale: Amazon Textract extracts text, forms, and tables from scanned documents and images, which is exactly this requirement and needs no generative model. Comprehend analyzes text that has already been extracted, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Translate converts text between languages.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend performs NLP such as entity and sentiment analysis on existing text.

options.text: Amazon Transcribe
options.rationale: Transcribe handles audio, not scanned paper documents.

options.text: Amazon Translate
options.rationale: Translate converts languages and does not read scanned images.

questions.question: A support organization wants to classify incoming emails by sentiment and detect customer names and account numbers, with no custom model training. Which service meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Amazon Kendra
options.rationale: Kendra searches and ranks documents rather than classifying sentiment.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Amazon Comprehend provides pre-trained natural language processing for sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and detection of personally identifiable information, so no training work is required. Kendra performs enterprise search, Polly synthesizes speech, and Rekognition analyzes images and video.

options.text: Amazon Polly
options.rationale: Polly converts text into spoken audio.

options.text: Amazon Rekognition
options.rationale: Rekognition analyzes visual content, not email text.

questions.question: A software company wants an assistant that answers employee questions using content in its internal wiki, Amazon S3, and ticketing system, with enterprise permissions respected and minimal development work. Which AWS service is the BEST fit?

options.text: Amazon Q Business
options.rationale: Amazon Q Business is a managed generative AI assistant that connects to enterprise data sources, respects existing access permissions, and requires no custom application build. Amazon Q Developer assists with coding and AWS tasks, SageMaker Canvas is a no-code ML modeling tool, and Bedrock Flows orchestrates generative AI workflows that you design yourself.

options.text: Amazon Q Developer
options.rationale: Amazon Q Developer targets software development and AWS operations, not enterprise knowledge search.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Canvas
options.rationale: SageMaker Canvas builds predictive ML models without code; it is not an enterprise assistant.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Flows
options.rationale: Bedrock Flows requires you to build and connect the workflow components.

questions.question: A hospital deploys a generative AI assistant that drafts patient discharge instructions. Because incorrect instructions could harm patients, the hospital must add a clinician review step before any document is released. Which AWS capability supports this human review workflow?

options.text: SageMaker Feature Store
options.rationale: Feature Store stores and serves ML features for training and inference.

options.text: SageMaker Autopilot
options.rationale: Autopilot automatically trains and tunes candidate models on tabular data.

options.text: AWS AI Service Cards
options.rationale: AI Service Cards provide transparency documentation, not a review workflow.

options.text: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
options.rationale: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) builds human review workflows into machine learning and AI predictions so people can verify or correct output before it is used. Keeping a human in the loop is the standard mitigation for high-stakes generative AI output. Feature Store manages ML features, Autopilot automates model building, and AI Service Cards document service characteristics.

questions.question: A retail company is running a structured evaluation to choose a foundation model for product description generation. Place the steps in the correct order.

options.text: 1. Define the business requirement and the quality criteria for an acceptable description → 2. Build a representative test set of products and reference descriptions → 3. Compare candidate models on quality, latency, and cost using the same test set → 4. Select the model that meets the quality bar at the lowest cost and deploy a limited pilot
options.rationale: Sound model selection starts with the business requirement and explicit quality criteria, then builds a representative test set so comparisons are meaningful. Only after candidates are scored on the same data can quality be weighed against latency and cost, leading to a pilot deployment. Choosing a model before defining success leads to rework.

options.text: 1. Select the model that meets the quality bar at the lowest cost and deploy a limited pilot → 2. Compare candidate models on quality, latency, and cost using the same test set → 3. Build a representative test set of products and reference descriptions → 4. Define the business requirement and the quality criteria for an acceptable description
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Build a representative test set of products and reference descriptions → 2. Compare candidate models on quality, latency, and cost using the same test set → 3. Select the model that meets the quality bar at the lowest cost and deploy a limited pilot → 4. Define the business requirement and the quality criteria for an acceptable description
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Build a representative test set of products and reference descriptions → 2. Define the business requirement and the quality criteria for an acceptable description → 3. Compare candidate models on quality, latency, and cost using the same test set → 4. Select the model that meets the quality bar at the lowest cost and deploy a limited pilot
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

questions.question: A company plans to fine-tune a foundation model using customer support transcripts that contain names, email addresses, and payment card numbers. Which risk is MOST directly created by this plan?

options.text: The model may reproduce sensitive customer information in responses to other users
options.rationale: Training on unredacted records creates data leakage risk, because a customized model can surface memorized sensitive details in later outputs. The mitigation is to redact or tokenize personal data before customization and to add sensitive information filters in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. Fine-tuning can narrow general ability somewhat, but it does not remove it, make output deterministic, or block evaluation.

options.text: The model will no longer be able to answer general questions in any domain
options.rationale: Fine-tuning can shift behavior toward the task but does not eliminate general capability.

options.text: Fine-tuning will make the model deterministic and unable to vary phrasing
options.rationale: Determinism depends on inference settings, not on whether the model was fine-tuned.

options.text: The fine-tuned model can no longer be evaluated for accuracy
options.rationale: Customized models can and should be evaluated with held-out test data.

questions.question: A design agency wants to generate marketing images with a foundation model but is concerned that generated art could resemble protected works and create legal exposure. Which actions MOST directly address this concern? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Increase the image resolution setting
options.rationale: Higher resolution changes image quality, not IP risk.

options.text: Review the model provider's usage terms and any indemnification coverage before adopting the model
options.rationale: Intellectual property exposure is a legal and governance risk, so it is managed through provider terms, available indemnification, usage policies, and human legal review before assets are published. Technical settings such as resolution, sampling parameters, or output count do not change copyright risk.

options.text: Lower the temperature parameter for image generation
options.rationale: Sampling settings alter variability, not the legal status of an output.

options.text: Add a legal review of generated assets before they are published
options.rationale: Intellectual property exposure is a legal and governance risk, so it is managed through provider terms, available indemnification, usage policies, and human legal review before assets are published. Technical settings such as resolution, sampling parameters, or output count do not change copyright risk.

options.text: Generate more images per prompt so there are more options
options.rationale: More candidate images does not reduce the chance that one resembles a protected work.

questions.question: A startup with two developers and no ML infrastructure wants a customer-facing generative AI feature live this quarter. Which build versus buy decision BEST matches its constraints?

options.text: Pre-train a foundation model from scratch on public web data
options.rationale: Pre-training a foundation model requires enormous data, compute, and expertise.

options.text: Consume a managed foundation model through the Amazon Bedrock API
options.rationale: Buying access to a managed foundation model gives a small team production capability without training data, GPU capacity, or ML research skills. Pre-training from scratch or standing up hardware costs millions of dollars and months of effort, which no two-person team can absorb in a quarter.

options.text: Purchase and colocate GPU servers to host a model in a data center
options.rationale: Buying and colocating GPUs adds capital cost and operational burden.

options.text: Hire a research team to design a new model architecture
options.rationale: Building a research team cannot deliver a feature within the quarter.

questions.question: A payments company runs a generative AI assistant with steady, predictable traffic of about 400 requests per second all day and needs consistent throughput guarantees. Which Amazon Bedrock option BEST controls cost and performance for this profile?

options.text: On-demand inference only, because it is always the cheapest option
options.rationale: On-demand is best for spiky or low traffic; at constant heavy volume it can cost more and offers no reserved throughput.

options.text: Provisioned Throughput, which reserves capacity for predictable high-volume workloads
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput reserves model capacity for a committed term, which suits sustained, predictable high volume and provides consistent throughput at a known price. On-demand pricing is better for variable or low traffic; at constant heavy load a reservation is typically more economical. Batch inference does not fit interactive assistants.

options.text: Batch inference submitted once per hour
options.rationale: Hourly batch jobs cannot serve real-time assistant requests.

options.text: Deploying the model to a public web server without capacity planning
options.rationale: Skipping capacity planning is not an Amazon Bedrock option and would not guarantee throughput.

questions.question: A retail chain wants a system that recommends products to individual shoppers based on their browsing and purchase history. The team has no ML specialists. Which service is purpose-built for this requirement?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.rationale: Agents orchestrate API calls and reasoning steps; they are not a recommendation engine.

options.text: Amazon Lex
options.rationale: Lex handles dialog management for chat and voice bots.

options.text: Amazon Personalize
options.rationale: Amazon Personalize is a managed service built for real-time personalization and recommendations from user interaction data, so it fits better than a general generative model. Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step generative tasks, Lex builds conversational interfaces, and Comprehend analyzes text.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend extracts insight from text, not personalized product rankings.

questions.question: A company must decide whether a generative AI approach or a traditional deterministic approach fits each requirement. For which requirements is generative AI the WRONG tool? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Producing an exact monthly account balance from transaction records
options.rationale: Tasks requiring exact computation or strict rule enforcement should use deterministic code or database logic, since generative output varies and cannot guarantee arithmetic or pattern correctness. Drafting, summarizing, and rewriting open-ended language are natural strengths of generative models.

options.text: Enforcing a validation rule that a submitted postal code matches a fixed pattern
options.rationale: Tasks requiring exact computation or strict rule enforcement should use deterministic code or database logic, since generative output varies and cannot guarantee arithmetic or pattern correctness. Drafting, summarizing, and rewriting open-ended language are natural strengths of generative models.

options.text: Drafting a personalized onboarding email for each new customer
options.rationale: Personalized drafting from customer attributes is a strong generative AI use case.

options.text: Summarizing the main themes across thousands of open-ended survey comments
options.rationale: Thematic summarization of unstructured comments suits generative models well.

options.text: Rewriting technical release notes in plain language for non-technical readers
options.rationale: Rewriting for a different audience is a language transformation task generative AI handles well.

questions.question: A media company measures its generative AI captioning feature and finds the model produces good captions but each request costs more than expected because the prompt includes 20 long few-shot examples. Which change reduces cost with the least quality risk?

options.text: Switch to a much larger model with a bigger context window
options.rationale: Larger models generally cost more per token, which worsens the problem.

options.text: Trim the prompt to the few examples that measurably improve output and re-evaluate quality
options.rationale: Input tokens are billed, so long prompts raise cost on every request. Pruning few-shot examples down to the ones that demonstrably help, then re-measuring quality, reduces token spend while protecting output. A larger model raises cost, stripping instructions degrades quality, and a higher output limit increases output tokens rather than reducing calls.

options.text: Remove all instructions from the prompt
options.rationale: Removing instructions damages output quality and consistency.

options.text: Increase the maximum output tokens to reduce the number of calls
options.rationale: Allowing longer responses increases billed output tokens.

questions.question: A public sector agency is moving a generative AI assistant from idea to production. Place the phases in the correct order.

options.text: 1. Identify the business problem and confirm that generative AI is the right tool for it → 2. Select and evaluate candidate foundation models against the defined success criteria → 3. Run a limited pilot with real users and measure business metrics against the baseline → 4. Deploy to production with guardrails, human review, and monitoring of quality and cost
options.rationale: Value comes from confirming the problem fits generative AI before any model work, then evaluating candidate models against defined criteria, piloting with real users to measure business impact, and only then deploying broadly with guardrails, human review, and ongoing monitoring. Skipping the fit assessment is the most common source of failed generative AI projects.

options.text: 1. Deploy to production with guardrails, human review, and monitoring of quality and cost → 2. Run a limited pilot with real users and measure business metrics against the baseline → 3. Select and evaluate candidate foundation models against the defined success criteria → 4. Identify the business problem and confirm that generative AI is the right tool for it
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Select and evaluate candidate foundation models against the defined success criteria → 2. Run a limited pilot with real users and measure business metrics against the baseline → 3. Deploy to production with guardrails, human review, and monitoring of quality and cost → 4. Identify the business problem and confirm that generative AI is the right tool for it
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Select and evaluate candidate foundation models against the defined success criteria → 2. Identify the business problem and confirm that generative AI is the right tool for it → 3. Run a limited pilot with real users and measure business metrics against the baseline → 4. Deploy to production with guardrails, human review, and monitoring of quality and cost
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

questions.question: A logistics startup wants to call several foundation models from different providers through a single API to build a shipment-summarization feature. The team has no ML engineers and does not want to provision or patch any servers. Which AWS service meets these requirements?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints
options.rationale: SageMaker AI endpoints require you to choose instance types, manage scaling, and operate the endpoint.

options.text: Amazon EC2 instances with the AWS Deep Learning AMI
options.rationale: Self-managed EC2 hosting means you own model weights, drivers, scaling, and patching.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock
options.rationale: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed, serverless service that exposes foundation models from Amazon and several third-party providers through a common set of APIs. There is no infrastructure to provision, scale, or patch, and billing is based on tokens processed. That makes it the lowest-overhead choice for a team without ML specialists.

options.text: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with self-hosted models
options.rationale: Running models on EKS adds cluster and container operations that this team cannot support.

questions.question: A media company wants a product manager to type a few sample prompts into a console and visually compare the responses of three different foundation models before any code is written. Which Amazon Bedrock capability should the company use?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock playgrounds
options.rationale: Bedrock playgrounds are console environments for chat, text, and image models where a user can enter prompts, adjust inference parameters, and inspect responses without writing code. They are designed for quick, hands-on model exploration. Formal side-by-side scoring with metrics is handled later by Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput buys committed model capacity; it does not provide an interactive console for prompt testing.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import
options.rationale: Custom Model Import brings externally trained model weights into Bedrock, which is unrelated to console experimentation.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.rationale: Agents orchestrate multi-step tasks against APIs and data sources rather than offering a prompt sandbox.

questions.question: A gaming company is building a multi-turn in-game assistant on Amazon Bedrock. Developers want one consistent request format for conversation history, system instructions, and tool use so they can swap between Anthropic Claude and Amazon Nova models without rewriting the request payload. Which approach meets this requirement?

options.text: Call InvokeModel and build each provider's native JSON body in the application
options.rationale: InvokeModel requires provider-specific request and response bodies, which is exactly the coupling the team wants to avoid.

options.text: Use the Amazon Bedrock Converse API
options.rationale: The Converse API provides a unified, model-agnostic interface for conversational inference on Bedrock, with standard fields for messages, system prompts, inference configuration, and tool use. Because the shape is the same across supported models, switching models is usually a change to the model ID. ConverseStream provides the same interface for streaming responses.

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock Batch inference for every conversation turn
options.rationale: Batch inference is asynchronous and intended for large offline jobs, not interactive dialogue.

options.text: Deploy each model behind its own Amazon API Gateway resource and translate payloads in AWS Lambda
options.rationale: Custom translation layers add code and operational burden that the Converse API already removes.

questions.question: A developer uses the Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel operation and switches the model ID from one provider's text model to another provider's text model. The application now fails to parse the response. What is the MOST likely cause?

options.text: InvokeModel supports only a single foundation model per AWS account
options.rationale: Bedrock does not restrict an account to one model; access is granted per model.

options.text: The application must purchase Provisioned Throughput before any model can be invoked
options.rationale: On-demand invocation works without Provisioned Throughput, which is a capacity commitment option.

options.text: InvokeModel cannot return text output and requires Amazon Bedrock Flows
options.rationale: InvokeModel returns text for text models; Flows is a visual workflow builder, not a requirement for inference.

options.text: InvokeModel passes a provider-specific request and response body, so the JSON structure differs between models
options.rationale: With InvokeModel the body is the model provider's native payload, so field names for prompts, token limits, and returned completions vary by model family. Changing the model ID therefore usually requires changing the parsing logic. The Converse API exists precisely to normalize these differences across models.

questions.question: A healthcare analytics company runs a customer-facing summarization API on Amazon Bedrock. Traffic occasionally spikes and the team receives throttling errors. The company wants to improve resiliency and capacity headroom without changing its application code or managing capacity reservations. Which Amazon Bedrock feature should the company use?

options.text: Provisioned Throughput with a one-year commitment
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput adds committed capacity but requires a purchase commitment and capacity planning.

options.text: Batch inference with S3 input manifests
options.rationale: Batch inference is asynchronous and unsuitable for a synchronous customer-facing API.

options.text: Custom Model Import of an equivalent open-weights model
options.rationale: Importing a custom model adds work and does not by itself increase on-demand capacity headroom.

options.text: Cross-Region inference (inference profiles)
options.rationale: Cross-Region inference uses an inference profile that lets Bedrock route a request to one of several Regions in a geography, drawing on capacity beyond a single Region. The application keeps the same API call and simply targets the inference profile ID, which reduces throttling during bursts. It requires no capacity purchase.

questions.question: A bank must guarantee a fixed level of model throughput for a trading-desk assistant during market hours and is willing to commit to a term for a lower effective rate. Which Amazon Bedrock purchasing option meets this requirement?

options.text: On-demand token pricing
options.rationale: On-demand charges per token and provides no throughput guarantee.

options.text: Batch inference pricing
options.rationale: Batch inference offers a discount for offline jobs but no committed real-time throughput.

options.text: Provisioned Throughput
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput reserves a set number of model units that deliver a consistent maximum rate of tokens processed, and it can be purchased with a time commitment for a lower effective price. It is the option to choose when predictable, guaranteed throughput matters. On-demand billing, by contrast, is per token with shared capacity.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Marketplace subscription
options.rationale: Bedrock Marketplace expands the catalog of available models; it is not a throughput guarantee.

questions.question: A manufacturing company must classify 4 million archived maintenance reports overnight. Results are consumed by an analytics job the next morning, so no response is needed in real time. Which Amazon Bedrock option is MOST cost-effective?

options.text: Batch inference
options.rationale: Bedrock batch inference processes large sets of prompts asynchronously from Amazon S3 and is offered at a discount compared with on-demand real-time pricing. Because the workload tolerates delayed results, batch is the cheapest fit. Provisioned Throughput would pay for reserved capacity that idles outside the nightly window.

options.text: Provisioned Throughput sized for peak concurrency
options.rationale: Reserved capacity for a once-nightly job wastes money during idle hours.

options.text: On-demand invocation from a large Lambda fan-out
options.rationale: Massive on-demand fan-out pays full per-token rates and risks throttling.

options.text: Prompt caching on a real-time endpoint
options.rationale: Prompt caching reduces cost only for repeated prompt prefixes and does not provide the batch discount.

questions.question: A legal technology company sends the same 20-page contract policy as a static preamble on every request, followed by a short user question. The team wants to lower per-request cost and latency without shortening the preamble. Which Amazon Bedrock feature addresses this?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation
options.rationale: Model Distillation trains a smaller model from a larger teacher; it does not reuse repeated prompt prefixes.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock prompt caching
options.rationale: Prompt caching lets Bedrock reuse the processed representation of a repeated prompt prefix across requests, so the cached portion is billed at a reduced rate and adds less latency. It is designed exactly for long, stable context followed by short variable input. The preamble text itself does not need to change.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Guardrails filter harmful content and topics; they do not reduce token processing cost for repeated context.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Flows
options.rationale: Flows orchestrates steps visually and does not address repeated prompt tokens.

questions.question: A retail company gets good accuracy from a large foundation model but the per-token price and latency are too high for a high-volume product-tagging workload. The company wants a smaller, cheaper model that retains accuracy on this specific task by learning from the larger model's outputs. Which Amazon Bedrock capability should the company use?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput changes how capacity is purchased, not the size or speed of the model.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.rationale: Knowledge Bases add retrieval of company data; they do not shrink the model.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
options.rationale: Model Evaluation measures quality; it does not create a smaller model.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Distillation
options.rationale: Model Distillation uses a large teacher model to generate responses that fine-tune a smaller student model, producing a model that is faster and cheaper to run while preserving accuracy on the targeted use case. This is the standard cost-and-latency lever when a big model is more capable than the workload strictly needs. The tradeoff is that gains are narrow to the distilled task.

questions.question: A public sector research lab has already fine-tuned an open-weights model in its own environment and wants to serve it through the same Amazon Bedrock APIs it uses for other models, without operating inference servers. Which Amazon Bedrock capability supports this?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock playgrounds
options.rationale: Playgrounds are a console for prompt experimentation, not a path to host your own weights.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.rationale: Agents orchestrate tasks with existing models; they do not import model weights.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import
options.rationale: Custom Model Import brings externally trained or customized weights of supported model architectures into Bedrock so they can be invoked through Bedrock's serverless APIs. The lab keeps its own training pipeline while offloading hosting to Bedrock. SageMaker AI would be the alternative if the lab wanted full control of the serving stack.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Data Automation
options.rationale: Bedrock Data Automation extracts insights from unstructured content such as documents, images, audio, and video.

questions.question: An insurance company wants a generative AI assistant that can answer policy questions grounded in the company's PDF policy library stored in Amazon S3, with citations. The team wants a managed retrieval pipeline rather than building embedding and vector search code. Which Amazon Bedrock capability should the company use?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Guardrails apply content and topic policies; they do not retrieve company documents.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
options.rationale: Model Evaluation scores model quality rather than serving grounded answers.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.rationale: Bedrock Knowledge Bases implements Retrieval Augmented Generation as a managed capability: it ingests documents from sources such as S3, chunks and embeds them, stores vectors, and retrieves relevant passages at query time with source attribution. The company avoids writing its own ingestion and retrieval stack. Grounding responses in current documents also reduces hallucination.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management
options.rationale: Prompt Management stores and versions prompts; it does not index documents.

questions.question: A travel company wants a generative AI assistant that can decide which internal APIs to call to look up a booking, change a seat, and issue a refund, chaining several steps to complete a user request. Which Amazon Bedrock capability is designed for this?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
options.rationale: Knowledge Bases retrieve documents for grounding but cannot execute booking changes.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Agents
options.rationale: Bedrock Agents use a foundation model to plan and execute multi-step tasks, invoking action groups that map to your APIs or Lambda functions and optionally consulting a knowledge base. That combination of reasoning plus tool invocation is what distinguishes agents from plain retrieval. Knowledge Bases alone would return text, not perform actions.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock batch inference
options.rationale: Batch inference processes offline prompt sets and has no tool-calling orchestration.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Marketplace
options.rationale: Marketplace broadens the model catalog and does not orchestrate API calls.

questions.question: A marketing team of non-developers needs to build a multi-step generative AI workflow that classifies an inbound request, retrieves related content, and then drafts a reply, all wired together visually and versioned for release. Which Amazon Bedrock capability best fits?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Flows
options.rationale: Bedrock Flows provides a visual builder for linking prompts, knowledge bases, agents, Lambda functions, and conditional logic into an executable workflow, with versions and aliases for release control. It targets teams that want orchestration without writing orchestration code. Playgrounds, by contrast, only test single prompts.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Custom Model Import
options.rationale: Custom Model Import handles bringing your own model weights into Bedrock.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput is a capacity purchase option, not a workflow builder.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock playgrounds
options.rationale: Playgrounds support single-prompt experimentation, not multi-step workflows.

questions.question: A children's education platform must block violent and sexual content in both user prompts and model responses, and must prevent the assistant from discussing competitor products. Which Amazon Bedrock capability should the platform configure?

options.text: SageMaker Model Monitor
options.rationale: Model Monitor detects data and model quality drift on SageMaker endpoints.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Bedrock Guardrails apply configurable content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive information redaction, and contextual grounding checks to both inputs and outputs. A denied topic handles the competitor restriction while content filters handle harmful categories. Guardrails can be attached to models, agents, and knowledge bases.

options.text: SageMaker Clarify
options.rationale: Clarify measures bias and explains feature importance; it does not filter generated content at runtime.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
options.rationale: Model Evaluation scores model quality offline rather than enforcing runtime policy.
