options.rationale: Custom Model Import brings your own model weights into Bedrock; it is not a safety control.

options.text: Prompt caching
options.rationale: Prompt caching reduces latency and cost for repeated prompt prefixes, not content risk.

questions.question: An insurance company runs a generative assistant that answers policy questions from an internal document store. Compliance requires that the assistant refuse to answer when its response is not supported by the retrieved documents. Which Amazon Bedrock Guardrails capability meets this requirement?

options.text: Word filters
options.rationale: Word filters block specific words and phrases such as profanity or competitor names.

options.text: Contextual grounding checks
options.rationale: Contextual grounding checks evaluate whether a model response is factually grounded in the supplied source passages and whether it is relevant to the user query, filtering responses that fall below configured thresholds. This is the guardrail feature aimed specifically at hallucination in RAG applications. The other filters target profanity, subject matter, and sensitive data.

options.text: Denied topics
options.rationale: Denied topics refuse whole subject areas regardless of whether sources support the answer.

options.text: Sensitive information filters
options.rationale: Sensitive information filters detect and mask PII, which is a different concern.

questions.question: A logistics company deploys a document classification model and wants low-confidence predictions routed to human reviewers before any action is taken. Which AWS service provides this workflow?

options.text: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I)
options.rationale: Amazon Augmented AI (A2I) inserts human review into machine learning workflows, triggering review tasks when confidence falls below a threshold or on a sampled basis. Ground Truth labels datasets for training, Model Monitor watches for drift, and Audit Manager collects compliance evidence.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor
options.rationale: Model Monitor reports data and quality drift on endpoints; it does not route items to reviewers.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
options.rationale: Ground Truth builds labeled training datasets, which happens before deployment.

options.text: AWS Audit Manager
options.rationale: Audit Manager automates evidence collection for audits, unrelated to per-prediction review.

questions.question: A model trained to detect defects performs well on the manufacturer's own factory images but fails badly on images from a newly acquired plant with different lighting. Which responsible AI dimension is most clearly lacking?

options.text: Governance
options.rationale: Governance concerns oversight policies and accountability structures, not generalization.

options.text: Robustness
options.rationale: Robustness is the ability of a system to maintain reliable performance when inputs differ from training conditions, including noisy, shifted, or adversarial data. Failing on a new plant's lighting is a robustness and generalization gap, typically addressed with more diverse training data and augmentation.

options.text: Transparency
options.rationale: Transparency concerns disclosing where and how AI is used to stakeholders.

options.text: Privacy and security
options.rationale: Privacy and security concern protecting data and models from exposure.

questions.question: A retailer's training set for a facial analysis feature contains images that heavily over-represent one skin tone. Which mitigation most directly addresses the root cause?

options.text: Increase the model's learning rate during training
options.rationale: Learning rate affects optimization speed and stability, not dataset representativeness.

options.text: Collect additional representative data and balance the dataset across groups
options.rationale: Unbalanced representation is a data problem, so the durable fix is curating a more inclusive and diverse dataset, supplemented where appropriate by data augmentation or re-weighting. Adjusting hyperparameters, thresholds, or instance sizes does not add the missing information about under-represented groups.

options.text: Raise the inference confidence threshold for all predictions
options.rationale: A higher threshold suppresses low-confidence outputs but leaves the underlying disparity intact.

options.text: Deploy the model to a larger instance type
options.rationale: Instance size affects throughput and cost, never fairness.

questions.question: A team needs to explain which input features contributed most to an individual credit-scoring prediction so an adverse action notice can be issued. Which SageMaker Clarify capability provides this?

options.text: Class imbalance metric
options.rationale: Class imbalance measures how unevenly a facet is represented in the dataset.

options.text: SHAP-based feature attribution
options.rationale: SageMaker Clarify uses SHAP values to attribute a prediction to individual input features, supporting both global explanations across a dataset and local explanations for a single record. Class imbalance and difference in proportions of labels are bias metrics that describe dataset composition, not per-prediction attribution.

options.text: Difference in proportions of labels
options.rationale: Difference in proportions of labels compares positive outcome rates across groups, not feature influence.

options.text: Data quality baseline
options.rationale: A data quality baseline captures statistics used to detect drift later.

questions.question: A media company plans to use a generative model to produce marketing images. Legal raises intellectual property concerns. Which two practices reduce this risk? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Review the model provider's terms regarding training data and output ownership
options.rationale: Intellectual property risk in generative AI is managed through contractual and procedural controls: understanding the provider's licensing and indemnification terms, and inserting human review to catch outputs that resemble protected works. Sampling parameters, Region choice, and throughput settings have no bearing on IP exposure.

options.text: Add human review of generated assets before publication
options.rationale: Intellectual property risk in generative AI is managed through contractual and procedural controls: understanding the provider's licensing and indemnification terms, and inserting human review to catch outputs that resemble protected works. Sampling parameters, Region choice, and throughput settings have no bearing on IP exposure.

options.text: Increase the temperature parameter to produce more original outputs
options.rationale: Temperature changes randomness of sampling; it does not establish that output is legally clear.

options.text: Store all generated images in a separate AWS Region
options.rationale: Region selection affects data residency and latency, not copyright status.

options.text: Enable Provisioned Throughput for the image model
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity and carries no legal effect.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the relationship between bias and variance in a machine learning model?

options.text: High bias means the model memorizes training data; high variance means it oversimplifies
options.rationale: This reverses the definitions; memorizing training data is high variance.

options.text: High bias means the model oversimplifies and underfits; high variance means it is overly sensitive to training data and overfits
options.rationale: In the statistical sense, high bias means the model makes strong simplifying assumptions and underfits, missing real patterns. High variance means the model fits noise in the training set and fails to generalize, which is overfitting. Increasing complexity typically lowers bias while raising variance, which is the classic tradeoff.

options.text: Bias and variance both increase together as model complexity increases
options.rationale: They generally move in opposite directions as complexity changes, which is why it is a tradeoff.

options.text: Bias applies only to generative models and variance only to classification models
options.rationale: Both concepts apply across model families and tasks.

questions.question: A public sector agency must apply the same content safety policy to a model it hosts outside Amazon Bedrock as well as to its Bedrock models. Which approach allows a single guardrail configuration to be reused?

options.text: Attach the guardrail to a Bedrock Knowledge Base
options.rationale: Attaching to a Knowledge Base covers Bedrock retrieval flows, not an externally hosted model.

options.text: Call the independent ApplyGuardrail API to evaluate text from any source
options.rationale: The ApplyGuardrail API evaluates arbitrary text against a configured guardrail independently of a model invocation, so the same policy can protect self-hosted models, third-party models, or application text. Attaching a guardrail to a Bedrock invocation only covers that path.

options.text: Enable Bedrock Model Evaluation on the external model
options.rationale: Model Evaluation scores model quality; it does not enforce runtime content policy.

options.text: Configure the guardrail as a SageMaker Model Monitor schedule
options.rationale: Model Monitor tracks drift and quality metrics on SageMaker endpoints, not content safety policy.

questions.question: A company discovers that its deployed fraud model has quietly degraded because spending patterns shifted after a holiday season. Which governance practice would have surfaced this earliest?

options.text: Continuous monitoring of model quality and data drift in production
options.rationale: Model behavior changes as the world changes, so responsible operation requires ongoing monitoring of input distributions and prediction quality with alerting and retraining triggers. A pre-launch audit is a point-in-time snapshot and cannot detect post-deployment drift.

options.text: A one-time fairness audit performed before launch
options.rationale: A launch-time audit says nothing about behavior months later once data has shifted.

options.text: Increasing the size of the training dataset
options.rationale: More training data may help accuracy but does not detect a later distribution shift.

options.text: Publishing an AI Service Card for the model
options.rationale: Service cards document intended use and limitations; they are not a monitoring control.

questions.question: Which dataset characteristic most directly supports fairness in a model used across many countries?

options.text: A dataset stored in a single AWS Region for consistency
options.rationale: Region choice concerns residency and latency, not who is represented in the data.

options.text: A dataset that is inclusive and diverse, representing the populations the model will serve
options.rationale: Fairness depends on whether the training data represents the people the system will affect. Inclusive, diverse, and balanced datasets reduce the chance that a group is systematically mispredicted. Storage location, compression, and synthetic-only sourcing do not by themselves ensure representativeness.

options.text: A dataset compressed to reduce storage cost
options.rationale: Compression is a storage optimization with no effect on data composition.

options.text: A dataset consisting entirely of synthetic records
options.rationale: Purely synthetic data can still encode the biases of the process that generated it.

questions.question: An organization is defining consequences it must guard against from a poorly governed generative AI deployment. Which two are realistic business impacts? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Regulatory penalties and legal exposure from discriminatory or non-compliant outputs
options.rationale: Weak governance exposes an organization to legal and regulatory consequences when outputs are discriminatory, non-compliant, or unsafe, and to reputational harm when customers encounter toxic or fabricated content. The remaining options describe unrelated cost effects, an impossible guarantee, and a consequence AWS does not impose.

options.text: Reputational damage from toxic or fabricated content reaching customers
options.rationale: Weak governance exposes an organization to legal and regulatory consequences when outputs are discriminatory, non-compliant, or unsafe, and to reputational harm when customers encounter toxic or fabricated content. The remaining options describe unrelated cost effects, an impossible guarantee, and a consequence AWS does not impose.

options.text: Automatic reduction of Amazon S3 storage costs
options.rationale: Governance practices do not change storage pricing.

options.text: Guaranteed elimination of all model hallucinations
options.rationale: No governance program eliminates hallucination entirely; it reduces and detects it.

options.text: Permanent loss of access to foundation models in the AWS Region
options.rationale: AWS does not revoke Regional model access as a penalty for governance gaps.

questions.question: A sustainability team asks how the company can reduce the environmental footprint of its machine learning workloads. Which action is most aligned with that goal?

options.text: Train every model from scratch to maximize control
options.rationale: Training from scratch is the most compute and energy intensive option available.

options.text: Start from a pre-trained foundation model and fine-tune only when required
options.rationale: Reusing a pre-trained model and customizing it, or using prompt engineering and retrieval before considering training, avoids the very large compute cost of pre-training. Purpose-built accelerators such as AWS Trainium and right-sized jobs further reduce energy use, whereas training from scratch and extra epochs increase it.

options.text: Run all training jobs on general purpose CPU instances
options.rationale: CPUs are typically far less efficient than accelerators for deep learning training workloads.

options.text: Increase the number of training epochs to improve accuracy
options.rationale: More epochs consume more compute and often yield diminishing or negative returns.

questions.question: A support assistant confidently tells a customer about a refund policy that does not exist. What is this failure called, and which mitigation is most directly targeted at it?

options.text: Overfitting, mitigated by adding regularization
options.rationale: Overfitting is a training generalization problem, not fabricated generative content.

options.text: Hallucination, mitigated by grounding responses in retrieved source documents
options.rationale: A hallucination is fluent output that is not supported by any real source. Grounding the model in authoritative content through retrieval augmented generation, and verifying groundedness with contextual grounding checks, is the standard mitigation. The other terms describe different failure modes.

options.text: Data drift, mitigated by retraining on newer data
options.rationale: Data drift describes changing input distributions over time, not invented facts.

options.text: Prompt injection, mitigated by input validation
options.rationale: Prompt injection is an adversarial input attack, not spontaneous fabrication.

questions.question: A lender must show a regulator that its model does not produce a materially different approval rate for a protected group after training. Which SageMaker Clarify measurement addresses this?

options.text: A pre-training class imbalance metric
options.rationale: Class imbalance describes dataset composition, not the model's predicted outcomes.

options.text: A post-training bias metric such as difference in positive proportions in predicted labels
options.rationale: Post-training bias metrics compare model outcomes across groups, for example the difference in positive prediction rates or disparate impact ratio, which is what a regulator asking about approval rates wants. Pre-training metrics describe only the dataset, before the model's behavior exists.

options.text: A partial dependence plot of a single feature
options.rationale: Partial dependence shows how a feature influences predictions on average, not group disparity.

options.text: An endpoint latency percentile report
options.rationale: Latency is an operational metric with no fairness meaning.

questions.question: Which responsible AI dimension is concerned with clearly disclosing to users that they are interacting with an AI system and what its limitations are?

options.text: Transparency
options.rationale: Transparency is about openly communicating how and where AI is used, what data informs it, and what its known limitations are, so people can make informed decisions. Explainability is the related but distinct question of describing how a specific output was produced.

options.text: Controllability
options.rationale: Controllability is the ability to monitor and steer a deployed system's behavior.

options.text: Robustness
options.rationale: Robustness concerns reliable performance under unexpected or adversarial inputs.

options.text: Fairness
options.rationale: Fairness concerns unjustified differences in outcomes across groups.

questions.question: A hiring platform wants to reduce the chance that its resume screening model penalizes candidates who took career breaks. Which combination of steps best reflects responsible practice?

options.text: Remove the model from production and rely only on keyword search
options.rationale: Abandoning the system entirely is rarely required and keyword search has its own bias problems.

options.text: Audit the dataset for representation, measure outcome disparities, and keep a human decision-maker in the loop
options.rationale: Responsible deployment combines data auditing, quantitative fairness measurement on outcomes, and human oversight for consequential decisions. Retraining on the same biased history repeats the problem, and a larger model learns existing patterns more strongly rather than correcting them.

options.text: Retrain the model weekly with the same historical data
options.rationale: Repeating training on unchanged historical data reproduces the same disparities.

options.text: Increase model size so it can learn more nuanced patterns
options.rationale: Model capacity does not correct bias in the underlying data.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of an AWS AI Service Card?

options.text: A billing statement showing per-service AI usage costs
options.rationale: Cost and usage information appears in AWS Billing and Cost Management, not service cards.

options.text: Documentation describing an AWS AI service's intended use cases, limitations, and responsible design choices
options.rationale: AWS AI Service Cards are transparency documents that describe an AWS AI service's intended use cases, how it was designed and tested, and its known limitations and responsible AI considerations. They inform appropriate use; they are not billing artifacts, runtime configuration, or certifications.

options.text: A configuration file that enables content filtering
options.rationale: Content filtering is configured in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, not in a service card.

options.text: A certificate proving a model passed a fairness audit
options.rationale: A service card documents design and limitations; it does not certify audit results.

questions.question: A company is designing human oversight for a generative AI system that drafts customer emails. Which two design choices strengthen controllability? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Logging every prompt and response for later review
options.rationale: Controllability means the operator can observe and steer the system. Comprehensive invocation logging provides the observability, and a human approval gate before an irreversible action provides the control. The other options remove visibility, widen blast radius, and remove safety enforcement.

options.text: Requiring human approval before any drafted email is sent
options.rationale: Controllability means the operator can observe and steer the system. Comprehensive invocation logging provides the observability, and a human approval gate before an irreversible action provides the control. The other options remove visibility, widen blast radius, and remove safety enforcement.

options.text: Removing all logging to reduce storage costs
options.rationale: Removing logging eliminates the ability to audit or investigate model behavior.

options.text: Allowing the model unrestricted access to internal APIs
options.rationale: Unrestricted tool access increases the impact of a mistake or an injection attack.

options.text: Disabling all guardrails to avoid blocking legitimate drafts
options.rationale: Disabling guardrails removes the enforcement layer that keeps outputs within policy.

questions.question: An engineering team wants automated verification that a model's answers about company policy are logically consistent with a formal specification of that policy. Which Amazon Bedrock Guardrails capability targets this?

options.text: Content filters
options.rationale: Content filters score harmful categories such as hate and violence, not logical consistency.

options.text: Automated Reasoning checks
options.rationale: Automated Reasoning checks in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails use formal, logic-based verification against an encoded policy model to determine whether a response is consistent with defined rules, which addresses factual and policy correctness rather than harmful content. Content filters, word filters, and denied topics screen for harm, specific terms, and subject matter.

options.text: Word filters
options.rationale: Word filters match specific words and phrases; they perform no reasoning.

options.text: Denied topics
options.rationale: Denied topics block subject areas entirely rather than verifying correctness.

questions.question: A team must decide when human review is most warranted in an AI workflow. Which situation makes human-in-the-loop review most important?

options.text: A model that suggests background colors for a marketing slide
options.rationale: A color suggestion is trivially reversible and carries no material consequence.

options.text: A model that recommends whether to deny a medical claim
options.rationale: Human review is prioritized where errors carry high consequence for individuals, such as medical, financial, legal, or employment decisions. Low-stakes, easily reversible outputs like styling suggestions or search autocomplete do not justify the same cost and latency of review.

options.text: A model that autocompletes internal search queries
options.rationale: An incorrect query suggestion is immediately visible and costless to ignore.

options.text: A model that tags photos with generic scene labels
options.rationale: Generic scene tags are low impact and easily corrected.

questions.question: Which responsible AI dimension focuses on protecting training data and model artifacts from unauthorized access or exposure?

options.text: Veracity
options.rationale: Veracity is about outputs being truthful and accurate.

options.text: Privacy and security
options.rationale: Privacy and security covers protecting data used to build and operate AI systems, preventing leakage of sensitive information through model outputs, and controlling access to models and endpoints. Veracity concerns truthfulness, explainability concerns describing decisions, and fairness concerns outcome equity.

options.text: Explainability
options.rationale: Explainability is about describing how the model reached an output.

options.text: Fairness
options.rationale: Fairness is about equitable outcomes across groups.

questions.question: A team is establishing a responsible AI review for a new generative feature. Place the following activities in the order they should occur.

options.text: 1. Continuously monitor production outputs and feed issues back into the review → 2. Configure guardrails and human review gates before launch → 3. Audit the data sources for representation, licensing, and sensitive content → 4. Define the intended use, affected users, and unacceptable outcomes
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Define the intended use, affected users, and unacceptable outcomes → 2. Audit the data sources for representation, licensing, and sensitive content → 3. Configure guardrails and human review gates before launch → 4. Continuously monitor production outputs and feed issues back into the review
options.rationale: Responsible AI work starts by defining intended use and the harms to avoid, since that determines what to measure. Data auditing follows, then technical and procedural safeguards are configured before launch, and finally production monitoring closes the loop by feeding real behavior back into the review.

options.text: 1. Audit the data sources for representation, licensing, and sensitive content → 2. Configure guardrails and human review gates before launch → 3. Continuously monitor production outputs and feed issues back into the review → 4. Define the intended use, affected users, and unacceptable outcomes
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

options.text: 1. Audit the data sources for representation, licensing, and sensitive content → 2. Define the intended use, affected users, and unacceptable outcomes → 3. Configure guardrails and human review gates before launch → 4. Continuously monitor production outputs and feed issues back into the review
options.rationale: That is not the correct order for these steps.

questions.question: A generative assistant occasionally produces insulting language when users are hostile. Which control most directly reduces this without retraining the model?

options.text: Configuring content filters for the insults category in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Guardrails content filters score both prompts and responses across harmful categories including insults, and can block or mask content at configurable strength levels, all without changing the model. Token limits, capacity mode, and caching affect length, cost, and latency instead.

options.text: Reducing the max tokens setting
options.rationale: Fewer tokens produce shorter output but do not make it less toxic.

options.text: Switching the endpoint to Provisioned Throughput
options.rationale: Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity and applies no content policy.

options.text: Enabling prompt caching
options.rationale: Prompt caching reuses computed prompt prefixes to cut latency and cost.

questions.question: Two candidate models perform similarly on overall accuracy, but one shows a much larger accuracy gap between demographic groups. Which decision best reflects responsible AI practice?

options.text: Choose the model with the smaller group gap, accepting equal overall accuracy
options.rationale: Aggregate accuracy can conceal that a model performs much worse for some groups. When overall performance is comparable, the model with more consistent performance across groups is the responsible choice. Averaging predictions to obscure a measured disparity conceals rather than fixes the problem.

options.text: Choose either model since overall accuracy is the same
options.rationale: Equal aggregate accuracy does not mean equal treatment; the disparity is a real harm.

options.text: Choose the model with the larger gap if it trains faster
options.rationale: Training speed is an engineering convenience and does not outweigh a fairness gap.

options.text: Combine both models and average their predictions to hide the gap
options.rationale: Ensembling to mask a disparity is a transparency failure and may not remove the gap.

questions.question: A company wants to reduce the chance that its fine-tuning dataset causes the model to reveal customer names in later responses. Which practice addresses this best?

options.text: Increasing the number of fine-tuning epochs
options.rationale: More epochs increase the chance the model memorizes specific training examples.

options.text: Removing or redacting personally identifiable information from the training data before fine-tuning
options.rationale: Models can memorize and later emit distinctive strings from their training data, so sensitive values should be removed or redacted before fine-tuning. Amazon Macie can help discover sensitive data at scale. More epochs actually increase memorization risk, and streaming or model size do not affect what was learned.

options.text: Enabling streaming responses on the endpoint
options.rationale: Streaming changes how tokens are delivered, not what the model learned.

options.text: Choosing a larger base model
options.rationale: A larger base model does not remove sensitive data that was in the fine-tuning set.

questions.question: Which responsible AI dimension is most concerned with whether a system's outputs are truthful and accurate?

options.text: Governance
options.rationale: Governance concerns policies, roles, and accountability.

options.text: Veracity
options.rationale: Veracity, often paired with robustness, is the dimension concerned with outputs being truthful, accurate, and reliable, which makes hallucination a veracity failure. Governance is oversight structure, controllability is operational steering, and transparency is disclosure.

options.text: Controllability
options.rationale: Controllability is the ability to monitor and constrain deployed behavior.

options.text: Transparency
options.rationale: Transparency concerns disclosing how and where AI is used.

questions.question: A retail company is preparing training data for a recommendation model and wants to reduce the risk of biased outcomes. Which two data practices are most relevant? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Verify that the dataset covers the full range of customer segments the model will serve
options.rationale: Fair outcomes depend on representative coverage of the populations served and on knowing where data came from, since provenance reveals collection biases and licensing constraints. Archival storage class, type conversion, and duplicating the majority class are irrelevant or actively worsen imbalance.

options.text: Document the provenance and collection method of each data source
options.rationale: Fair outcomes depend on representative coverage of the populations served and on knowing where data came from, since provenance reveals collection biases and licensing constraints. Archival storage class, type conversion, and duplicating the majority class are irrelevant or actively worsen imbalance.

options.text: Store the dataset in Amazon S3 Glacier to reduce cost
options.rationale: Storage class affects retrieval time and cost, not data fairness.

options.text: Convert all numeric features to strings before training
options.rationale: Changing feature types is a preprocessing detail unrelated to bias.

options.text: Duplicate the majority-class records to increase dataset size
options.rationale: Duplicating majority records worsens class imbalance rather than reducing it.

questions.question: During red-team testing, a user convinces a customer service assistant to ignore its instructions and reveal its system prompt. Which responsible AI concern does this illustrate?

options.text: Model drift
options.rationale: Drift is a gradual change in data distribution over time, not an adversarial prompt.

options.text: Safety and security weakness from prompt injection
options.rationale: Persuading a model to disregard its instructions is prompt injection or jailbreaking, a safety and security weakness. Mitigations include input validation, clear delimiting of untrusted content, guardrails, and never placing secrets in the system prompt. The other options describe unrelated statistical or data issues.

options.text: Underfitting
options.rationale: Underfitting is a training capacity problem, unrelated to instruction bypass.

options.text: Class imbalance
options.rationale: Class imbalance describes uneven label distribution in a dataset.

questions.question: A team argues that because their model is highly accurate, no fairness evaluation is needed. What is the strongest counterargument?

options.text: Accuracy always decreases when fairness is measured
options.rationale: Measuring fairness does not by itself change accuracy; it reveals how accuracy is distributed.

options.text: High aggregate accuracy can coexist with poor performance for a minority subgroup
options.rationale: An aggregate metric is dominated by the largest groups, so a model can be highly accurate overall while performing badly for a small but important subgroup. Disaggregated evaluation across groups is what reveals this, which is why fairness assessment is separate from headline accuracy.

options.text: Fairness evaluation is required by AWS before deploying any model
options.rationale: AWS does not impose a mandatory fairness evaluation gate on customer deployments.

options.text: Accuracy is not a valid metric for classification problems
options.rationale: Accuracy is a valid classification metric, though incomplete on imbalanced data.

questions.question: A company wants a record of a model's intended use, training approach, evaluation results, and known limitations, maintained alongside the model itself for internal governance. Which SageMaker AI feature is purpose-built for this?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
options.rationale: SageMaker Model Cards capture model documentation including intended use, training details, evaluation results, and limitations in a single governed artifact tied to the model. Feature Store manages features, Experiments tracks training runs, and Data Wrangler prepares data.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
options.rationale: Feature Store stores and serves engineered features for training and inference.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Experiments
options.rationale: Experiments organizes and compares training runs and their metrics.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Data Wrangler
options.rationale: Data Wrangler is a data preparation and transformation tool.

questions.question: Which statement about data augmentation as a bias mitigation technique is most accurate?

options.text: It eliminates the need to examine the original dataset
options.rationale: Examining the original data is what tells you which groups are under-represented in the first place.

options.text: It can increase the representation of under-represented groups but does not substitute for collecting genuinely diverse data
options.rationale: Augmentation generates additional variations of existing examples, which can help balance a dataset and improve robustness, but it amplifies the information already present rather than adding genuinely new coverage. It is a useful supplement to, not a replacement for, representative data collection.

options.text: It works only for tabular datasets
options.rationale: Augmentation is widely used for images, audio, and text as well as tabular data.

options.text: It guarantees equal model accuracy across all groups
options.rationale: No technique guarantees equal accuracy across groups; outcomes must still be measured.

questions.question: A generative AI feature is being launched in a regulated industry. Which practice best supports the safety dimension of responsible AI?

options.text: Testing the system against adversarial and edge-case prompts before release
options.rationale: Safety is supported by deliberately probing the system with adversarial, harmful, and edge-case inputs before release so failure modes are found internally rather than by customers. Model size, context window, and multi-Region deployment address capability and availability, not safety behavior.

options.text: Selecting the largest available foundation model
options.rationale: A larger model is not inherently safer and may produce more convincing unsafe output.

options.text: Increasing the context window size
options.rationale: Context window affects how much input the model can consider, not output safety.

options.text: Deploying to multiple AWS Regions
options.rationale: Multi-Region deployment improves availability and latency, not content safety.

questions.question: Which scenario best illustrates a need for the fairness dimension rather than the explainability dimension?

options.text: A clinician asks which symptoms drove a specific diagnosis suggestion
options.rationale: Asking which inputs drove one prediction is an explainability question.

options.text: An auditor finds the model approves one gender at a significantly lower rate
options.rationale: Fairness concerns whether outcomes differ unjustifiably across groups, which is exactly what a disparity in approval rates by gender represents. The other scenarios ask how a particular output was produced or where it came from, which are explainability and transparency questions.

options.text: A developer wants to know which layer of a neural network activated most
options.rationale: Inspecting internal activations is a model interpretability and debugging concern.

options.text: A user asks the assistant to cite the document its answer came from
options.rationale: Requesting a source citation is about grounding and transparency of an individual answer.

questions.question: A public sector agency is reviewing a machine learning model that screens benefits applications. The review board describes the model as a black box. What does this description mean?

options.text: The model was trained on data that the agency is not allowed to store.
options.rationale: Data retention restrictions are a privacy and governance concern, not a definition of opacity.

options.text: The internal logic that maps an input to a prediction cannot be readily inspected or described by a human reviewer.
options.rationale: A black box (opaque) model is one whose internal decision process is not directly interpretable, which is typical of deep neural networks and large ensembles. Transparency is about being able to understand and describe how inputs lead to outputs, not about network isolation or data residency. Opaque models can still be explained after the fact with techniques such as feature attribution.

options.text: The model is deployed in a private subnet with no internet connectivity.
options.rationale: Network placement is an infrastructure control and has nothing to do with model interpretability.

options.text: The model returns a different prediction each time it receives the same input.
options.rationale: Nondeterminism is a separate property; most black-box classifiers are deterministic at inference time.

questions.question: A finance company must tell each declined applicant which input factors most influenced the credit decision made by its Amazon SageMaker AI model. Which capability meets this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor data quality monitoring
options.rationale: Model Monitor detects drift and data quality problems in production; it does not attribute a prediction to input features.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
options.rationale: Feature Store stores and serves features for training and inference; it produces no explanations.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Clarify feature attribution explanations based on SHAP values
options.rationale: SageMaker Clarify computes SHAP feature attributions that quantify how much each input feature contributed to a prediction, both globally and for individual records. That is exactly what an adverse action notice or a customer explanation requires. The other services address data drift, feature reuse, and generative AI content filtering rather than explaining a prediction.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails content filters
options.rationale: Guardrails filters harmful content in generative AI applications and does not explain a tabular model prediction.

questions.question: A media company plans to adopt an AWS managed AI service and needs published information about the service's intended use cases, design choices, and known limitations before approving it. Which resource should the company consult?

options.text: AWS AI Service Cards
options.rationale: AWS AI Service Cards are responsible AI documentation published by AWS for its AI services and Amazon models. They describe intended use cases, limitations, responsible AI design considerations, and performance optimization guidance. Model Cards, by contrast, are artifacts the customer creates to document their own models.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
options.rationale: Model Cards document a customer's own trained models, not an AWS managed service.

options.text: AWS Trusted Advisor checks
options.rationale: Trusted Advisor gives cost, performance, and security recommendations for AWS accounts.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard
options.rationale: Model Dashboard monitors a customer's deployed models and endpoints.

questions.question: A healthcare organization needs a single governance artifact per model that records the model's intended use, training data description, evaluation results, risk rating, and approved caveats so internal auditors can review it. Which AWS capability should the organization use?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
options.rationale: Feature Store centralizes features for training and inference, not model documentation.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
options.rationale: Ground Truth creates labeled training datasets.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Canvas
options.rationale: Canvas is a no-code environment for building models, not a documentation registry.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
options.rationale: SageMaker Model Cards create a versioned, centralized record of a model's purpose, training details, evaluation metrics, risk rating, and intended and unintended uses. Auditors can use that documentation to review how a model was built and where it should not be applied. The other options support feature management, data labeling, and no-code model building.

questions.question: An ML platform team at a logistics company manages dozens of models across several accounts. Leadership wants one place to see all deployed models, their monitoring alert status, and any missing monitors. Which SageMaker capability provides this view?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard
options.rationale: SageMaker Model Dashboard is a unified view of all models in an account, showing endpoint status, Model Monitor alert history, links to model cards and lineage, and which models lack monitoring. It supports transparency at the fleet level rather than for a single prediction. JumpStart, Clarify, and Autopilot serve model discovery, explainability analysis, and automated model building.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
options.rationale: JumpStart is a hub of pretrained models and solution templates, not an oversight dashboard.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Clarify
options.rationale: Clarify explains individual models and detects bias; it does not aggregate fleet status.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
options.rationale: Autopilot builds models automatically from tabular data; it is not a monitoring view.

questions.question: A bank must deploy a loan approval model in a jurisdiction where regulators require that every automated decision be fully traceable to explicit, human-readable rules on input variables. Model accuracy differences among candidates are small. Which model choice BEST satisfies the regulator?

options.text: A gradient-boosted tree ensemble with 2,000 trees plus post hoc SHAP explanations
options.rationale: SHAP on a large ensemble is a post hoc approximation, not exact human-readable decision logic.

options.text: A deep neural network with an attention visualization layer
options.rationale: Attention maps offer partial insight but the network remains opaque.

options.text: A logistic regression model with a small set of well-understood features
options.rationale: When regulators demand full traceability, an intrinsically interpretable model such as logistic regression is the right choice because its coefficients directly show how each feature moves the decision. Post hoc explanations of complex models are approximations and may not satisfy a requirement for exact, human-readable logic. Since the accuracy gap is small, the interpretability benefit dominates.

options.text: A fine-tuned foundation model accessed through Amazon Bedrock
options.rationale: A foundation model is the least transparent option for a regulated tabular decision.

questions.question: A retail analytics team is choosing between a deep neural network and a decision tree for a customer churn model. In which circumstances should the team prefer the simpler decision tree? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Business stakeholders must be able to follow the exact decision path for any customer.
options.rationale: Simple models such as decision trees are preferred when stakeholders and reviewers must directly follow and verify the decision logic. A tree's splits can be read as if-then rules without extra tooling. Deep networks are the better fit for unstructured data such as images or raw text, or when squeezing out maximum accuracy outweighs interpretability.

options.text: The input data consists of millions of unstructured product images.
options.rationale: Image data at scale favors deep learning, which learns visual features automatically.

options.text: The team must maximize predictive accuracy regardless of any other consideration.
options.rationale: Prioritizing accuracy above all typically favors more complex models, not simpler ones.

options.text: Compliance reviewers require the model logic to be verifiable without specialized tooling.
options.rationale: Simple models such as decision trees are preferred when stakeholders and reviewers must directly follow and verify the decision logic. A tree's splits can be read as if-then rules without extra tooling. Deep networks are the better fit for unstructured data such as images or raw text, or when squeezing out maximum accuracy outweighs interpretability.

options.text: The team wants the model to learn feature representations automatically from raw text.
options.rationale: Automatic representation learning from raw text is a strength of neural networks, not trees.

questions.question: An insurance company's data science lead states that the fraud model is explainable but not interpretable. Which statement is consistent with that claim?

options.text: Anyone can read the model parameters and directly understand the decision rules.
options.rationale: Directly readable decision rules describe an interpretable model, which contradicts the claim.

options.text: The model cannot be understood by inspection, but post hoc techniques can describe why it produced a given output.
options.rationale: Interpretability refers to understanding a model's internal mechanics directly, which is a property of simple models like linear regression or small trees. Explainability refers to describing model behavior, often with post hoc methods such as SHAP or LIME, even when the internals remain opaque. A complex model can therefore be explainable without being interpretable.

options.text: The model publishes its full training dataset for external review.
options.rationale: Publishing training data relates to data transparency, not to interpretability of model internals.

options.text: The model is small enough to be retrained on a laptop.
options.rationale: Model size and retraining cost do not define interpretability.

questions.question: Which statement BEST describes the tradeoff a team commonly faces between model interpretability and model performance?

options.text: Interpretable models always outperform complex models on structured data.
options.rationale: Simple models sometimes match complex ones, but they do not always outperform them.

options.text: Highly complex models often achieve higher accuracy on difficult tasks but are harder for humans to understand.
options.rationale: There is a well-known tension: models with many parameters, such as deep neural networks and large ensembles, can capture complex patterns and often achieve higher accuracy, but their reasoning is opaque. Simple models such as linear regression trade some predictive power for direct human understanding. The tradeoff is a tendency, not an absolute law, which is why teams should evaluate both.

options.text: Complex models are always required whenever the training dataset is large.
options.rationale: Large datasets do not mandate complex models; the task and requirements drive the choice.

options.text: Interpretability and accuracy are independent, so the choice of model family never affects either.
options.rationale: Model family strongly influences both interpretability and achievable accuracy.

questions.question: A hospital deploys an AI triage assistant. Designers ensure the interface shows the top contributing symptoms for each recommendation, lets clinicians override the suggestion, and records the override. Which design philosophy do these choices reflect?

options.text: Retrieval Augmented Generation
options.rationale: RAG grounds generative model answers in retrieved documents; it is not a user-experience philosophy.

options.text: Human-centered design for explainable AI
options.rationale: Human-centered design for explainable AI builds systems around the needs of the people using them: explanations are presented in context, humans keep decision authority, and actions are reversible and auditable. Showing contributing factors, enabling overrides, and logging them are hallmark practices. The other options are model training or architecture techniques, not design philosophies.

options.text: Continued pre-training
options.rationale: Continued pre-training extends a foundation model on domain data.

options.text: Federated learning
options.rationale: Federated learning trains across decentralized data without moving it.

questions.question: A gaming company's ops dashboard uses an ML model to flag suspicious accounts. Analysts complain that each alert shows 40 raw feature values, forcing them to dig through data before acting. Designers redesign the alert to show only the three most influential factors with plain-language labels. Which human-centered design principle does the redesign apply?

options.text: Reducing cognitive load on the human decision maker
options.rationale: Minimizing cognitive load means presenting explanations at the level of detail a human can absorb quickly, surfacing the most decision-relevant information instead of overwhelming users with raw data. Showing the top contributing factors in plain language is a classic application. Reversibility concerns undoing actions, and amplified decision making is about augmenting human judgment, not dumping all data.

options.text: Designing for reversibility of automated actions
options.rationale: Reversibility is about making it easy to undo decisions, which this change does not address.

options.text: Amplified decision making through full data disclosure
options.rationale: Amplified decision making augments human judgment; disclosing every raw value works against usability.

options.text: Increasing model temperature to diversify outputs
options.rationale: Temperature is a generative inference parameter unrelated to interface design.

questions.question: A manufacturing company rolls out an AI system that automatically reroutes factory work orders. The design team insists that any automated rerouting can be undone with a single action and that the system keeps the prior state available. Which principle of human-centered design for explainable AI is being applied?

options.text: Cognitive load minimization
options.rationale: Cognitive load concerns how much mental effort the interface demands, not undo capability.

options.text: Decision theory optimization
options.rationale: Decision theory guides structuring choices under uncertainty rather than rollback design.

options.text: Design for reversibility
options.rationale: Design for reversibility means users can undo or roll back consequences of AI-driven actions, which builds trust and limits the damage from wrong predictions. Preserving prior state and offering a one-step undo are direct implementations. Cognitive load is about information presentation, and decision theory informs how choices are structured, not how they are undone.

options.text: Data augmentation
options.rationale: Data augmentation is a training technique for expanding datasets.

questions.question: A regulator requires a lender to state the specific reasons an applicant was declined. The data science team currently uses a deep neural network with the highest accuracy. What is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Keep the neural network and explain that deep models cannot be interpreted
options.rationale: Declaring the model uninterpretable does not satisfy a legal obligation to give reasons.

options.text: Evaluate whether a more interpretable model such as logistic regression or a decision tree meets the accuracy requirement, or add feature attribution to explain individual decisions
options.rationale: When regulation demands per-decision reasons, either adopt an inherently interpretable model or add post-hoc explanation such as SHAP feature attribution through SageMaker Clarify. Interpretable models often perform comparably on tabular data, so the accuracy tradeoff should be measured rather than assumed.

options.text: Increase the number of layers so the model captures the reasons more precisely
options.rationale: Adding layers increases opacity and does nothing to produce human-readable reasons.

options.text: Publish the model weights so the regulator can inspect them directly
options.rationale: Raw weights are not a human-understandable explanation of an individual decision.

questions.question: Which pair of models is generally considered the most transparent and easiest to interpret?

options.text: Deep convolutional neural networks and transformers
options.rationale: Deep networks and transformers have millions of parameters with no directly readable decision logic.

options.text: Linear regression and decision trees
options.rationale: Linear and logistic regression expose coefficients that map directly to feature influence, and shallow decision trees expose an explicit rule path. These are inherently interpretable, unlike deep networks, generative models, and large language models, which require post-hoc explanation techniques.

options.text: Generative adversarial networks and diffusion models
options.rationale: Generative adversarial and diffusion models are highly opaque generative architectures.

options.text: Large language models and mixture-of-experts models
options.rationale: Large language models are the canonical example of black box behavior.

questions.question: A governance team wants documented transparency artifacts for both an AWS managed AI service and a custom model the company trained. Which two artifacts should they use? (Select TWO.)

options.text: An AWS AI Service Card for the managed AWS AI service
options.rationale: AWS AI Service Cards document AWS managed AI services, covering intended use, design, and limitations. SageMaker Model Cards document your own models with intended use, training details, evaluation, and limitations. Dashboards, cost reports, and bucket policies serve operations, finance, and access control instead.

options.text: An Amazon SageMaker Model Card for the custom trained model
options.rationale: AWS AI Service Cards document AWS managed AI services, covering intended use, design, and limitations. SageMaker Model Cards document your own models with intended use, training details, evaluation, and limitations. Dashboards, cost reports, and bucket policies serve operations, finance, and access control instead.

options.text: An Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for the managed service
options.rationale: A CloudWatch dashboard shows operational metrics, not model documentation.

options.text: An AWS Cost and Usage Report for the custom model
options.rationale: Cost reports describe spend, not model behavior or limitations.

options.text: An Amazon S3 bucket policy for the training data
options.rationale: A bucket policy controls access to data and documents nothing about the model.

questions.question: A company needs a single place to view all its models, their current status, and monitoring results across the organization. Which SageMaker AI capability provides this?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Dashboard
options.rationale: SageMaker Model Dashboard gives a centralized view of models, endpoints, and their monitoring and compliance status across an account, which supports governance oversight. Ground Truth labels data, Autopilot builds models automatically, and Canvas offers a no-code modeling interface.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
options.rationale: Ground Truth creates labeled training datasets.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
options.rationale: Autopilot automatically trains and tunes candidate models.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Canvas
options.rationale: Canvas provides a visual, no-code interface for building models.

questions.question: Which statement best captures the difference between interpretability and explainability?

options.text: They are synonyms used interchangeably in AWS documentation
options.rationale: They are related but distinct concepts, and the exam tests the distinction.

options.text: Interpretability is the degree to which a human can inherently understand the model's internal mechanics; explainability is the ability to describe why a particular output occurred, often using post-hoc techniques
options.rationale: Interpretability is an intrinsic property of the model: a shallow decision tree is interpretable because a person can follow its logic directly. Explainability is the ability to produce an understandable account of a specific decision, which for opaque models comes from post-hoc methods such as SHAP.

options.text: Interpretability applies only to generative models; explainability applies only to classification models
options.rationale: Both concepts apply across model families regardless of task.

options.text: Explainability requires open source weights while interpretability does not
options.rationale: Post-hoc explanation methods work on closed models without exposing weights.

questions.question: A product team designs a UI for an AI assistant used by nurses during triage. Which human-centered design choice best reduces the risk of over-reliance on the model?

options.text: Hide the model's confidence so nurses are not distracted
options.rationale: Hiding uncertainty removes the signal a clinician needs to judge when to doubt the system.

options.text: Display the model's confidence and the sources behind each suggestion, and make it easy to override
options.rationale: Human-centered design for explainable AI surfaces uncertainty and provenance so the human can calibrate trust, and preserves easy reversal and override so the person remains the decision-maker. Hiding confidence or auto-applying suggestions encourages automation bias.

options.text: Automatically apply the model's suggestion after a five second delay
options.rationale: Auto-applying a suggestion removes human agency and is the opposite of design for reversibility.

options.text: Increase the font size of the model's recommendation
options.rationale: Typography does not affect whether the recommendation is appropriately trusted.

questions.question: A team is told that adopting a more explainable model may reduce raw predictive accuracy. How should they frame this tradeoff?

options.text: Accuracy must always be maximized regardless of context
options.rationale: Maximizing accuracy while ignoring legal and ethical obligations is not defensible.

options.text: The acceptable balance depends on the stakes of the decision and any regulatory obligation to explain it
options.rationale: The tradeoff is contextual: for low-stakes recommendations, a small accuracy gain may justify opacity, while for consequential decisions subject to regulation, the ability to explain can outweigh a marginal accuracy improvement. On many tabular problems the accuracy gap is small or nonexistent.

options.text: Explainable models are always less accurate than opaque models
options.rationale: Interpretable models frequently match complex models on structured tabular data.

options.text: Explainability is only relevant for generative AI systems
options.rationale: Explainability applies to traditional predictive models at least as much as to generative AI.

questions.question: Which capability of Amazon SageMaker Clarify supports explainability rather than bias detection?

options.text: Class imbalance metric
options.rationale: Class imbalance is a pre-training bias metric about dataset composition.

options.text: Feature attribution using SHAP values
options.rationale: SHAP-based feature attribution quantifies how much each feature contributed to a prediction, which is the explainability function of SageMaker Clarify. Class imbalance, difference in proportions of labels, and disparate impact are all bias metrics describing group disparities.

options.text: Difference in proportions of labels
options.rationale: Difference in proportions of labels compares positive outcome rates between groups.

options.text: Disparate impact ratio
options.rationale: Disparate impact is a ratio-based fairness metric, not an explanation of a prediction.

questions.question: A bank must retain evidence that each production model was reviewed and approved, including who approved it and what evaluation results were considered. Which combination best supports an audit years later?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch metrics retained for 15 months
options.rationale: CloudWatch metrics show operational behavior, not review decisions or approvals.

options.text: SageMaker Model Cards for documentation combined with AWS CloudTrail logs of API activity
options.rationale: Model Cards preserve the documented intent, evaluation results, and limitations reviewed at approval time, while CloudTrail provides an immutable record of who performed which API actions. Together they answer both what was decided and who did it. Metrics, data versioning, and content filters do not capture approval context.

options.text: Amazon S3 versioning on the training data bucket alone
options.rationale: Data versioning preserves inputs but records nothing about model review or approval.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails configured with denied topics
options.rationale: Guardrails enforce runtime content policy and produce no governance documentation.

questions.question: Which principle of human-centered design for explainable AI is illustrated by allowing a user to undo an action the AI system took?

options.text: Design for reversibility
options.rationale: Design for reversibility means building in the ability to undo or correct automated actions, which limits the harm of an incorrect output and keeps a human meaningfully in control. Cognitive load, amplified decision making, and decision theory address information volume, augmentation of human judgment, and structured choice under uncertainty.

options.text: Cognitive load reduction
options.rationale: Cognitive load reduction concerns presenting only the information the user needs to decide.

options.text: Amplified decision making
options.rationale: Amplified decision making concerns using AI to strengthen rather than replace human judgment.

options.text: Decision theory
options.rationale: Decision theory concerns modeling choices and their expected outcomes under uncertainty.

questions.question: An organization wants to increase transparency about a third-party foundation model it plans to adopt. Which two sources of information are most relevant? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The model provider's published documentation of intended use, training approach, and limitations
options.rationale: Transparency about an adopted model comes from what the provider discloses about how it was built and what it should not be used for, together with licensing terms that govern permitted use of the model and its outputs. Region, instance family, and context window are operational and capability facts, not transparency artifacts.

options.text: Licensing terms governing how the model and its outputs may be used
options.rationale: Transparency about an adopted model comes from what the provider discloses about how it was built and what it should not be used for, together with licensing terms that govern permitted use of the model and its outputs. Region, instance family, and context window are operational and capability facts, not transparency artifacts.

options.text: The AWS Region in which the model endpoint is deployed
options.rationale: Region choice affects residency and latency, not disclosure about the model.

options.text: The instance family used for inference
options.rationale: Instance family is an infrastructure detail unrelated to model transparency.

options.text: The number of tokens in the model's context window
options.rationale: Context window describes capacity, not intended use or limitations.

questions.question: A team presents a dashboard showing 40 feature attribution charts for every prediction a loan officer reviews. Officers report they cannot use it. Which human-centered design principle was violated?

options.text: Design for reversibility
options.rationale: Reversibility concerns the ability to undo actions, which is not what failed here.

options.text: Managing cognitive load by presenting only the information needed for the decision
options.rationale: Explanations must be usable, not merely available. Presenting an overwhelming volume of detail increases cognitive load and makes the explanation effectively useless, so good design surfaces the few most influential factors with detail available on demand.

options.text: Amplified decision making
options.rationale: Amplified decision making is the goal; excessive detail is what prevented it.

options.text: Transparency about AI involvement
options.rationale: The officers know AI is involved; the problem is the volume of explanation.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a model card in AI governance?

options.text: To store the model's trained weights for deployment
options.rationale: Weights are stored as model artifacts in Amazon S3, not in a documentation card.

options.text: To document a model's intended use, performance, training data characteristics, and limitations in one place
options.rationale: A model card is a structured documentation artifact recording what a model is for, how it was built and evaluated, and where it should not be used. It exists so reviewers, auditors, and downstream users can judge appropriate use. It is documentation, not storage, scaling, or encryption.

options.text: To configure autoscaling for the model endpoint
options.rationale: Autoscaling is configured on the endpoint, unrelated to documentation.

options.text: To encrypt the model artifact at rest
options.rationale: Encryption at rest is handled by AWS KMS and storage configuration.

questions.question: A company must justify to an internal ethics board why it selected a foundation model. Which evidence best demonstrates a transparent selection process?

options.text: A statement that the model had the lowest cost per token
options.rationale: Cost alone ignores safety, bias, and suitability considerations the board must review.

options.text: Documented evaluation results across accuracy, safety, and bias criteria, with the provider's stated limitations and the reasons alternatives were rejected
options.rationale: Transparency in selection means recording what criteria were applied, what the measured results were, what the provider disclosed about limitations, and why other candidates were rejected. A single cost figure or capability detail does not show that responsible criteria were weighed.

options.text: A screenshot of the model appearing in the Amazon Bedrock console
options.rationale: Console availability says nothing about why the model was appropriate.

options.text: Confirmation that the model supports streaming responses
options.rationale: Streaming support is a delivery feature unrelated to responsible selection.

questions.question: Which AWS capability lets a team compare foundation models on custom criteria, including using human reviewers, to inform a documented selection decision?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation
options.rationale: Amazon Bedrock Model Evaluation supports automatic evaluation with built-in and custom prompt datasets, human-based evaluation using your own work teams and criteria, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, producing comparable results that support a documented model choice.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
options.rationale: Feature Store manages engineered features for traditional ML workflows.

options.text: AWS Config
options.rationale: AWS Config tracks resource configuration compliance, not model quality.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management
options.rationale: Prompt Management versions and stores prompts; it does not score models.

questions.question: An engineer says a model is a black box and therefore nothing can be said about why it produced an output. Which response is most accurate?

options.text: The engineer is correct; opaque models cannot be explained at all
options.rationale: Post-hoc explanation methods exist precisely for opaque models.

options.text: Post-hoc techniques such as SHAP feature attribution can estimate each input's contribution even when internal mechanics are opaque
options.rationale: Even when a model's internals are not human-readable, post-hoc explanation methods can attribute an output to input features, and tools such as SageMaker Clarify implement this. Opacity limits interpretability but does not eliminate explainability.

options.text: Only the model provider can explain any output
options.rationale: Customers can apply attribution techniques themselves without provider involvement.

options.text: Explanation requires retraining the model as a decision tree
options.rationale: Retraining as a simpler model is one option, but it is not a prerequisite for explanation.

questions.question: A generative AI assistant answers employee policy questions. Which design choice most improves users' ability to verify an answer themselves?

options.text: Returning citations linking each claim to the source document passage
options.rationale: Citations that link a claim back to the retrieved source let a user check the answer against authoritative text, which is the practical form transparency takes in a RAG assistant. Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases can return source attribution with responses. Sampling settings, length limits, and model size do not provide verifiability.

options.text: Reducing the temperature parameter to zero
options.rationale: A temperature of zero makes output more deterministic but no more verifiable.

options.text: Increasing the maximum token limit
options.rationale: A higher token limit allows longer answers, not checkable ones.

options.text: Using a larger foundation model
options.rationale: A larger model may still state unverifiable claims confidently.

questions.question: Which principle of human-centered design for explainable AI is best described as using AI to strengthen human judgment rather than replace it?

options.text: Amplified decision making
options.rationale: Amplified decision making positions the AI as a tool that improves the quality and speed of a human decision while the human retains responsibility for the outcome. Reversibility, cognitive load, and feedback mechanisms are distinct supporting principles.

options.text: Design for reversibility
options.rationale: Reversibility concerns the ability to undo automated actions.

options.text: Cognitive load management
options.rationale: Cognitive load management concerns limiting information to what is decision-relevant.

options.text: User feedback mechanisms
options.rationale: Feedback mechanisms let users report problems so the system can improve.

questions.question: A team must choose between a gradient boosted tree ensemble with 91 percent accuracy and a logistic regression with 89 percent accuracy for an automated benefits eligibility decision that must be explained to applicants by law. Which choice is best justified?

options.text: The gradient boosted ensemble, because accuracy is the only defensible criterion
options.rationale: Accuracy is not the only criterion when a legal explanation duty applies.

options.text: The logistic regression, because its coefficients provide directly stateable reasons and the accuracy difference is small relative to the legal requirement
options.rationale: With a binding legal duty to explain decisions and only a two point accuracy difference, the inherently interpretable model is the defensible choice because its coefficients translate directly into stateable reasons. Post-hoc attribution on the ensemble is an alternative but adds an approximation layer where the law expects a direct account.

options.text: Neither model, because automated eligibility decisions are prohibited
options.rationale: Automated eligibility decisions are not universally prohibited; they are subject to explanation requirements.

options.text: The gradient boosted ensemble, because tree models are inherently interpretable at any depth
options.rationale: A large boosted ensemble of many deep trees is not human-interpretable, unlike a single shallow tree.

questions.question: Which practice best supports the user feedback principle of human-centered design in a deployed AI assistant?

options.text: Providing an in-product way for users to flag an incorrect or harmful response, routed to a review process
options.rationale: User feedback mechanisms give the people affected by the system a direct channel to report problems, and routing that feedback into review closes the loop so issues drive improvement. Architecture diagrams, latency, and Region scope do not capture user-observed failures.

options.text: Publishing the model architecture diagram on the company website
options.rationale: An architecture diagram informs engineers but gives users no way to report a bad output.

options.text: Increasing the assistant's response speed
options.rationale: Faster responses do not surface incorrect ones.

options.text: Restricting the assistant to a single AWS Region
options.rationale: Region restriction is a data residency and availability decision.

questions.question: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task remains the customer's responsibility when using Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: Patching the physical servers that host foundation models
options.rationale: Physical server patching is part of AWS responsibility for the underlying infrastructure.

options.text: Configuring IAM policies that control which users can invoke which models
options.rationale: AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, including physical facilities and the managed service infrastructure. The customer is responsible for security in the cloud, which for Bedrock includes identity and access management, data protection choices, and how the application uses the service.

options.text: Maintaining the physical security of AWS data centers
options.rationale: Data center physical security is entirely an AWS responsibility.

options.text: Applying security patches to the Bedrock service infrastructure
options.rationale: Patching the managed service infrastructure is handled by AWS.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company must ensure traffic between its VPC and Amazon Bedrock never traverses the public internet. Which approach meets this requirement?

options.text: Attach an internet gateway to the VPC
options.rationale: An internet gateway is exactly what sends traffic to the public internet.

options.text: Create a VPC endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink for Amazon Bedrock
options.rationale: An interface VPC endpoint backed by AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity from a VPC to a supported AWS service, keeping traffic on the AWS network. Internet and NAT gateways both route traffic to the public internet, and S3 encryption protects stored objects rather than network paths.

options.text: Use a NAT gateway for all Bedrock requests
options.rationale: A NAT gateway still routes outbound traffic over the internet.

options.text: Enable server-side encryption on the S3 bucket holding prompts
options.rationale: Encryption at rest protects stored data; it does not change the network path.

questions.question: Which AWS service should be used to record who called which Amazon Bedrock API and when, for security auditing?

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
options.rationale: CloudWatch Logs stores application and service log output, not an authoritative API audit trail.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail
options.rationale: AWS CloudTrail records API activity across AWS services, capturing the identity, action, time, and source IP, which is the standard answer for auditing who did what. CloudWatch collects operational metrics and application logs, Config tracks resource configuration state, and Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.

options.text: AWS Config
options.rationale: AWS Config records configuration changes and compliance state, not per-call API identity.

options.text: Amazon Inspector
options.rationale: Inspector performs vulnerability assessments on workloads.

questions.question: A team stores training data containing customer records in Amazon S3. Which two controls best protect this data at rest and limit exposure? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable server-side encryption with an AWS KMS customer managed key
options.rationale: Encryption with a KMS key protects the objects at rest and lets you control and audit key usage, while Block Public Access prevents any policy or ACL from unintentionally exposing the bucket publicly. Storage class, acceleration, and Requester Pays affect cost and transfer behavior, not security posture.

options.text: Enable S3 Block Public Access on the bucket
options.rationale: Encryption with a KMS key protects the objects at rest and lets you control and audit key usage, while Block Public Access prevents any policy or ACL from unintentionally exposing the bucket publicly. Storage class, acceleration, and Requester Pays affect cost and transfer behavior, not security posture.

options.text: Increase the S3 bucket's storage class to S3 Standard-IA
options.rationale: Storage class changes cost and retrieval characteristics, not protection.

options.text: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration
options.rationale: Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over long distances; it is not a security control.

options.text: Turn on S3 Requester Pays
options.rationale: Requester Pays shifts data transfer billing and does not restrict access.
