questions.question: A company wants to discover whether any of its S3 buckets used for machine learning contain personally identifiable information. Which service is purpose-built for this?

options.text: Amazon Macie
options.rationale: Amazon Macie uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII in Amazon S3 at scale, and reports findings. Comprehend can detect PII entities within text you pass to it, but Macie is the service designed to scan S3 estates for sensitive data discovery.

options.text: Amazon Comprehend
options.rationale: Comprehend analyzes text you submit; it does not inventory and scan S3 buckets on its own.

options.text: AWS Config
options.rationale: AWS Config evaluates resource configuration compliance, not object contents.

options.text: Amazon GuardDuty
options.rationale: GuardDuty detects malicious activity and unauthorized behavior, not sensitive data classification.

questions.question: An attacker submits input designed to make a customer support assistant ignore its system instructions and reveal internal pricing rules. Which combination of mitigations is most appropriate?

options.text: Increase the model's temperature and reduce max tokens
options.rationale: Sampling parameters do not prevent an instruction-override attack.

options.text: Validate and delimit untrusted input, apply Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and never place secrets in the system prompt
options.rationale: Prompt injection is mitigated in layers: treat user content as untrusted and clearly delimit it, enforce content and topic policy with Guardrails, apply least privilege to any tools the model can call, and keep genuine secrets out of prompts entirely since a sufficiently determined prompt may surface them.

options.text: Move the endpoint to a different AWS Region
options.rationale: Region choice affects residency and latency, not adversarial input handling.

options.text: Switch from on-demand to Provisioned Throughput
options.rationale: Capacity mode is a pricing and throughput decision with no security effect.

questions.question: Which IAM practice best reflects least privilege for a data scientist who only needs to invoke one specific foundation model in Amazon Bedrock?

options.text: Attach the AdministratorAccess managed policy
options.rationale: Administrator access grants far more than the task requires.

options.text: Grant an IAM role a policy allowing bedrock:InvokeModel scoped to that model's ARN
options.rationale: Least privilege means granting only the actions required on only the resources required, so an identity-based policy allowing the specific invoke action against the specific model ARN is correct. Administrator access, wildcard service permissions, and shared long-lived credentials all violate the principle.

options.text: Share long-lived IAM user access keys across the team
options.rationale: Shared long-lived keys break individual accountability and are hard to rotate.

options.text: Grant bedrock:* on all resources
options.rationale: A service-wide wildcard permits every Bedrock action on every resource.

questions.question: A regulated customer asks whether their prompts and completions sent to Amazon Bedrock are used to train the underlying base foundation models. What is accurate?

options.text: All customer inputs are automatically added to base model training data
options.rationale: Inputs are not automatically added to base model training data.

options.text: Customer content submitted to Amazon Bedrock is not used to train the underlying base foundation models and is not shared with model providers
options.rationale: Amazon Bedrock does not use customer prompts and completions to train the underlying base foundation models, and does not share that content with third-party model providers. This data privacy posture is a common reason regulated customers select Bedrock, and it does not depend on the pricing mode.

options.text: Customer data is used for training unless Provisioned Throughput is purchased
options.rationale: The posture does not depend on purchasing Provisioned Throughput.

options.text: Customer data is used for training only in non-production accounts
options.rationale: The posture does not vary by whether the account is production or not.

options.rationale: Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging captures request and response content and delivers it to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3, or both, which is what an investigation into actual model content requires. CloudTrail records that an API call happened and by whom, but is not the mechanism for full prompt and completion content.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail data events only
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity metadata rather than serving as the content logging feature.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails denied topics
options.rationale: Denied topics block subject matter; they do not record traffic.

options.text: SageMaker Model Monitor data capture
options.rationale: SageMaker data capture applies to SageMaker endpoints, not Bedrock invocations.

questions.question: Which AWS service securely stores and rotates database credentials that an ML application needs at runtime?

options.text: AWS Secrets Manager
options.rationale: AWS Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database credentials and API keys, encrypts them with AWS KMS, controls access through IAM, and supports automatic rotation. Storing credentials in S3 objects, log files, or code is the anti-pattern this service exists to eliminate.

options.text: Amazon S3
options.rationale: S3 is object storage and offers no secret rotation or purpose-built credential handling.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity; it does not store application secrets.

options.text: Amazon EBS
options.rationale: EBS provides block storage volumes for EC2 instances.

questions.question: A security team is enumerating threats specific to machine learning systems. Which two are genuine ML-specific attack types? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Data poisoning, where an attacker corrupts training data to alter model behavior
options.rationale: Data poisoning targets the training pipeline by injecting crafted examples that change what the model learns, and model inversion attempts to recover sensitive training data by probing the model. The remaining options are generic web, storage, and certificate operational issues rather than ML-specific attacks.

options.text: Model inversion, where an attacker reconstructs sensitive training data from model outputs
options.rationale: Data poisoning targets the training pipeline by injecting crafted examples that change what the model learns, and model inversion attempts to recover sensitive training data by probing the model. The remaining options are generic web, storage, and certificate operational issues rather than ML-specific attacks.

options.text: Cross-site scripting in the training job console
options.rationale: Cross-site scripting is a general web application vulnerability, not ML specific.

options.text: Disk fragmentation on the training instance
options.rationale: Disk fragmentation is a performance concern, not a security attack.

options.text: TLS certificate expiry on the endpoint
options.rationale: Certificate expiry causes an availability or trust failure but is not an ML attack.

questions.question: A SageMaker training job processes highly sensitive data and must not have any internet connectivity. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Run the training job with network isolation enabled and within a VPC with no internet route
options.rationale: SageMaker supports network isolation for training jobs, which prevents the training container from making outbound network calls, and jobs can be launched into a customer VPC with private subnets and VPC endpoints so no internet path exists. Instance size, versioning, and purchase option have no bearing on network exposure.

options.text: Run the training job on a larger instance type
options.rationale: Instance type affects compute capacity and cost, not network reachability.

options.text: Enable Amazon S3 versioning on the input bucket
options.rationale: Versioning protects against accidental overwrite; it is not network control.

options.text: Use a spot instance for the training job
options.rationale: Spot is a pricing model for interruptible capacity.

questions.question: Which practice best prevents sensitive customer data from leaking into a foundation model's responses through the application's own prompts?

options.text: Increase the model's context window
options.rationale: A larger context window lets you send more data, which increases rather than reduces exposure.

options.text: Redact or tokenize sensitive fields before including any data in the prompt
options.rationale: Whatever is placed in a prompt can appear in a response or in logs, so sensitive values should be removed, masked, or replaced with tokens before the prompt is constructed. Bedrock Guardrails sensitive information filters can add a second layer by redacting PII in prompts and responses.

options.text: Use a smaller foundation model
options.rationale: Model size does not determine whether sensitive input is echoed back.

options.text: Enable response streaming
options.rationale: Streaming changes delivery of tokens, not what data was sent.

questions.question: Which statement about encryption for machine learning workloads on AWS is accurate?

options.text: Encryption in transit is handled by TLS, and encryption at rest is commonly handled with AWS KMS keys
options.rationale: TLS protects data moving between clients and services, while AWS KMS manages keys used to encrypt data at rest in services such as Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, and SageMaker volumes. The two protect different states of data and both are typically required.

options.text: Encryption at rest is unnecessary when data is stored in a private VPC
options.rationale: A private network does not encrypt stored data; at-rest encryption is still required.

options.text: AWS KMS encrypts network traffic between services
options.rationale: KMS manages keys for data at rest; network encryption is provided by TLS.

options.text: TLS protects stored objects in Amazon S3
options.rationale: TLS protects data in transit, not objects sitting in storage.

questions.question: An organization wants to give a Bedrock agent the ability to call an internal order API, while limiting the damage if the model is manipulated. Which control is most important?

options.text: Grant the agent's execution role permission only to the specific read actions it needs, and require human approval for state-changing calls
options.rationale: An agent acts with the permissions of its execution role, so scoping that role narrowly limits the blast radius of a successful prompt injection, and requiring human approval before irreversible actions provides a second gate. Broad permissions, larger token limits, and disabled logging all increase risk.

options.text: Give the agent full administrative permissions so it never fails a request
options.rationale: Administrative permissions turn any successful manipulation into a full compromise.

options.text: Increase the agent's maximum token limit
options.rationale: Token limits affect response length, not authorization scope.

options.text: Disable CloudTrail logging to reduce noise
options.rationale: Disabling CloudTrail removes the audit trail needed to investigate an incident.

options.text: AWS Secrets Manager
options.rationale: Secrets Manager stores and rotates credentials, not role definitions for ML personas.

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

options.text: AWS Artifact
options.rationale: Artifact provides AWS compliance reports.

questions.question: A competitor repeatedly queries a company's public prediction API to reconstruct an equivalent model. Which threat is this, and which mitigation is most relevant?

options.text: Overfitting, mitigated by regularization

questions.question: Which statement about IAM roles versus IAM users is most accurate for machine learning workloads on AWS?

options.text: IAM users are preferred because their access keys never expire
options.rationale: Non-expiring access keys are a liability, not an advantage.

options.text: IAM roles provide temporary credentials and are preferred for applications and services such as SageMaker training jobs
options.rationale: IAM roles deliver short-lived, automatically rotated credentials and can be assumed by AWS services, which is why SageMaker training jobs, Bedrock agents, and Lambda functions use execution roles. Long-lived IAM user access keys are harder to rotate and are a common source of credential leakage.

options.text: IAM roles cannot be assumed by AWS services

options.rationale: They differ meaningfully in credential lifetime and how they are assumed.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best description of defense in depth for an AI application?

options.text: Applying multiple independent layers such as identity controls, network isolation, input validation, guardrails, logging, and human review

options.text: Encrypting data at rest and considering the system secure

options.rationale: CloudWatch is the metrics, logs, and alarming service, while CloudTrail is the API audit trail identifying who performed which action. Macie classifies sensitive data, KMS manages encryption keys, and S3 stores objects without evaluating model quality.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail provides an audit trail of API calls including the calling identity
options.rationale: CloudWatch is the metrics, logs, and alarming service, while CloudTrail is the API audit trail identifying who performed which action. Macie classifies sensitive data, KMS manages encryption keys, and S3 stores objects without evaluating model quality.

options.text: Amazon Macie streams real-time inference latency metrics
options.rationale: Macie performs sensitive data discovery, not latency monitoring.

options.text: AWS KMS records which users viewed model outputs
options.rationale: KMS manages keys and logs key usage, not who read model outputs.

options.text: Amazon S3 automatically alerts on model accuracy degradation
options.rationale: S3 has no awareness of model accuracy.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: An application passes user-supplied text directly into a prompt that also contains instructions. Which single change most reduces prompt injection risk?

options.text: Clearly delimit the untrusted user content and instruct the model to treat it as data rather than instructions
options.rationale: Marking untrusted content with explicit delimiters and telling the model that the enclosed text is data to be processed rather than instructions to follow is the foundational structural mitigation. It is combined with guardrails, input validation, and least-privilege tool access rather than replacing them.

options.text: Increase the temperature so responses vary
options.rationale: Higher temperature increases variability and does not resist injection.

options.text: Reduce the number of few-shot examples
options.rationale: Few-shot example count affects response quality, not injection resistance.

options.text: Switch the model to a different provider
options.rationale: Changing provider does not remove the structural weakness of mixing data and instructions.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which statement about the AWS shared responsibility model is accurate for a fully managed AI service such as Amazon Rekognition?

options.text: The customer must patch the operating system running the service
options.rationale: There is no customer-managed operating system in a fully managed AI service.

options.text: AWS manages the underlying infrastructure and model operations, while the customer controls access, input data, and how results are used
options.rationale: With a fully managed AI service, AWS operates the infrastructure and the service itself, which shifts more responsibility to AWS than with self-managed compute. The customer still controls identity and access, what data is submitted, and how outputs are applied in their business process.

options.text: The customer is responsible for physical data center access controls
options.rationale: Physical security is always an AWS responsibility.

options.text: AWS assumes responsibility for how the customer uses the service's outputs
options.rationale: How outputs are used in a business decision remains the customer's responsibility.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company must ensure that only encrypted connections are used when an application calls an ML inference endpoint. Which mechanism provides this?

options.text: TLS for data in transit
options.rationale: TLS encrypts data as it moves between the client and the endpoint, which is the in-transit protection AWS service endpoints use by default. KMS handles keys for data at rest, Block Public Access governs S3 exposure, and permission boundaries limit maximum IAM permissions.

options.text: AWS KMS envelope encryption
options.rationale: KMS envelope encryption protects stored data, not the network connection.

options.text: S3 Block Public Access
options.rationale: Block Public Access prevents public S3 exposure and is unrelated to endpoint connections.

options.text: IAM permission boundaries
options.rationale: Permission boundaries constrain IAM privileges rather than encrypt traffic.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which approach best addresses the risk that employees paste confidential information into a third-party generative AI tool?

options.text: Provide an approved internal assistant built on Amazon Bedrock with appropriate controls, and set clear usage policy and training
options.rationale: Shadow AI use is best addressed by providing a sanctioned alternative with proper data controls, combined with explicit policy and employee training so people know what may be shared and where. Blanket internet blocking is impractical, and relying on an external provider's terms transfers no real control.

options.text: Block all internet access company-wide
options.rationale: Blocking all internet access is disproportionate and rarely feasible.

options.text: Rely on the third-party provider's terms of service
options.rationale: Provider terms do not prevent employees from disclosing confidential data.

options.text: Increase the company's AWS spending limit
options.rationale: Spending limits have no relationship to data handling behavior.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A team wants to verify that an S3 bucket holding fine-tuning data has not been made publicly accessible at any point. Which combination provides both current state and historical evidence?

options.text: AWS Config for configuration state and history, together with AWS CloudTrail for the API calls that changed it
options.rationale: AWS Config records the configuration state of a resource over time and can flag non-compliant public access settings, while CloudTrail identifies the specific API calls and identities that changed the configuration. Together they answer both what the state was and who changed it.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch metrics alone
options.rationale: CloudWatch metrics describe operational performance, not bucket access configuration history.

options.text: Amazon Macie findings alone
options.rationale: Macie identifies sensitive data content but does not track configuration history.

options.text: S3 lifecycle policies
options.rationale: Lifecycle policies transition or expire objects and record nothing about access settings.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which statement best describes why data quality matters as a security and governance concern, not only an accuracy concern?

options.text: Poor quality data always increases storage cost
options.rationale: Cost effects are incidental and not the governance concern.

options.text: Corrupted or maliciously altered training data can change model behavior in ways that create safety, fairness, and compliance failures
options.rationale: Training data integrity is a security property because an attacker who alters it, or an unnoticed corruption, changes what the model learns and can produce unsafe, biased, or non-compliant behavior. This is why data validation, lineage, and access controls on training data are governance controls.

options.text: Data quality affects only the training time of a model
options.rationale: Quality affects behavior and outcomes, not merely how long training takes.

options.text: Data quality is checked automatically by AWS before training begins
options.rationale: AWS does not automatically validate the semantic quality of customer training data.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which AWS service centralizes workforce identity and single sign-on across multiple AWS accounts for an ML platform team?

options.text: AWS IAM Identity Center
options.rationale: AWS IAM Identity Center provides centralized workforce single sign-on and permission set assignment across accounts in an organization, which is the standard answer for employee access at scale. Cognito is aimed at application end users, and the other services manage secrets and certificates.

options.text: Amazon Cognito user pools for end customers
options.rationale: Cognito handles authentication for customer-facing applications rather than workforce SSO.

options.text: AWS Secrets Manager
options.rationale: Secrets Manager stores credentials, not identity federation.

options.text: AWS Certificate Manager
options.rationale: Certificate Manager provisions and manages TLS certificates.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company sets a policy that model training data must be deleted 90 days after a project ends. Which concept does this represent?

options.text: Data retention as part of the data lifecycle
options.rationale: Retention defines how long data is kept before deletion and is a core part of data lifecycle governance, often enforced with S3 lifecycle policies. Lineage traces origin and transformations, cataloging records metadata, and residency concerns the geographic location of data.

options.text: Data lineage
options.rationale: Lineage describes where data came from and how it was transformed.

options.text: Data cataloging
options.rationale: Cataloging maintains searchable metadata about datasets.

options.text: Data residency
options.rationale: Residency concerns which country or Region stores the data.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: An application allows users to upload documents that are then embedded into a shared vector store used by all employees. What is the most significant security concern with this design?

options.text: Embedding generation will be too slow
options.rationale: Embedding latency is an operational concern, not the primary security risk.

options.text: A user could upload confidential content that then surfaces in answers given to employees who should not see it
options.rationale: A shared retrieval index without per-document access controls collapses distinct permission boundaries, so anything ingested becomes reachable by every user of the assistant. The fix is to enforce document-level access filtering at retrieval time or maintain separate indexes per audience.

options.text: The vector store will exceed its maximum dimension count
options.rationale: Dimension count is a fixed property of the embedding model, not a security issue.

options.text: Prompt caching will be disabled
options.rationale: Prompt caching is a latency and cost optimization unrelated to this risk.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A healthcare provider in the United States plans to process patient records with a machine learning model. Which compliance standard is most directly relevant?

options.text: PCI DSS
options.rationale: PCI DSS applies to cardholder payment data, not medical records.

options.text: HIPAA
options.rationale: HIPAA governs the handling of protected health information in the United States, so a workload processing patient records must be designed for HIPAA requirements. PCI DSS covers payment card data, GDPR covers personal data of individuals in the EU, and ISO 27001 is a general information security management standard.

options.text: GDPR
options.rationale: GDPR governs personal data of individuals in the European Union.
ISO 27001 is a broad security management certification, not health-data specific.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A European retailer must honor customer requests to delete personal data used in model training. Which regulation drives this requirement?

options.text: GDPR
options.rationale: The General Data Protection Regulation grants individuals rights over their personal data including access, correction, and erasure, which is why data lifecycle and deletion capability must be designed into ML pipelines handling EU personal data. The other frameworks address payment data, service organization controls, and health information.

options.text: PCI DSS
options.rationale: PCI DSS governs payment card data security, not individual data subject rights.

options.text: SOC 2
options.rationale: SOC 2 reports on service organization controls; it does not grant deletion rights.

options.text: HIPAA
options.rationale: HIPAA governs protected health information in the United States.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a centralized data catalog with fine-grained access permissions for a data lake used by multiple analytics and ML teams?

options.text: AWS Lake Formation
options.rationale: AWS Lake Formation centralizes data lake permissions, allowing database, table, column, row, and cell level access control layered over the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Macie classifies sensitive data, Artifact supplies compliance documents, and Inspector scans for vulnerabilities.

options.text: Amazon Macie
options.rationale: Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data in Amazon S3 without managing lake permissions.

options.text: AWS Artifact
options.rationale: Artifact provides AWS compliance reports for download.

options.text: Amazon Inspector
options.rationale: Inspector performs automated vulnerability assessments.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: An organization wants business users to discover, understand, and request access to datasets across accounts with governed workflows. Which AWS service is designed for this?

options.text: Amazon DataZone
options.rationale: Amazon DataZone is a data management service for cataloging, discovering, sharing, and governing data across AWS accounts and on-premises sources, including subscription-based access request workflows. Athena queries data, Glue crawlers populate technical metadata, and QuickSight visualizes results.

options.text: Amazon Athena
options.rationale: Athena runs SQL queries over data in Amazon S3; it does not provide governed discovery workflows.

options.text: AWS Glue crawlers
options.rationale: Glue crawlers infer schema and populate the Data Catalog but offer no business governance layer.

options.text: Amazon QuickSight
options.rationale: QuickSight is a business intelligence and dashboarding service.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company is establishing an AI governance program. Which two elements are core to such a program? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Defined policies with named owners and a regular review cadence for deployed models
options.rationale: Governance programs are built on written policies with accountable owners and a review cadence, plus standards for what must be disclosed to users and regulators. Prescriptive infrastructure rules about instance types, retraining frequency, or bucket layout are operational choices rather than governance principles.

options.text: Documented transparency standards describing when and how AI use is disclosed
options.rationale: Governance programs are built on written policies with accountable owners and a review cadence, plus standards for what must be disclosed to users and regulators. Prescriptive infrastructure rules about instance types, retraining frequency, or bucket layout are operational choices rather than governance principles.

options.text: A requirement that all models use the largest available instance type
options.rationale: Instance sizing is a cost and performance decision, not governance.

options.text: A rule that models must be retrained daily regardless of drift
options.rationale: Retraining should be triggered by drift and business need, not an arbitrary daily schedule.

options.text: A policy that all training data be stored in a single S3 bucket
options.rationale: Consolidating storage into one bucket is not a governance requirement and may hinder access control.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which AWS service should a compliance officer use to download AWS's SOC 2 report?

options.text: AWS Artifact
options.rationale: AWS Artifact is the on-demand portal for AWS compliance reports and agreements, including SOC reports, ISO certifications, and PCI documents. Audit Manager produces evidence about the customer's own workloads rather than AWS's certifications.

options.text: AWS Audit Manager
options.rationale: Audit Manager collects evidence about your workloads for your own audits.

options.text: AWS Config
options.rationale: AWS Config records and evaluates resource configurations.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity in your account.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A financial services company must demonstrate that its generative AI application's controls map to a recognized framework and produce evidence continuously. Which service best supports this?

options.text: AWS Audit Manager
options.rationale: AWS Audit Manager maps AWS activity to control frameworks, continuously collects evidence, and generates audit-ready reports, which is what demonstrating control coverage to an auditor requires. CloudWatch supplies operational telemetry, Guardrails enforce content policy, and Secrets Manager stores credentials.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch
options.rationale: CloudWatch provides metrics and logs but does not map them to compliance controls.

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
options.rationale: Guardrails enforce runtime content policy and produce no framework evidence.

options.text: AWS Secrets Manager
options.rationale: Secrets Manager handles credential storage and rotation.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company operating in the European Union is assessing obligations under the EU AI Act. Which statement best reflects its general approach?

options.text: All AI systems are prohibited unless individually approved by regulators
options.rationale: Most AI systems are permitted; only a narrow category of practices is prohibited outright.

options.text: Obligations scale with the risk category of the AI system, with stricter requirements for high-risk uses
options.rationale: The EU AI Act uses a risk-based structure in which obligations increase with the assessed risk of the use case, imposing the strictest requirements on high-risk applications and prohibiting a narrow set of unacceptable practices. It is not a blanket prohibition and is not limited to generative systems or EU-trained models.

options.text: It applies only to systems trained inside the European Union
options.rationale: Applicability follows where the system is placed on the market or used, not solely where it was trained.

options.text: It regulates only generative AI systems
options.rationale: The framework covers AI systems broadly, not only generative AI.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which concept describes an organizational approach where individual business domains own and publish their data as products, with federated governance?

options.text: Data mesh
options.rationale: A data mesh decentralizes ownership so domain teams publish and maintain their data as products, governed by federated standards rather than a single central team. A warehouse is a storage and analytics architecture, lineage traces data movement, and residency concerns geographic location.

options.text: Data warehouse
options.rationale: A data warehouse is a centralized analytical store, not an ownership model.

options.text: Data lineage
options.rationale: Lineage describes where data came from and how it was transformed.

options.text: Data residency
options.rationale: Residency concerns which jurisdiction stores the data.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A multinational company must keep customer data physically within a specific country. Which governance concept is this, and which AWS control most directly supports it?

options.text: Data residency, supported by selecting the AWS Region where data is stored and processed
options.rationale: Data residency is the requirement that data remain within a defined geography, and the primary AWS control is choosing the Region in which data is stored and processed, reinforced by policies restricting Region use. Lineage, retention, and cataloging address different governance questions.

options.text: Data lineage, supported by AWS Glue crawlers
options.rationale: Lineage traces transformations rather than constraining geography.

options.text: Data retention, supported by S3 lifecycle policies
options.rationale: Retention governs how long data is kept, not where it lives.

options.text: Data cataloging, supported by Amazon DataZone
options.rationale: Cataloging makes data discoverable and does not enforce location.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which compliance standard applies to an ML system that processes credit card transaction data?

options.text: HIPAA
options.rationale: HIPAA governs protected health information.

options.text: PCI DSS
options.rationale: The Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard governs the storage, processing, and transmission of cardholder data, so a fraud model handling transaction data falls in scope. HIPAA covers health information, FERPA covers education records, and ISO 9001 addresses quality management.

options.text: FERPA
options.rationale: FERPA governs student education records in the United States.

options.text: ISO 9001
options.rationale: ISO 9001 is a quality management standard, not a data security standard.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: An AI governance board is being formed. Which two responsibilities are appropriate for it? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reviewing and approving high-risk AI use cases before deployment
options.rationale: A governance board sets standards and reviews consequential use cases, providing cross-functional oversight and accountability. Writing code and provisioning infrastructure are engineering activities that the board governs rather than performs.

options.text: Setting organization-wide standards for documentation, evaluation, and monitoring of models
options.rationale: A governance board sets standards and reviews consequential use cases, providing cross-functional oversight and accountability. Writing code and provisioning infrastructure are engineering activities that the board governs rather than performs.

options.text: Writing the training code for each model
options.rationale: Implementation work belongs to engineering teams, not the oversight body.

options.text: Provisioning EC2 capacity for training jobs
options.rationale: Capacity provisioning is an operational engineering task.

options.text: Selecting the instance type for each inference endpoint
options.rationale: Instance selection is a technical decision made by the delivery team.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which AWS service maintains centralized technical metadata such as table definitions and schemas that other analytics and ML services can query?

options.text: AWS Glue Data Catalog
options.rationale: The AWS Glue Data Catalog is the central metadata repository storing table definitions, schemas, and partition information, and it is consumed by services such as Athena, EMR, and Redshift Spectrum. S3 Inventory lists objects, CloudTrail records API calls, and EventBridge routes events.

options.text: Amazon S3 Inventory
options.rationale: S3 Inventory produces object listings without schema-level metadata.

options.text: AWS CloudTrail
options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity for auditing.

options.text: Amazon EventBridge
options.rationale: EventBridge is an event bus for routing and reacting to events.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company is classifying its generative AI use cases to decide how much governance each needs. Which factor most appropriately determines the level of oversight?

options.text: The number of tokens the model consumes per request
options.rationale: Token consumption is a cost metric with no relationship to risk of harm.

options.text: The potential impact on individuals and the organization if the system behaves incorrectly
options.rationale: Risk-based governance scales oversight to consequence, so systems that can materially affect people's rights, safety, finances, or opportunities receive the most scrutiny regardless of technical details. Token usage, Region, and provider identity do not determine potential harm.

options.text: The AWS Region where the model is hosted
options.rationale: Region affects residency and latency, not the consequence of an error.

options.text: Whether the model is from Amazon or a third-party provider
options.rationale: Provider choice does not by itself determine how consequential the use case is.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which artifact best supports an auditor's question about what a specific production model was designed to do and what its known limitations are?

options.text: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards
options.rationale: SageMaker Model Cards record intended use, training data characteristics, evaluation results, and limitations in a governed artifact attached to the model, which is exactly the documentation an auditor requests. Dashboards, cost reports, and access logs describe operations, spend, and data access instead.

options.text: Amazon CloudWatch dashboards
options.rationale: Dashboards show operational metrics, not documented intent or limitations.

options.text: AWS Cost and Usage Report
options.rationale: Cost reports describe spending patterns.

options.text: Amazon S3 access logs
options.rationale: S3 access logs record who read objects, not model design intent.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company adopts a policy requiring periodic review of all deployed models. What is the primary governance purpose of a defined review cadence?

options.text: To reduce inference costs over time

options.text: To confirm models still perform as intended and remain appropriate as data, business needs, and regulations change
options.rationale: A review cadence exists because a model approved once does not stay appropriate forever: data shifts, the business changes, and regulations evolve. Periodic review re-verifies performance, fairness, and continued fit for purpose, and may conclude that retirement is the right outcome.

options.text: To force migration to newer instance families
options.rationale: Instance family migration is an infrastructure optimization decision.

options.text: To increase the frequency of model retraining regardless of need
options.rationale: Retraining should follow evidence of need rather than a fixed schedule.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which statement about ISO certifications and AWS is accurate?

options.text: AWS holds ISO certifications for its infrastructure and services, and customers can obtain the reports through AWS Artifact
options.rationale: AWS maintains ISO certifications covering its infrastructure and in-scope services, and customers can download the certificates from AWS Artifact to support their own audits. Inheriting AWS's certification does not make a customer workload compliant, because the customer's own configuration and processes are in scope under shared responsibility.

options.text: AWS ISO certifications automatically make any customer workload compliant
options.rationale: Customer workloads must independently meet requirements; certification is not inherited wholesale.

options.text: Customers must obtain ISO certification on behalf of AWS
options.rationale: AWS obtains its own certifications; customers do not certify on its behalf.

options.text: ISO certifications apply only to on-premises data centers
options.rationale: ISO standards apply to cloud environments as well as on-premises facilities.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which practice best supports accountability when a generative AI system produces a harmful output in production?

options.text: Retaining invocation logs and an API audit trail so the request, response, and calling identity can be reconstructed
options.rationale: Accountability requires being able to reconstruct what happened, which depends on invocation logging of prompts and responses together with CloudTrail records of who invoked the service. Aggressive log deletion, disabled monitoring, and anonymous access all destroy the evidence an investigation needs.

options.text: Deleting logs after 24 hours to minimize data retention
options.rationale: Very short retention can leave an incident uninvestigable.

options.text: Disabling monitoring to avoid capturing sensitive content
options.rationale: Disabling monitoring removes the ability to detect or explain harmful outputs.

options.text: Allowing anonymous access to the assistant
options.rationale: Anonymous access removes attribution entirely.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company uses a scoping approach to decide governance requirements for generative AI, ranging from consumer applications through to self-trained models. What is the main benefit of such a scoping model?

options.text: It guarantees regulatory approval in every jurisdiction
options.rationale: No framework guarantees regulatory approval.

options.text: It clarifies which security and governance responsibilities the organization holds based on how much of the AI stack it controls
options.rationale: A scoping framework maps deployment patterns, from using a third-party consumer app through to pre-training your own model, to the responsibilities the organization actually carries at each level. The more of the stack you control, the more governance and security obligations you own.

options.text: It reduces the cost of foundation model inference
options.rationale: Scoping clarifies responsibility; it does not change inference pricing.

options.text: It removes the need for model documentation
options.rationale: Documentation remains necessary at every scope level.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which two practices support data governance for machine learning training datasets? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Recording data lineage from source system through every transformation
options.rationale: Lineage and cataloging are the foundations of data governance: lineage answers where data came from and how it changed, and cataloging makes datasets discoverable with clear ownership. Flattening storage layout, granting broad admin access, and disabling versioning weaken governance.

options.text: Cataloging datasets with searchable metadata and documented ownership
options.rationale: Lineage and cataloging are the foundations of data governance: lineage answers where data came from and how it changed, and cataloging makes datasets discoverable with clear ownership. Flattening storage layout, granting broad admin access, and disabling versioning weaken governance.

options.text: Storing all datasets in the same S3 prefix for simplicity
options.rationale: A single shared prefix makes fine-grained access control and organization harder.

options.text: Granting all data scientists administrator access to accelerate work
options.rationale: Blanket administrator access violates least privilege.

options.text: Disabling versioning to reduce storage cost
options.rationale: Disabling versioning removes protection against accidental or malicious overwrite.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which statement best explains why team training is part of an AI governance program?

options.text: Training reduces the cost of AWS services
options.rationale: Training does not affect AWS service pricing.

options.text: Controls only work if the people building and operating AI systems understand the policies, risks, and escalation paths
options.rationale: Written policies do not enforce themselves; people implement them. Training ensures builders and operators recognize risks such as prompt injection and data leakage, know the documentation standards, and understand when and how to escalate. It complements rather than replaces technical controls.

options.text: Training is required by AWS before enabling Amazon Bedrock
options.rationale: AWS does not mandate training before enabling Bedrock.

options.text: Training replaces the need for technical guardrails
options.rationale: Human awareness supplements technical guardrails; it does not substitute for them.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which service records configuration changes to AWS resources so a compliance team can see how a resource was configured at a past point in time?

options.text: AWS Config
options.rationale: AWS Config maintains a configuration history and timeline for supported resources and can evaluate them against rules, which lets a compliance team answer what a resource looked like on a given date. Macie classifies data, Artifact supplies AWS reports, and DataZone governs data discovery and sharing.

options.text: Amazon Macie
options.rationale: Macie discovers sensitive data rather than tracking resource configuration.

options.text: AWS Artifact
options.rationale: Artifact provides AWS compliance documents.

options.text: Amazon DataZone
options.rationale: DataZone provides business data cataloging and access workflows.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: An organization must show which datasets contributed to a model that produced a disputed decision. Which capability is most essential?

options.text: Data lineage tracking across the pipeline
options.rationale: Lineage records the chain from source data through transformations into the training set and ultimately the model version, which is what lets an organization trace a disputed output back to its inputs. Metrics resolution, instance sizing, and throughput are performance concerns.

options.text: Increased CloudWatch metric resolution
options.rationale: Metric resolution affects operational monitoring granularity, not data provenance.

options.text: Larger training instance types

options.text: Higher S3 request throughput
options.rationale: Request throughput is a performance characteristic of storage access.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company must comply with a regulation requiring that automated decisions affecting consumers be explainable and contestable. Which combination of measures best satisfies this?

options.rationale: Explainable and contestable decisions require documentation of the model's intent and limits, an explanation of the individual decision, a human process through which a person can challenge it, and retained records so the decision can be reviewed. questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which description best fits SOC 2 in the context of a company evaluating a cloud provider?

options.rationale: SOC 2 reports describe a service organization's controls against the Trust Services Criteria, and customers review them when assessing a provider. GDPR, PCI DSS, and HIPAA are the European privacy regulation, the card data standard, and the US health privacy law respectively.

options.text: A European regulation granting individuals data deletion rights
options.rationale: That describes GDPR.

options.text: A payment card industry security standard

options.text: A United States health information privacy law
options.rationale: That describes HIPAA.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which practice best reduces the risk that an organization loses track of which models are running in production?

options.text: Maintaining a central model inventory with owners, status, and monitoring results
options.rationale: A central inventory recording every model, its owner, its status, and its monitoring results is the control that prevents undocumented or orphaned models persisting in production. options.text: Increasing the retention period of application logs
options.rationale: Longer log retention does not tell you which models exist or who owns them.

options.text: Deploying all models to the same endpoint
options.rationale: Sharing one endpoint does not create an inventory and can complicate isolation.

options.text: Standardizing on a single foundation model provider
options.rationale: Using one provider does not by itself track deployed models.

questions.question: What is the primary governance purpose of documenting a dataset's intended use and known limitations?

options.text: To reduce the storage footprint of the dataset
options.rationale: Documentation does not change storage size.

options.text: To prevent the dataset from being reused in contexts where it would produce misleading or unfair results
options.rationale: Datasets carry assumptions from how and why they were collected, so documenting intended use and limitations stops a later team from applying them to a population or purpose they do not represent. That reuse mismatch is a common source of biased and misleading models.

options.text: To improve query performance
options.rationale: Documentation has no effect on query performance.

options.text: To satisfy AWS service quotas
options.rationale: Service quotas are unrelated to dataset documentation.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company wants to enforce that no ML workload can be deployed to an unapproved AWS Region. Which mechanism most directly enforces this at scale?

options.text: A service control policy in AWS Organizations restricting Regions
options.rationale: Service control policies in AWS Organizations set the maximum permissions available to accounts and can deny actions outside approved Regions, which is preventive enforcement rather than detection. Alarms detect after the fact, runbooks rely on human compliance, and lifecycle policies manage object transitions.

options.text: An Amazon CloudWatch alarm on Region usage
options.rationale: An alarm notifies after the deployment has already occurred.

options.text: A note in the team's runbook
options.rationale: A runbook is guidance and cannot technically prevent an action.

options.text: An Amazon S3 lifecycle policy
options.rationale: Lifecycle policies transition or expire S3 objects.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes AWS Config from AWS Audit Manager?

options.text: Config evaluates resource configurations against rules; Audit Manager maps evidence to control frameworks and produces audit reports
options.rationale: AWS Config continuously records and evaluates resource configuration state against rules, answering whether resources are configured compliantly. Audit Manager consumes evidence from across AWS, maps it to controls in a framework such as HIPAA or PCI DSS, and assembles an audit-ready report.

options.text: Config downloads AWS certifications; Audit Manager records API calls
options.rationale: Downloading certifications is AWS Artifact and API recording is CloudTrail.

options.text: Config scans for software vulnerabilities; Audit Manager classifies sensitive data
options.rationale: Vulnerability scanning is Amazon Inspector and sensitive data classification is Amazon Macie.

options.text: They are the same service under different names
options.rationale: They are distinct services with different purposes.

questions.question: An organization's policy requires that any AI system making decisions about people be registered and reviewed before launch. Which governance element does this represent?

options.text: A defined approval gate tied to risk classification
options.rationale: Requiring registration and review before launch for systems that affect people is an approval gate driven by risk classification, ensuring consequential systems receive oversight proportionate to their impact. Retention schedules, tagging, and key rotation are separate operational controls.

options.text: A data retention schedule
options.rationale: Retention schedules govern how long data is kept.

options.text: A cost allocation tag policy
options.rationale: Cost allocation tags support financial reporting.

options.text: An encryption key rotation schedule
options.rationale: Key rotation is an encryption hygiene practice.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: Which of the following is the clearest example of a transparency standard within an AI governance program?

options.text: A rule that users must be told when they are interacting with an AI system and how to reach a human
options.rationale: Transparency standards define what must be disclosed to the people affected by a system, such as informing users they are interacting with AI and providing a path to human assistance. Accuracy thresholds, runtime limits, and storage choices are performance and infrastructure standards.

options.text: A rule that all models must achieve at least 95 percent accuracy
options.rationale: An accuracy threshold is a performance standard, not a disclosure standard.

options.text: A rule that training jobs must complete within four hours
options.rationale: Training duration is an operational constraint.

options.text: A rule that all data must be stored in Amazon S3
options.rationale: Storage location is an infrastructure decision.

questions.topic: Security, Compliance, and Governance for AI Solutions

questions.question: A company must decide how long to keep prompt and response logs from its generative AI assistant. Which consideration should drive the decision?

options.text: Balancing investigative and regulatory needs against privacy obligations and data minimization
options.rationale: Retention decisions weigh the need to investigate incidents and satisfy regulators against privacy principles such as data minimization and any legal limits on holding personal data. Indefinite retention increases exposure, immediate deletion removes accountability, and context window size is unrelated.

options.text: Keeping logs indefinitely because storage is inexpensive
options.rationale: Indefinite retention of potentially sensitive content increases privacy and breach exposure.

options.text: Deleting logs immediately to eliminate all risk
options.rationale: Immediate deletion leaves incidents uninvestigable and may itself violate obligations.

options.text: Matching the retention period to the model's context window
options.rationale: Context window is a model capability with no bearing on retention policy.
